build-a-sharepoint-launch-readiness-chec.problemStatement: A solution works for its maker and fails for everyone else on day one, because permissions, connections and volumes were never tested as a real user.
whenToUse: Before launching any SharePoint-based solution to more than a pilot group
Handing a solution to a support team
After a major change
whenNotToUse: Personal productivity lists
Prototypes that will not be used for real work
build-a-sharepoint-launch-readiness-chec.formulaOrCode:
Launch readiness checklist (track it as a list: Item | Area | Owner | Status | Evidence | Due)

DATA AND LISTS
  [ ] Columns filtered by apps, flows and views are indexed
  [ ] Default view filtered so it works beyond 5,000 items
  [ ] Required columns and validation match what the app enforces
  [ ] Versioning on for business lists, limit set
  [ ] Test data removed; ID gaps are acceptable or the list was recreated

PERMISSIONS
  [ ] Tested as a normal user account, not as a site owner
  [ ] Users have the right access to every list the app reads, including reference lists
  [ ] Sensitive lists not exposed through "Everyone except external users"
  [ ] App shared with a security group, not individuals

POWER APPS
  [ ] No delegation warnings left unreviewed
  [ ] Tested with realistic volumes and on the devices people will use
  [ ] App published, and the published version is the one tested
  [ ] Error messages are readable; App.OnError set

POWER AUTOMATE
  [ ] Flows owned by a service account or have at least two owners
  [ ] Connections use an account with a licence and the right permissions
  [ ] Trigger conditions in place; no flow triggers itself
  [ ] Failure notifications go to a monitored mailbox
  [ ] Solution-aware where possible, with connection references

SUPPORT
  [ ] Named business owner, technical owner and backup
  [ ] Support contact shown in the app and on the site
  [ ] Short user guide and a known-issues note
  [ ] Rollback plan: how to hide the app or pause flows

COMMUNICATIONS
  [ ] Users told what changes, when, and where to get help
  [ ] Old process or form withdrawn or redirected on the launch date
  [ ] Feedback route open for the first two weeks

GO / NO-GO
  All items in Data, Permissions and Power Automate must be done. Others may launch with an owner and date.
stepByStepInstructions: Copy the checklist into a list with an owner and status per item.
Test the whole process signed in as an ordinary user.
Check indexes, view filters and delegation with realistic data volumes.
Confirm flow ownership, connections and failure alerts.
Hold a short go or no-go review and record the decision.
commonMistakes: Testing only as the maker, who has full permissions.
Launching flows owned by one person's account.
Leaving the old process running in parallel indefinitely.
troubleshooting: If users get access errors at launch, check each data source the app connects to, including reference lists and libraries.
If the app works in Studio but not when played, publish it. Users run the last published version.
If flows fail for some users, the flow runs under the connection owner's permissions, or under the user's for Power Apps triggers. Check which applies.
If performance is poor on day one, look for non-delegable filters and large collections loaded at start.

create-an-intranet-page-review-workflow.shortDescription: Add owners and review dates to site pages and remind owners to review or retire them on a schedule.
create-an-intranet-page-review-workflow.fullDescription: Intranet pages go stale because nobody is asked to look at them again. Adding an owner and a review date to the Site Pages library, with a scheduled flow that reminds owners, keeps content current.
create-an-intranet-page-review-workflow.problemStatement: The intranet is full of pages last edited years ago, some wrong, and nobody knows who is responsible for each.
whenToUse: Intranets and knowledge sites with many pages
Policy and how-to content that must stay correct
Sites with several authors
whenNotToUse: News posts, which age naturally
Small team sites with a handful of pages
create-an-intranet-page-review-workflow.formulaOrCode:
Site Pages library: add columns
  PageOwner      Person               accountable for the content
  ReviewDate     Date                 next review due                    (indexed)
  ReviewStatus   Choice               Current | Review due | Under review | Retire
  LastReviewedOn Date
  ReviewMonths   Number               6 or 12, default 12

Show the details on the page: add the Page properties web part with PageOwner and LastReviewedOn.

Views on Site Pages
  Review due      : ReviewDate <= [Today]+30, sort ReviewDate
  No owner        : PageOwner is empty
  By owner        : group by PageOwner

Optional: page approval
  Site Pages > Automate > Power Automate > Configure page approval flow
  Authors submit, approvers publish. Good for policy pages.

Flow 1: monthly review reminders
  Trigger: Recurrence, monthly
  Get files (properties only), Site Pages
    Filter Query : ReviewDate le '@{addDays(utcNow(), 30, 'yyyy-MM-dd')}' and ReviewStatus eq 'Current'
  Apply to each page
    Send an email (V2)
      To      : @{items('Apply_to_each')?['PageOwner']?['Email']}
      Subject : Review due: @{items('Apply_to_each')?['Title']}
      Body    : Please check this page is still correct, update it if needed, then set Review status to Current.
                @{items('Apply_to_each')?['{Link}']}
    Update file properties: ReviewStatus = Review due

Flow 2: roll the date forward
  Trigger: When a file is created or modified (properties only), Site Pages
    Trigger condition:
      @and(equals(triggerBody()?['ReviewStatus']?['Value'], 'Current'), less(triggerBody()?['ReviewDate'], utcNow()))
  Update file properties
    LastReviewedOn : @{utcNow()}
    ReviewDate     : @{addToTime(utcNow(), int(coalesce(triggerBody()?['ReviewMonths'], 12)), 'Month', 'yyyy-MM-dd')}

Escalation: pages still "Review due" after 60 days go to the site owner in a monthly digest.
Retire: ReviewStatus = Retire -> unpublish the page, or move it to an archive folder, and remove navigation links.
stepByStepInstructions: Add owner, review date, review status and interval columns to Site Pages.
Set an owner and first review date on every existing page.
Add the page properties web part so readers see the owner and last review date.
Run a monthly flow that emails owners of pages due for review.
When the owner marks a page current, roll the review date forward, and escalate pages left overdue.
commonMistakes: One owner for the whole site, who cannot judge every page.
Reminders with no link to the page.
Deleting old pages without checking for inbound links.
troubleshooting: If the flow finds no pages, check the internal names of the new columns in the filter query.
If updating properties creates a draft of the page, publish it again in the flow or accept minor versions for metadata changes.
If owners have left, the email fails. Send those to the site owner and use the No owner view.
If the review date rolls forward without a real review, require a comment column or use page approval for important pages.

build-a-sharepoint-permissions-exception.shortDescription: Record every case where a site, list, folder or item has unique permissions, with who approved it and when it should be reviewed.
build-a-sharepoint-permissions-exception.fullDescription: Broken permission inheritance is sometimes necessary and always hard to see later. A log of each exception, with a reason, an approver and a review date, keeps unique permissions deliberate and reviewable.
build-a-sharepoint-permissions-exception.problemStatement: Nobody can say why a folder is shared with a particular person, or how many places on the site have their own permissions.
whenToUse: Sites with sensitive content
Sites where owners share items and folders individually
Preparing for an access review or audit
whenNotToUse: Sites with simple, inherited permissions throughout
Personal OneDrive sharing
build-a-sharepoint-permissions-exception.formulaOrCode:
List: Permission Exceptions
  Title            Single line     what was secured, in plain words
  Scope            Choice          Site | List or library | Folder | Item or file | Sharing link
  Location         Hyperlink       URL of the object
  GrantedTo        Single line     person, group or "anyone with the link"
  PermissionLevel  Choice          Read | Edit | Contribute | Full control | Restricted view
  ExternalAccess   Yes/No
  Reason           Multiple lines
  RequestedBy      Person
  ApprovedBy       Person
  GrantedOn        Date
  ReviewDate       Date            when the exception must be re-confirmed      (indexed)
  ExpiresOn        Date            optional end date
  Status           Choice          Active | Removed | Expired                    (indexed)
  RemovedOn        Date

Views
  Active exceptions : Status = Active, group by Scope
  Review due        : Status = Active AND ReviewDate <= [Today]+14
  External access   : ExternalAccess = Yes AND Status = Active

Finding existing exceptions
  Site settings > Site permissions > Advanced > "Some content on this site has different permissions"
  PnP PowerShell:
    Get-PnPList | Where-Object { $_.HasUniqueRoleAssignments }
    Get-PnPListItem -List "Documents" -PageSize 2000 | Where-Object { $_.HasUniqueRoleAssignments }
  Sharing links: Site usage > Shared with external users; or the sharing report (Site usage > Run report)

Process
  1. Request: who needs access to what, at which level, and why.
  2. Prefer a group over an individual, and a library or folder over single items.
  3. Site owner approves and records the exception with a review date (3 to 6 months).
  4. Monthly flow: email approvers the exceptions due for review.
       Filter Query: Status eq 'Active' and ReviewDate le '@{addDays(utcNow(), 14, 'yyyy-MM-dd')}'
  5. Remove: restore inheritance (Manage access > Advanced > Delete unique permissions) and set Status = Removed.

Limits worth knowing
  Supported limit of 50,000 unique permission scopes per list or library; keep well under 5,000 for performance.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the exception log with scope, location, who has access, reason, approver and review date.
Find existing unique permissions using site settings or PnP PowerShell and record them.
Require a log entry for every new exception.
Run a monthly reminder for exceptions due for review.
Remove exceptions that are no longer needed and mark them in the log.
commonMistakes: Sharing individual files instead of using a folder or library with its own permissions.
Granting access to individuals who later change role.
No review date, so exceptions last for ever.
troubleshooting: If the list of unique permissions is long, group related items into one secured folder and restore inheritance on the items.
If a list is slow or errors when breaking inheritance, it has too many unique scopes. Consolidate.
If someone has access that is not in the log, check sharing links, which grant access without appearing as a normal permission entry.
If restoring inheritance removes access someone needs, add them to the parent's group first.

use-view-formatting-for-overdue-items.shortDescription: Highlight overdue rows in a SharePoint list view with JSON view formatting, using the due date and status together.
use-view-formatting-for-overdue-items.fullDescription: View formatting can add a class to a whole row based on its values. This pattern shades rows that are past due and not complete, with a second shade for items due soon, and includes the column formatting equivalent.
use-view-formatting-for-overdue-items.problemStatement: Overdue items look the same as everything else in the list, so they are only found when someone sorts by date.
whenToUse: Task, issue and request lists with a due date
Views people scan daily
Highlighting that depends on more than one column
whenNotToUse: Rules needing data from other lists
Views where conditional formatting from the simple rule builder is enough
stepByStepInstructions: Make sure the view includes the due date and status columns.
Open Format current view and switch to advanced mode.
Paste the row formatting JSON and adjust the status values to match your list.
Optionally format the due date column to show how many days late an item is.
Save, then check items that are overdue, due soon, complete and without a date.
commonMistakes: Highlighting completed items because the rule ignores status.
Referencing a column that is not in the view, which makes the rule fail silently.
Using display names instead of internal column names after the $ sign.
troubleshooting: If nothing is highlighted, check the internal name of each column, such as Due_x0020_Date, and that the column is in the view.
If items with no due date turn red, add the empty check as shown.
If today's items show as overdue, @now includes the time. Compare with @now - 86400000 or use a date-only column.
If colours look wrong in dark mode or Teams, use the sp-field-severity classes rather than fixed colour codes.

create-a-sharepoint-vendor-onboarding-li.shortDescription: Design a list that tracks each new vendor from request through checks to approved, with the documents and owners involved.
create-a-sharepoint-vendor-onboarding-li.fullDescription: Vendor onboarding passes through procurement, finance, legal and sometimes security. This list design captures the vendor's details, each check's status, key dates and the documents collected, so anyone can see where a vendor stands.
create-a-sharepoint-vendor-onboarding-li.problemStatement: Vendor setup is tracked in email threads and a spreadsheet, so nobody knows which checks are outstanding or why a vendor cannot be paid yet.
whenToUse: Organisations onboarding vendors regularly
Processes with several teams' checks
A front end in Power Apps or the list form
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a procurement or ERP system that manages vendor setup
Storing bank details, which should not be kept in a general list
create-a-sharepoint-vendor-onboarding-li.formulaOrCode:
List: Vendor Onboarding
  Title               Single line     vendor legal name                              (required)
  VendorType          Choice          Goods | Services | Contractor | Software
  RequestedBy         Person                                                          (indexed)
  BusinessOwner       Person          internal sponsor for the relationship
  ContactName         Single line     ContactEmail  Single line    ContactPhone  Single line
  Country             Choice
  EstimatedAnnualSpend Currency
  RiskTier            Choice          Low | Medium | High     (drives which checks apply)

  Status              Choice          Requested | Checks in progress | Awaiting approval |
                                      Approved | Rejected | On hold                   (indexed, default Requested)

  Checks (each a Choice: Not required | Pending | Passed | Failed)
    TaxFormStatus | InsuranceStatus | ContractStatus | SecurityReviewStatus | FinanceSetupStatus

  ContractExpiry      Date            InsuranceExpiry  Date                           (indexed)
  ERPVendorNumber     Single line     filled once finance has created the record
  ApprovedBy          Person          ApprovedOn  Date
  Notes               Multiple lines (append changes)

Documents
  Use a document library "Vendor Documents" with a VendorId (Number) column, or a document set per vendor.
  Attachments on the list item suit a few small files only.

Do not store
  Bank account numbers or tax identifiers. Keep those in the finance system and store only its reference.

Views
  In progress        : Status = Checks in progress, group by RiskTier
  Awaiting approval  : Status = Awaiting approval
  My requests        : RequestedBy = [Me]
  Expiring documents : InsuranceExpiry <= [Today]+60 OR ContractExpiry <= [Today]+60

Rules (list validation, or in the app)
  Approved needs every check to be Passed or Not required:
  =IF([Status]="Approved", AND([TaxFormStatus]<>"Pending",[TaxFormStatus]<>"Failed",
      [ContractStatus]<>"Pending",[ContractStatus]<>"Failed",
      [FinanceSetupStatus]<>"Pending",[FinanceSetupStatus]<>"Failed"), TRUE)

Automation
  On create : set which checks apply from RiskTier, and create tasks for each team
  On change : when all checks pass, set Status = Awaiting approval and start the approval
  Scheduled : remind owners of expiring insurance and contracts
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with vendor details, a status, and a status column per check.
Add a risk tier that decides which checks apply.
Store documents in a linked library and keep sensitive financial details out of the list.
Add views for work in progress, approvals, the requester and expiring documents.
Add validation so a vendor cannot be approved with checks outstanding, and automate tasks and reminders.
commonMistakes: One overall status with no view of individual checks.
Storing bank details in the list.
No expiry dates, so insurance and contracts lapse unnoticed.
troubleshooting: If the validation formula is rejected, check the column names and that the formula stays under the length limit. Move complex rules into the app or a flow.
If teams cannot see what they need to do, add a view per check filtered on Pending.
If duplicate vendors appear, enforce unique values on the vendor name or a registration number column.
If the list becomes slow, index the status and expiry columns and filter the default view to vendors in progress.

design-a-sharepoint-permission-audit-int.shortDescription: Design a list for requesting and tracking permission audits of sites, so each review has a scope, an owner and recorded findings.
design-a-sharepoint-permission-audit-int.fullDescription: Access reviews happen when someone asks: a site owner changes, a project closes, an audit is due. This intake list captures the request, the scope, who will carry it out, and the outcome with follow-up actions.
design-a-sharepoint-permission-audit-int.problemStatement: Permission reviews are requested by email, carried out inconsistently and leave no record of what was checked or changed.
whenToUse: IT or governance teams that review site access on request
Periodic access reviews of sensitive sites
Evidence for auditors
whenNotToUse: Tenants using Microsoft Entra access reviews for group membership, which covers that part automatically
A single site reviewed informally by its owner
design-a-sharepoint-permission-audit-int.formulaOrCode:
List: Permission Audit Requests
  Title             Single line     short name for the audit
  SiteUrl           Hyperlink       site or library to review                       (required)
  Scope             Choice          Whole site | Library or list | Folder | External sharing only
  Reason            Choice          Owner change | Project closed | Scheduled review | Incident | Audit request
  Sensitivity       Choice          Internal | Confidential | Highly confidential
  RequestedBy       Person          RequestedOn  Date (default today)
  SiteOwner         Person          confirms what access is correct
  AssignedTo        Person          who carries out the review                      (indexed)
  DueDate           Date                                                            (indexed)
  Status            Choice          New | Scheduled | In review | Awaiting owner | Remediation | Closed   (indexed)

  Findings (filled by the reviewer)
  UsersReviewed       Number
  ExternalUsersFound  Number
  UniquePermissionScopes Number
  AccessRemovedCount  Number
  FindingsSummary     Multiple lines
  ReportLink          Hyperlink     exported permission report in a restricted library
  OwnerSignedOffOn    Date
  NextReviewDate      Date

Views
  Queue           : Status <> Closed, sort DueDate
  My audits       : AssignedTo = [Me] AND Status <> Closed
  Awaiting owner  : Status = Awaiting owner
  Closed this year: Status = Closed, sort OwnerSignedOffOn descending

Review steps to record in a linked checklist
  1. Export members of the site's groups and Microsoft 365 group
  2. List items and folders with unique permissions
  3. List sharing links, especially "Anyone" and external
  4. Owner confirms keep or remove for each entry
  5. Remove access, restore inheritance where possible
  6. Owner signs off; set NextReviewDate (6 or 12 months by sensitivity)

Helpful commands
  Get-PnPGroup | ForEach-Object { Get-PnPGroupMember -Group $_ }
  Get-PnPListItem -List "Documents" -PageSize 2000 | Where-Object { $_.HasUniqueRoleAssignments }
  Site usage > Run report (sharing report as CSV)

Automation
  On create: notify the governance team. On Status = Awaiting owner: email the site owner with the report link.
  On Closed: create next year's request automatically when NextReviewDate arrives.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with the site, scope, reason, sensitivity and people involved.
Add findings columns for counts, a summary and a link to the exported report.
Build views for the queue, each reviewer's work and items waiting on site owners.
Follow the same review steps each time and record owner sign-off.
Set the next review date on closure and raise the next request automatically.
commonMistakes: Recording that a review happened without what was found or changed.
Storing the exported permission report where the people being reviewed can read it.
No owner sign-off, so the reviewer guesses what access is right.
troubleshooting: If requests stall at Awaiting owner, add a reminder and an escalation to the owner's manager after 14 days.
If the review misses sharing links, run the site's sharing report as well as checking groups.
If the same findings recur, restrict sharing settings on the site rather than cleaning up each time.
If volumes grow, prioritise by sensitivity and schedule low-risk sites yearly.

build-a-sharepoint-readiness-assessment-.shortDescription: Assess whether a team and its content are ready to move a process into SharePoint, before building anything.
build-a-sharepoint-readiness-assessment-.fullDescription: Many SharePoint builds fail because the process, ownership or data were not ready. This assessment asks the questions that predict trouble, scores the answers and points to what to fix first.
build-a-sharepoint-readiness-assessment-.problemStatement: A list and app are built quickly, then stall because nobody owns the process, the data is a mess or the volume exceeds what a list handles well.
whenToUse: Before moving a spreadsheet or email process into SharePoint and Power Apps
Prioritising several candidate processes
Setting expectations with a business team
whenNotToUse: Small personal lists
Projects already through a formal discovery
build-a-sharepoint-readiness-assessment-.formulaOrCode:
Score each question 0 (no), 1 (partly), 2 (yes). Record evidence.

PROCESS
  1. Is there one agreed way the process works today?
  2. Is there a named business owner who can make decisions?
  3. Are the statuses and who moves an item between them agreed?
  4. Are exceptions understood (what happens when it does not fit)?

DATA
  5. Is the existing data in a consistent structure (one row per thing, one value per cell)?
  6. Are volumes suitable: under about 100,000 rows in total, and filtered views under 5,000?
  7. Is the data free of content that needs stronger protection (health, payment, national identifiers)?
  8. Are relationships simple (one or two levels of parent and child)?

PEOPLE AND ACCESS
  9. Do all users have Microsoft 365 licences and access to the site?
 10. Is it clear who may see and edit what, without needing a different view of the data for every person?
 11. Is there someone who will maintain the solution after launch?

REPORTING AND INTEGRATION
 12. Are reporting needs known, and achievable with views or Power BI?
 13. Are connections to other systems limited to standard connectors?

CHANGE
 14. Will the old spreadsheet or mailbox be withdrawn on a set date?
 15. Is there time for users to test before launch?

Result (maximum 30)
  24-30 : Ready. Build.
  16-23 : Ready with actions. Fix items scored 0 first.
   0-15 : Not ready. Agree the process and ownership before building.

Stop signs regardless of score
  Q2 = 0 (no owner)                  -> do not start
  Q6 = 0 (very large volumes)        -> consider Dataverse or SQL
  Q7 = 0 (highly sensitive data)     -> involve security and compliance; SharePoint lists may not be suitable
  Q10 = 0 (row-level security needs) -> item-level permissions do not scale; consider Dataverse

Track it: a list with one row per question (Area, Question, Score, Evidence, Action, Owner).
stepByStepInstructions: Run the assessment with the business owner in a 45 minute session.
Score each question and note the evidence.
Check the stop signs before looking at the total.
Agree actions for any question scored zero.
Decide whether to build now, fix first or choose a different platform.
commonMistakes: Starting the build to work out the process as you go.
Ignoring volume and security until late.
Scoring generously to justify a decision already made.
troubleshooting: If the business cannot name an owner, pause. Nothing built will be maintained.
If the data is inconsistent, clean it in the spreadsheet first, or plan an import with rules for bad rows.
If security needs differ per row, test item-level permissions at realistic volume before committing, or move to Dataverse.
If stakeholders disagree on the process, map it together before designing a list.

design-a-sharepoint-list-schema-export-c.shortDescription: Capture a list's full design, including columns, types, internal names, views and settings, so it can be documented or rebuilt elsewhere.
design-a-sharepoint-list-schema-export-c.fullDescription: Moving a solution between sites or tenants, or simply documenting it, needs the list's schema written down. This checklist covers what to capture and the tools that export it, including the parts templates miss.
design-a-sharepoint-list-schema-export-c.problemStatement: A list is recreated by hand in another site, a column gets a different internal name, and the app and flows that depend on it break.
whenToUse: Moving a list between sites, environments or tenants
Documenting a solution for support
Before making risky changes to a list
whenNotToUse: Copying a list within the same tenant with no dependencies, where From existing list is enough
Lists with no apps or flows attached
design-a-sharepoint-list-schema-export-c.formulaOrCode:
What to capture
  LIST
   [ ] Title, URL (internal name), description, template type (list or library)
   [ ] Versioning, attachments, content approval, item-level permissions settings
   [ ] Unique permissions and who has access
  COLUMNS (for each)
   [ ] Display name and INTERNAL name (they differ after a rename or when spaces are used)
   [ ] Type, required, unique, indexed, default value
   [ ] Choices (exact text), lookup target list and column, person options (single or multiple, groups allowed)
   [ ] Calculated formula, column validation formula and message
   [ ] Column formatting JSON
  LIST-LEVEL
   [ ] Validation formula and message
   [ ] Content types and their order
  VIEWS (for each)
   [ ] Name, default or not, columns and order, filter, sort, group, row limit, view formatting JSON
  DEPENDENCIES
   [ ] Apps, flows, reports and pages that use the list
   [ ] Forms customised with Power Apps
  DATA
   [ ] Whether data moves too, and how lookups and people will be mapped

Export options
  1. Create from existing list (same tenant): New > List > From existing list. Copies columns, views, formatting. No data.
  2. Site script (JSON you can store in source control):
       Get-SPOSiteScriptFromList -ListUrl "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/ops/Lists/Requests"
  3. PnP provisioning template, most complete, optionally with data:
       Get-PnPSiteTemplate -Out requests.xml -ListsToExtract "Requests" -Handlers Lists
       Add-PnPDataRowsToSiteTemplate -Path requests.xml -List "Requests"
       Invoke-PnPSiteTemplate -Path requests.xml          (on the target site)
  4. Column list for documentation:
       Get-PnPField -List "Requests" | Select Title, InternalName, TypeAsString, Required, Indexed | Export-Csv fields.csv
       Get-PnPView -List "Requests" | Select Title, ViewQuery, DefaultView
  5. REST, read-only:
       _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Requests')/fields?$filter=Hidden eq false&$select=Title,InternalName,TypeAsString

After rebuilding
  [ ] Compare internal names in source and target
  [ ] Re-create indexes before loading data
  [ ] Reconnect apps and flows, or update connection references and environment variables
  [ ] Test as a normal user
stepByStepInstructions: List what uses the list: apps, flows, reports and pages.
Export the columns with their internal names, types and settings.
Capture views, formatting JSON, validation and list settings.
Choose an export method: from existing list, a site script or a PnP template.
Rebuild in the target, compare internal names, then reconnect and test dependencies.
commonMistakes: Recreating columns by hand with names that produce different internal names.
Forgetting indexes, validation and view formatting.
Moving data with lookups before the target lists exist.
troubleshooting: If an app breaks after the move, a column's internal name differs. Create the column with the original internal name first, then rename the display name.
If lookups are empty after import, the target IDs differ. Import the parent list first and map by a key column.
If person values fail to import, the users do not exist in the target tenant. Map them or store emails as text.
If a list template (.stp) cannot be saved, custom scripts are disabled on modern sites. Use a site script or PnP template.

design-a-facilities-request-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for facilities requests such as repairs, moves and cleaning, with location, priority and completion tracking.
design-a-facilities-request-list-schema.fullDescription: Facilities requests need to say where the problem is, how urgent it is and who is dealing with it. This schema captures location in a structured way, separates the requester's urgency from the team's priority, and records completion and feedback.
design-a-facilities-request-list-schema.problemStatement: Requests arrive as free-text emails with no building or room, so the team has to reply to ask where the problem is before anyone can be sent.
whenToUse: Maintenance, repairs, moves and cleaning requests
A small to mid-sized facilities team
A Power Apps or Microsoft Lists front end
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a facilities management or CAFM system
Planned preventive maintenance, which needs asset schedules
design-a-facilities-request-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Facilities Requests
  Title            Single line     short summary                                   required
  RequestType      Choice          Repair | Cleaning | Move | Furniture | Access | Heating and cooling | Other   required
  Description      Multiple lines  plain text
  Building         Choice or lookup to a Locations list                            required, indexed
  Floor            Single line
  RoomOrArea       Single line                                                     required
  Urgency          Choice          Safety risk | Stops work | Normal | When convenient   (set by requester)
  Priority         Choice          P1 | P2 | P3 | P4                                (set by the team, indexed)
  Status           Choice          New | Assigned | In progress | Waiting for parts | Completed | Cancelled   default New, indexed
  RequestedBy      Person          default current user                            indexed
  ContactPhone     Single line
  AssignedTo       Person          technician or contractor contact                indexed
  Contractor       Single line     external company, if used
  TargetDate       Date            calculated by a flow from Priority              indexed
  CompletedOn      Date and time
  ResolutionNotes  Multiple lines
  Cost             Currency
  Satisfaction     Number (1-5)    from a follow-up
  Attachments      on              photos of the problem

Target days by priority (flow on create):  P1 = same day, P2 = 2, P3 = 5, P4 = 15

Views
  Open by building : Status not Completed and not Cancelled, group by Building, sort Priority
  My requests      : RequestedBy = [Me]
  Assigned to me   : AssignedTo = [Me] AND Status not Completed
  Overdue          : TargetDate < [Today] AND Status not Completed
  Safety           : Urgency = Safety risk AND Status not Completed

Validation
  Column validation on CompletedOn is not possible across columns; use list validation:
  =IF([Status]="Completed", NOT(ISBLANK([ResolutionNotes])), TRUE)
  Message: "Add resolution notes before completing the request."

Automation
  New request with Urgency = Safety risk -> post to the facilities Teams channel immediately
  Status = Completed -> email the requester with a one-question satisfaction rating
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with request type, structured location, urgency and priority columns.
Keep the requester's urgency separate from the team's priority.
Add status, assignee, target date and completion columns.
Build views by building, by assignee and for overdue and safety items.
Index the columns used in view filters before the list passes 5,000 items.
commonMistakes: A single free-text location field.
Letting requesters set the team's priority.
No completion notes, so repeat problems cannot be spotted.
troubleshooting: If requesters skip the room, make it required and add an example in the column description.
If the list validation blocks unrelated edits, check the formula returns TRUE for every status other than Completed.
If photos make the list slow to sync, store them in a linked library instead of attachments.
If the same fault recurs, add an Asset or Equipment column and report by it.

design-an-it-access-request-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for requesting, approving and later reviewing access to systems and shared resources.
design-an-it-access-request-list-schema.fullDescription: Access requests need an audit trail: who asked, for whom, to what, at which level, who approved and when access ends. This schema records each of those and supports removal and periodic review.
design-an-it-access-request-list-schema.problemStatement: Access is granted from chat messages, nobody records who approved it, and access is never removed when people change role.
whenToUse: Requests for application, shared mailbox, site or folder access
Organisations without an identity governance tool
Audits that ask who approved access
whenNotToUse: Tenants using Microsoft Entra entitlement management and access packages
Privileged admin access, which needs a dedicated process
design-an-it-access-request-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Access Requests
  Title             Single line     generated: "<System> - <User>"
  RequestType       Choice          New access | Change level | Remove access       required
  AccessFor         Person          the person who needs access                     required, indexed
  RequestedBy       Person          default current user
  System            Lookup          to a Systems list (Title, OwnerEmail, DataClassification)   required, indexed
  AccessLevel       Choice          Read | Contribute | Admin | Custom              required
  CustomDetail      Single line     when level is Custom
  BusinessReason    Multiple lines                                                  required
  StartDate         Date            default today
  EndDate           Date            required for contractors and Admin level        indexed
  IsTemporary       Yes/No

  Status            Choice          Submitted | Manager approval | System owner approval | Approved |
                                    Provisioned | Rejected | Removed | Expired      default Submitted, indexed
  ManagerApprover   Person          ManagerDecisionOn      Date and time
  SystemApprover    Person          SystemDecisionOn       Date and time
  RejectionReason   Multiple lines
  ProvisionedBy     Person          ProvisionedOn          Date and time
  RemovedOn         Date and time
  TicketReference   Single line     service desk ticket, if any
  LastReviewedOn    Date            NextReviewDate   Date                          indexed

Supporting list: Systems
  Title | SystemOwner (Person) | BackupOwner (Person) | DataClassification (Choice) | AccessLevelsAvailable | ReviewMonths (Number)

Views
  Awaiting my approval : (ManagerApprover = [Me] AND Status = Manager approval) OR (SystemApprover = [Me] AND Status = System owner approval)
  To provision         : Status = Approved
  Expiring in 30 days  : EndDate <= [Today]+30 AND Status = Provisioned
  Access by system     : Status = Provisioned, group by System
  Access by person     : Status = Provisioned, group by AccessFor
  Review due           : NextReviewDate <= [Today]+30 AND Status = Provisioned

Validation (list)
  =IF(OR([AccessLevel]="Admin",[IsTemporary]=TRUE), NOT(ISBLANK([EndDate])), TRUE)
  Message: "Admin and temporary access need an end date."

Permissions
  Requesters: add items, read their own (item-level permissions: read items created by the user)
  IT and approvers: read all, through a flow or a group

Automation
  Create: manager approval, then system owner approval, then task for IT
  Daily: set Expired where EndDate has passed and notify IT to remove access
stepByStepInstructions: Create a Systems list with an owner per system.
Create the requests list with who the access is for, the system, the level and the reason.
Add approval, provisioning, end date and review columns.
Build views for approvers, the provisioning queue, expiring access and reviews.
Restrict who can read all requests, and automate approvals and expiry.
commonMistakes: Recording that access was requested but not that it was granted or removed.
No end date for temporary access.
Approval by the requester's manager only, with no say for the system owner.
troubleshooting: If the awaiting approval view is slow on a large list, split it into two views, as an OR filter cannot use indexes well.
If requesters can see each other's requests, set item-level permissions in the list's advanced settings.
If approvals stall, show the current approver and age in the view and add reminders.
If the list is used as evidence, turn on versioning and restrict editing of decision columns to flows.

design-a-training-request-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for staff training requests, with cost, approval, attendance and certificate tracking.
design-a-training-request-list-schema.fullDescription: Training requests involve a cost decision, a booking and a result. This schema captures the course and justification, the approval and budget details, and then what happened: attended, completed, certificate and expiry.
design-a-training-request-list-schema.problemStatement: Training is approved by email, nobody tracks the budget spent, and certificates that expire are discovered after the fact.
whenToUse: Teams approving external courses and conferences
Tracking a training budget
Certifications that need renewal
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a learning management system that handles requests
Mandatory e-learning tracked elsewhere
design-a-training-request-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Training Requests
  Title             Single line     course or event name                             required
  Attendee          Person          default current user                             required, indexed
  Provider          Single line
  CourseLink        Hyperlink
  TrainingType      Choice          Course | Certification | Conference | Workshop | Online subscription
  DeliveryMode      Choice          In person | Virtual | Self-paced
  StartDate         Date            EndDate   Date                                   indexed
  WorkingDaysAway   Number
  BusinessBenefit   Multiple lines  how this helps the role or team                  required
  LinkedObjective   Single line     development plan objective, optional

  Costs
  CourseFee         Currency        TravelCost   Currency       OtherCost   Currency
  TotalCost         Calculated      =[CourseFee]+[TravelCost]+[OtherCost]
  CostCentre        Single line     FinancialYear  Choice                             indexed

  Approval
  Status            Choice          Draft | Submitted | Approved | Rejected | Booked | Completed | Cancelled | Did not attend   indexed
  Manager           Person          ManagerDecisionOn  Date     ManagerComment  Multiple lines
  BudgetApprover    Person          required when TotalCost is over the threshold

  Outcome
  BookedOn          Date            BookingReference  Single line
  CompletedOn       Date
  Passed            Choice          Yes | No | Not assessed
  CertificateExpiry Date                                                             indexed
  Feedback          Multiple lines  Rating  Number (1-5)

  Attachments: quote before approval, certificate after completion

Views
  My requests          : Attendee = [Me]
  Awaiting my approval : Manager = [Me] AND Status = Submitted
  To book              : Status = Approved
  This year's spend    : FinancialYear = current, Status in Approved, Booked, Completed, totals on TotalCost, group by CostCentre
  Upcoming             : StartDate >= [Today] AND Status = Booked
  Certificates expiring: CertificateExpiry <= [Today]+90

Validation
  =[EndDate]>=[StartDate]            Message: "End date cannot be before the start date."

Automation
  Submitted -> manager approval; over threshold -> budget approver as well
  Day after EndDate -> ask the attendee to confirm completion, upload the certificate and rate the course
  90 days before CertificateExpiry -> remind attendee and manager
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with course details, dates and a business benefit.
Add cost columns with a calculated total, a cost centre and a financial year.
Add status, approval and outcome columns, including certificate expiry.
Build views for requesters, approvers, bookings, spend and expiring certificates.
Automate approval, post-course follow-up and expiry reminders.
commonMistakes: Tracking the request but not whether the training happened.
A single cost field that hides travel.
No financial year, so spend cannot be totalled by budget period.
troubleshooting: If view totals do not show for the calculated column, set the calculated column's return type to Currency or Number.
If managers cannot find requests, add the awaiting approval view to the Teams channel as a tab.
If spend reports include rejected requests, filter the spend view by status.
If certificate reminders go to leavers, check the attendee account is active in the flow.

design-a-policy-exception-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for requesting, approving and reviewing time-limited exceptions to a policy.
design-a-policy-exception-list-schema.fullDescription: A policy exception is an accepted risk with an owner and an end date. This schema records what rule is being set aside, why, what reduces the risk in the meantime, who accepted it and when it must be reviewed or closed.
design-a-policy-exception-list-schema.problemStatement: Exceptions are granted in meetings and never revisited, so temporary workarounds become permanent and nobody owns the risk.
whenToUse: Security, IT, finance or HR policy exceptions
Audits that ask for evidence of risk acceptance
Exceptions that must expire
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a GRC tool that tracks exceptions
Permanent changes, which should update the policy itself
design-a-policy-exception-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Policy Exceptions
  Title               Single line     short description                              required
  ExceptionId         Single line     generated, e.g. EXC-2026-014
  Policy              Lookup or Choice  the policy concerned                         required, indexed
  PolicyClause        Single line     section or control reference
  RequestedBy         Person          Department  Choice                             indexed
  ExceptionOwner      Person          accountable while the exception stands         required
  Description         Multiple lines  what will be done differently                  required
  BusinessJustification Multiple lines                                               required
  AffectedScope       Multiple lines  systems, sites, teams or data covered
  RiskDescription     Multiple lines
  RiskRating          Choice          Low | Medium | High | Critical                 indexed
  CompensatingControls Multiple lines what reduces the risk meanwhile                required for Medium and above
  RemediationPlan     Multiple lines  how and when compliance will be restored

  StartDate           Date
  ExpiryDate          Date            maximum 12 months from start                   required, indexed
  ReviewDate          Date            midpoint check                                 indexed

  Status              Choice          Draft | Submitted | Under review | Approved | Rejected | Expired | Closed (compliant) | Renewed   indexed
  PolicyOwnerDecision Choice          Pending | Approve | Reject     PolicyOwner  Person
  RiskAcceptedBy      Person          senior approver for High and Critical
  DecisionDate        Date            DecisionNotes  Multiple lines
  RenewalOf           Lookup          to this list, for renewed exceptions
  RenewalCount        Number

Views
  Active exceptions    : Status = Approved, group by Policy, sort ExpiryDate
  Expiring in 60 days  : Status = Approved AND ExpiryDate <= [Today]+60
  High and critical    : Status = Approved AND RiskRating = High or Critical
  Awaiting decision    : Status = Submitted or Under review
  By department        : Status = Approved, group by Department

Validation
  =AND([ExpiryDate]>[StartDate], [ExpiryDate]<=[StartDate]+366)
  Message: "Exceptions can last at most 12 months."

Settings: versioning on; decision columns edited only by approvers (through a flow or app).

Automation
  Submitted -> policy owner approval; High or Critical -> second approval by the risk owner
  60 and 30 days before expiry -> ask the owner to close, or renew with a fresh justification
  On ExpiryDate -> Status = Expired, notify the policy owner
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with the policy, the exception detail and the justification.
Add risk rating, compensating controls and a remediation plan.
Require an expiry date and limit how long an exception can last.
Add decision columns for the policy owner and a senior risk approver.
Build views for active and expiring exceptions, and automate reminders and expiry.
commonMistakes: Exceptions with no expiry date.
Approval by the requester's own manager only.
Renewing repeatedly with no record of how many times.
troubleshooting: If expired exceptions stay marked Approved, the daily expiry flow is not running or its date filter is wrong.
If the validation blocks drafts with empty dates, wrap it so blank dates pass until submission.
If approvers edit the request text, lock those columns once the status moves past Draft, in the app or with a flow.
If reporting by policy is hard with free text, make Policy a lookup to a policies list.

design-a-change-advisory-board-list-sche.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for change requests going to a change advisory board, with risk, schedule, approval and post-implementation review.
design-a-change-advisory-board-list-sche.fullDescription: A change record has to answer what is changing, when, what could go wrong and how it will be undone. This schema captures those answers, supports a CAB meeting agenda view and a forward schedule, and records the outcome.
design-a-change-advisory-board-list-sche.problemStatement: Changes are announced in chat, collide with each other, and after a failed change nobody can find what was planned or who approved it.
whenToUse: IT or operations teams introducing change control
Weekly CAB meetings
Small to mid-sized change volumes
whenNotToUse: Teams with an ITSM tool that includes change management
Fully automated deployment pipelines with their own approvals
design-a-change-advisory-board-list-sche.formulaOrCode:
List: Change Requests
  Title              Single line     summary of the change                          required
  ChangeNumber       Single line     generated, e.g. CHG-00231
  ChangeType         Choice          Standard (pre-approved) | Normal | Emergency   required, indexed
  Category           Choice          Application | Infrastructure | Network | Security | Data | Power Platform
  AffectedService    Lookup or Choice                                               indexed
  Requester          Person          ChangeOwner  Person (implements it)            indexed
  Description        Multiple lines  what and why                                   required
  ImplementationPlan Multiple lines  steps                                          required
  TestPlan           Multiple lines  how success is confirmed
  BackoutPlan        Multiple lines  how to undo                                    required for Normal and Emergency
  Impact             Choice          Low | Medium | High      (who is affected and how badly)
  Likelihood         Choice          Low | Medium | High      (chance of failure)
  RiskLevel          Choice          Low | Medium | High      set from the two above
  OutageExpected     Yes/No          OutageMinutes  Number
  UsersNotified      Yes/No

  PlannedStart       Date and time                                                  required, indexed
  PlannedEnd         Date and time
  CabDate            Date            meeting where it will be reviewed              indexed

  Status             Choice          Draft | Submitted | CAB review | Approved | Rejected | Scheduled |
                                     Implemented | Failed | Backed out | Cancelled   indexed
  CabDecision        Choice          Pending | Approved | Approved with conditions | Rejected | Deferred
  CabNotes           Multiple lines  Conditions  Multiple lines
  ApprovedBy         Person (multiple)

  ActualStart        Date and time   ActualEnd  Date and time
  Outcome            Choice          Successful | Successful with issues | Failed | Backed out
  PirRequired        Yes/No          PirNotes   Multiple lines   (post-implementation review)
  RelatedIncident    Single line

Views
  CAB agenda          : CabDate = next meeting AND Status = Submitted or CAB review, sort RiskLevel then PlannedStart
  Forward schedule    : Calendar view on PlannedStart / PlannedEnd, Status = Approved or Scheduled
  My changes          : ChangeOwner = [Me]
  Emergency changes   : ChangeType = Emergency, last 90 days
  Awaiting PIR        : PirRequired = Yes AND PirNotes is empty AND Status = Implemented, Failed or Backed out

Validation
  =[PlannedEnd]>[PlannedStart]
  =IF([ChangeType]<>"Standard", NOT(ISBLANK([BackoutPlan])), TRUE)     (as list validation, combine with AND)

Automation
  Submitted -> set CabDate to the next meeting if lead time is met, else the one after
  CAB decision Approved -> Status = Scheduled, add to the shared calendar, notify the owner
  PlannedEnd passed with no outcome -> ask the owner to record the result
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with change type, description and implementation, test and backout plans.
Add impact, likelihood and risk columns and the planned window.
Add CAB date, decision and conditions columns.
Add actual times, outcome and review columns.
Build an agenda view, a calendar of scheduled changes and a view for missing reviews.
commonMistakes: No backout plan.
Treating every change as normal, so low-risk standard changes clog the CAB.
Closing changes without recording the outcome.
troubleshooting: If the calendar view misses changes, it needs both start and end date columns and the status filter.
If the agenda view needs a moving date, set CabDate by flow and filter the view on CabDate >= [Today] and <= [Today]+7.
If two validation rules are needed, combine them with AND in the single list validation formula.
If overlapping changes are not noticed, add a view grouped by AffectedService and sorted by PlannedStart.

design-a-vendor-risk-review-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for assessing and periodically re-assessing the risk each vendor poses.
design-a-vendor-risk-review-list-schema.fullDescription: Vendor risk reviews ask what the vendor does for you, what data they touch and how well they protect it. This schema keeps one row per review, linked to a vendor, with tiering, assessment results, findings and the next review date.
design-a-vendor-risk-review-list-schema.problemStatement: Vendors are assessed once at signing and never again, and nobody can list which vendors hold personal data or are overdue for review.
whenToUse: Organisations that must evidence third-party risk management
A manageable number of vendors, in the hundreds
Annual or biennial reviews
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a third-party risk platform
Storing completed questionnaires that contain the vendor's confidential details without access controls
design-a-vendor-risk-review-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Vendors (one row per vendor)
  Title | VendorOwner (Person) | ServiceDescription | Criticality (Choice: Low, Medium, High, Critical)
  DataAccess (Choice: None, Internal, Personal data, Sensitive personal data, Financial)
  Tier (Choice: 1, 2, 3)   set from criticality and data access       ContractEnd (Date)
  CurrentRiskRating (Choice)   LastReviewDate   NextReviewDate (indexed)

List: Vendor Risk Reviews (one row per review)
  Title              Single line     "<Vendor> - <Year> review"
  Vendor             Lookup          to Vendors                                     required, indexed
  ReviewType         Choice          Onboarding | Periodic | Triggered (incident, change of service)
  Reviewer           Person          ReviewStart  Date     ReviewCompleted  Date     indexed
  Status             Choice          Planned | Questionnaire sent | Awaiting vendor | Assessing |
                                     Findings open | Completed                       indexed

  Assessment areas (each Choice: Satisfactory | Minor gaps | Major gaps | Not assessed | Not applicable)
    InformationSecurity | DataProtection | BusinessContinuity | FinancialStability | Compliance | Subcontractors

  Evidence
  CertificationsHeld  Choice (multiple)   ISO 27001 | SOC 2 Type II | Cyber Essentials | PCI DSS | None
  CertificateExpiry   Date
  QuestionnaireLink   Hyperlink        to a restricted document library
  EvidenceLink        Hyperlink

  Result
  InherentRisk       Choice          Low | Medium | High | Critical
  ResidualRisk       Choice          Low | Medium | High | Critical                  indexed
  FindingsSummary    Multiple lines
  OpenFindingsCount  Number
  RemediationDue     Date                                                            indexed
  Decision           Choice          Approve | Approve with conditions | Do not use | Exit plan required
  DecisionBy         Person          DecisionOn  Date
  NextReviewDate     Date            Tier 1: 12 months, Tier 2: 24, Tier 3: 36

Optional list: Review Findings (Finding, ReviewId, Severity, Owner, DueDate, Status)

Views
  Reviews in progress : Status <> Completed, group by Status
  Overdue reviews     : (on Vendors) NextReviewDate < [Today]
  High residual risk  : ResidualRisk = High or Critical AND Status = Completed, latest per vendor
  Remediation overdue : RemediationDue < [Today] AND OpenFindingsCount > 0
  Tier 1 vendors      : (on Vendors) Tier = 1

Automation
  Review completed -> copy ResidualRisk and dates to the vendor row
  90 days before NextReviewDate -> create the next review row and notify the vendor owner
stepByStepInstructions: Create a Vendors list with criticality, data access and tier.
Create a reviews list linked to the vendor, with assessment areas and evidence links.
Record inherent and residual risk, findings and a decision.
Set the next review date from the tier and copy results to the vendor row.
Build views for overdue reviews, high risk vendors and overdue remediation.
commonMistakes: Overwriting a single review row each year, losing history.
The same review depth for every vendor regardless of tier.
Storing questionnaires in attachments everyone can read.
troubleshooting: If the vendor row shows an old rating, the copy-back flow did not run on completion.
If sensitive evidence is exposed, move it to a library with restricted permissions and link to it.
If reviews stall waiting for vendors, track the date the questionnaire was sent and chase at 14 and 28 days.
If the lookup hits view limits, reduce the number of lookup and person columns shown in each view.

design-a-contract-intake-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for submitting contracts for review and tracking them through legal, signature and renewal.
design-a-contract-intake-list-schema.fullDescription: Contract intake gives legal and procurement what they need up front: the counterparty, value, term and what is unusual. This schema follows the contract through review, negotiation and signature, then keeps the dates that matter afterwards.
design-a-contract-intake-list-schema.problemStatement: Contracts are sent to legal with missing information, sit in inboxes, and auto-renew because nobody recorded the notice date.
whenToUse: Legal or procurement teams handling contract requests
Tracking turnaround and workload
A register of signed contracts and key dates
whenNotToUse: Organisations with contract lifecycle management software
Highly confidential agreements that need matter-level security
design-a-contract-intake-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List: Contract Requests
  Title              Single line     "<Counterparty> - <Agreement type>"            required
  ContractRef        Single line     generated, e.g. CT-2026-0187
  AgreementType      Choice          NDA | Master services | Statement of work | Licence | Supply |
                                     Data processing | Lease | Amendment | Other     required, indexed
  Counterparty       Single line                                                    required, indexed
  CounterpartyContact Single line
  Requester          Person          BusinessOwner  Person     Department  Choice    indexed
  Summary            Multiple lines  what is being bought or agreed                  required
  PaperSource        Choice          Our template | Their paper | Negotiated draft
  ContractValue      Currency        ValueBasis  Choice (Total | Per year)
  Currency           Choice
  TermMonths         Number
  PersonalData       Yes/No          triggers a data protection review
  NonStandardTerms   Multiple lines  anything unusual the requester knows about
  NeededBy           Date                                                           indexed
  Priority           Choice          Standard | Expedite (with reason)

  Workflow
  Status             Choice          Submitted | Triage | In legal review | With counterparty | With business |
                                     Approved for signature | Out for signature | Signed | Withdrawn   indexed
  AssignedLawyer     Person                                                         indexed
  RiskLevel          Choice          Low | Medium | High
  ReviewNotes        Multiple lines (append changes)
  ApprovalsNeeded    Choice (multiple)   Finance | Security | Data protection | Executive
  SignatoryInternal  Person          SignatoryExternal  Single line

  After signature
  SignedDate         Date
  EffectiveDate      Date            ExpiryDate  Date                                indexed
  AutoRenews         Yes/No          NoticePeriodDays  Number
  NoticeDeadline     Calculated      =IF(ISBLANK([ExpiryDate]),"",[ExpiryDate]-[NoticePeriodDays])
  SignedCopyLink     Hyperlink       to a restricted library

Views
  Intake queue        : Status = Submitted or Triage, sort NeededBy
  My matters          : AssignedLawyer = [Me] AND Status not Signed and not Withdrawn
  Waiting on others   : Status = With counterparty or With business, sort Modified ascending
  Signed register     : Status = Signed, group by AgreementType
  Renewals in 90 days : Status = Signed AND ExpiryDate <= [Today]+90
  By department       : open requests grouped by Department

Documents: a library with a ContractRef column or a document set per contract. Drafts as versions, signed copy marked.

Validation
  Add an ExpediteReason column and require it when Priority = Expedite:
  =IF([Priority]="Expedite", NOT(ISBLANK([ExpediteReason])), TRUE)

Automation
  Submitted -> acknowledge with the reference and a target date by agreement type
  PersonalData = Yes -> add Data protection to ApprovalsNeeded and notify that team
  Signed -> create reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days before NoticeDeadline
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with agreement type, counterparty, value, term and summary.
Add intake questions that drive routing, such as whose paper and whether personal data is involved.
Add workflow columns for status, assigned lawyer and approvals needed.
Add post-signature dates including notice period and a calculated notice deadline.
Build views for the queue, each lawyer's work, items waiting on others and upcoming renewals.
commonMistakes: Recording expiry but not the notice period.
Keeping drafts and signed copies as list attachments with no versions.
No status for waiting on the counterparty, so legal's turnaround looks worse than it is.
troubleshooting: If the calculated notice deadline shows as a number, set the calculated column's return type to Date.
If requests arrive incomplete, make the key intake columns required and use a form with guidance text.
If confidential contracts are visible too widely, hold those in a separate list or use item-level permissions sparingly.
If turnaround reporting is needed, log status changes to a history list with dates.

design-an-equipment-checkout-list-schema.shortDescription: A SharePoint design for lending equipment: an assets list and a checkouts list that shows what is out, with whom and when it is due back.
design-an-equipment-checkout-list-schema.fullDescription: Equipment lending needs two lists. Assets describes each item and its current state. Checkouts records each loan. Keeping them separate preserves the loan history and makes availability a simple filter.
design-an-equipment-checkout-list-schema.problemStatement: Laptops, cameras and tools are signed out on paper or not at all, items go missing, and nobody knows what is available right now.
whenToUse: Shared pools of laptops, cameras, tools, vehicles or keys
Short-term loans to staff or students
A Power Apps kiosk or mobile app with barcode scanning
whenNotToUse: Permanent assignment of devices, which belongs in asset management
Booking by time slot, which suits a resource calendar
design-an-equipment-checkout-list-schema.formulaOrCode:
List 1: Equipment
  Title            Single line     item name, e.g. "Canon R6 body #2"                required
  AssetTag         Single line     barcode or label value                            unique, indexed
  Category         Choice          Laptop | Camera | Audio | Tool | Vehicle | Key | Other   indexed
  SerialNumber     Single line
  Location         Choice          where it is stored
  Condition        Choice          Good | Fair | Needs repair | Retired
  Status           Choice          Available | Checked out | Reserved | In repair | Missing | Retired   default Available, indexed
  MaxLoanDays      Number          default 7
  Accessories      Multiple lines  what should come back with it
  Photo            Image
  CurrentCheckoutId Number         ID of the open checkout, blank when available
  Notes            Multiple lines

List 2: Checkouts
  Title            Single line     "<AssetTag> - <Borrower>"
  EquipmentId      Number          ID of the item in Equipment                       required, indexed
  AssetTag         Single line     copied for easy searching                         indexed
  Borrower         Person                                                           required, indexed
  IssuedBy         Person
  CheckedOutOn     Date and time   default now
  DueBack          Date                                                             required, indexed
  Purpose          Single line
  ConditionOut     Choice          Good | Fair
  AccessoriesOut   Multiple lines
  ReturnedOn       Date and time                                                    indexed
  ReceivedBy       Person
  ConditionIn      Choice          Good | Fair | Damaged | Incomplete
  ReturnNotes      Multiple lines
  IsOpen           Yes/No          default Yes; set to No on return                  indexed

Why a number instead of a lookup
  Easier to Patch in bulk from Power Apps, delegable, and does not count towards lookup limits.

Views
  Equipment: Available now  : Status = Available, group by Category
  Checkouts: Out now        : IsOpen = Yes, sort DueBack
  Checkouts: Overdue        : IsOpen = Yes AND DueBack < [Today]
  Checkouts: My loans       : Borrower = [Me] AND IsOpen = Yes
  Checkouts: History by item: group by AssetTag

Check out (Power Apps, after scanning a tag)
  With({ item: LookUp(Equipment, AssetTag = txtScan.Text) },
    If(item.Status.Value <> "Available", Notify(item.Title & " is " & item.Status.Value, NotificationType.Error),
       With({ loan: Patch(Checkouts, Defaults(Checkouts), { Title: item.AssetTag & " - " & cmbBorrower.Selected.DisplayName,
                EquipmentId: item.ID, AssetTag: item.AssetTag, DueBack: DateAdd(Today(), item.MaxLoanDays, TimeUnit.Days), IsOpen: true }) },
            Patch(Equipment, item, { Status: { Value: "Checked out" }, CurrentCheckoutId: loan.ID }))))

Return
  Patch(Checkouts, LookUp(Checkouts, ID = item.CurrentCheckoutId), { ReturnedOn: Now(), IsOpen: false, ConditionIn: { Value: ddCondition.Selected.Value } });
  Patch(Equipment, item, { Status: { Value: If(ddCondition.Selected.Value = "Damaged", "In repair", "Available") }, CurrentCheckoutId: Blank() })

Automation: daily flow emails borrowers with loans due tomorrow or overdue, copying the equipment manager after 3 days.
stepByStepInstructions: Create an Equipment list with an asset tag, category, condition and status.
Create a Checkouts list with the item's ID, borrower, due date and return details.
Update the item's status and current checkout whenever a loan opens or closes.
Build views for what is available, what is out and what is overdue.
Add reminders for items due back and overdue.
commonMistakes: One list with borrower columns on the asset, which loses loan history.
No condition recorded at checkout and return.
Letting the item status and the open checkout drift apart.
troubleshooting: If an item shows as checked out with no open loan, a return updated only one list. Add a view of equipment where Status = Checked out and CurrentCheckoutId is empty.
If scanning finds nothing, check the tag value matches the AssetTag column exactly, including leading zeros.
If two people check out the same item, re-read the item's status immediately before creating the loan, as in the formula.
If borrowers ignore reminders, copy their manager after a set number of days.

design-a-knowledge-article-review-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for tracking the review, approval and periodic re-validation of knowledge articles.
design-a-knowledge-article-review-list.fullDescription: Knowledge articles are only useful while they are right. This list tracks each article's owner, audience, review state and next review date, along with feedback, so a knowledge base can be kept current deliberately.
design-a-knowledge-article-review-list.problemStatement: The knowledge base has articles nobody has checked in years, with no owner to ask and no way to tell which ones are trusted.
whenToUse: Help desk, HR or operations knowledge bases
Articles stored as SharePoint pages or documents
Teams that want a review cadence
whenNotToUse: Knowledge bases inside a service desk tool with its own lifecycle
A handful of articles maintained by one person
design-a-knowledge-article-review-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Knowledge Articles
  Title             Single line     article title                                   required
  ArticleId         Single line     KB-0001 style reference                         unique, indexed
  ArticleLink       Hyperlink       the page or document                            required
  Category          Choice          How-to | Troubleshooting | Policy summary | FAQ | Reference   indexed
  Product           Choice or lookup  system or service the article covers          indexed
  Audience          Choice          All staff | Service desk | Managers | IT only
  Summary           Multiple lines  two sentences for search results
  Keywords          Single line

  Ownership
  Author            Person          ArticleOwner  Person (accountable)              indexed
  Reviewer          Person          subject matter expert who validates

  Lifecycle
  Status            Choice          Draft | In review | Published | Needs update | Retired   default Draft, indexed
  PublishedOn       Date
  LastReviewedOn    Date
  ReviewIntervalMonths Number       default 12; 6 for fast-changing topics
  NextReviewDate    Date                                                            indexed
  ReviewOutcome     Choice          Confirmed accurate | Updated | Merged | Retired
  ReviewNotes       Multiple lines (append changes)
  RetiredReason     Single line     ReplacedBy  Lookup to this list

  Usage and feedback (updated by a flow or monthly import)
  ViewsLast90Days   Number
  HelpfulYes        Number          HelpfulNo  Number
  OpenFeedbackCount Number

Optional list: Article Feedback
  Title | ArticleId (indexed) | Helpful (Yes/No) | Comment | SubmittedBy | SubmittedOn | Status (New, Actioned, No action)

Views
  Published          : Status = Published, group by Product
  My articles        : ArticleOwner = [Me]
  Awaiting my review : Reviewer = [Me] AND Status = In review
  Review due         : Status = Published AND NextReviewDate <= [Today]+30
  Needs attention    : Status = Needs update OR OpenFeedbackCount > 0
  Rarely used        : Status = Published AND ViewsLast90Days < 5       (candidates to retire or merge)

Validation
  =IF([Status]="Retired", NOT(ISBLANK([RetiredReason])), TRUE)

Automation
  Status = In review -> approval to the Reviewer; on approval set Published, PublishedOn, NextReviewDate
  Monthly -> email owners their articles due for review
  Review confirmed -> LastReviewedOn = today, NextReviewDate = today + interval
  New feedback with Helpful = No -> increase OpenFeedbackCount and notify the owner
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with a reference, a link to the article, category, product and audience.
Assign an owner and a reviewer to every article.
Add status, published, last reviewed and next review date columns.
Add usage and feedback counts, with a separate feedback list if needed.
Build views for reviews due, articles needing attention and rarely used articles.
commonMistakes: Tracking authors but not accountable owners.
The same review interval for stable and fast-changing topics.
Deleting retired articles so old links break, instead of marking them and pointing to a replacement.
troubleshooting: If the Needs attention view is slow, its OR filter cannot use an index. Split it into two views.
If owners have left, reassign from a view grouped by owner before the next review cycle.
If view counts are needed, take them from the site's usage analytics or a monthly export.
If the article page and its tracking row drift apart, keep the review columns on the Site Pages library itself instead of a separate list.

design-a-site-provisioning-request-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for requesting new sites and Teams, with the details needed to approve and create them consistently.
design-a-site-provisioning-request-list.fullDescription: A provisioning request list replaces ad hoc site creation with a short form: what the site is for, who owns it, how sensitive it is and when it should be reviewed. The same columns drive naming, template choice and automated creation.
design-a-site-provisioning-request-list.problemStatement: Sites and Teams are created freely, with unclear names, one owner and no record of their purpose, and many are abandoned within months.
whenToUse: Tenants where site or Teams creation is restricted or being brought under control
Automated provisioning with Power Automate or PnP
Lifecycle reviews of sites
whenNotToUse: Tenants happy with self-service creation and expiry policies alone
Very small organisations
design-a-site-provisioning-request-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Site Requests
  Title              Single line     requested site name                            required
  Purpose            Multiple lines  what the site is for and who will use it       required
  WorkspaceType      Choice          Team site (with Microsoft 365 group) | Team site with Teams |
                                     Communication site | Project site | Private channel site   required
  Template           Choice          Standard team | Project workspace | Department | Community
  Department         Choice                                                         indexed
  PrimaryOwner       Person                                                         required
  SecondaryOwner     Person          must differ from the primary                   required
  InitialMembers     Person (multiple)
  Sensitivity        Choice          General | Internal | Confidential | Highly confidential   required
  ExternalSharing    Choice          Not needed | Specific guests | Required for a client
  ExternalJustification Multiple lines
  ExpectedEndDate    Date            for projects and time-limited work
  HubSite            Choice          hub to associate with

  Generated by rules
  ProposedAlias      Single line     prefix + cleaned name, e.g. prj-officemove
  ProposedUrl        Single line     /sites/<alias>

  Workflow
  Status             Choice          Submitted | Needs information | Approved | Provisioning | Completed | Rejected | Failed   indexed
  RequestedBy        Person          default current user                           indexed
  Approver           Person          DecisionOn  Date     DecisionNotes  Multiple lines
  SiteUrl            Hyperlink       filled after creation
  GroupId            Single line     Microsoft 365 group ID
  ProvisionedOn      Date and time
  ErrorDetail        Multiple lines

  Lifecycle
  ReviewDate         Date            12 months after creation, or ExpectedEndDate    indexed
  LifecycleStatus    Choice          Active | Review due | Archived | Deleted

Views
  Queue           : Status = Submitted or Needs information
  My requests     : RequestedBy = [Me]
  Failed          : Status = Failed
  Site directory  : Status = Completed, group by Department     (a searchable list of approved sites)
  Review due      : ReviewDate <= [Today]+30 AND LifecycleStatus = Active

Validation
  =[PrimaryOwner]<>[SecondaryOwner] is not supported for person columns in list validation.
  Enforce two different owners in the form or flow instead.
  =IF([ExternalSharing]<>"Not needed", NOT(ISBLANK([ExternalJustification])), TRUE)

Naming rules (flow)
  alias = toLower(prefix-by-type + remove everything except letters, digits and hyphens from Title), max 40 characters
  Check for an existing site or group with that alias before approving.

Automation
  Approved -> create the group or site (Graph or SharePoint REST), apply the template, add owners and members,
              set sensitivity label and sharing, write SiteUrl and GroupId, Status = Completed
  Failure  -> Status = Failed with ErrorDetail, notify the admin
  ReviewDate reached -> ask both owners to confirm the site is still needed
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with purpose, workspace type, two owners and sensitivity.
Add external sharing and expected end date questions.
Generate a proposed alias and URL from naming rules and check for duplicates.
Add workflow columns for approval, the created site's URL and any error.
Keep the completed rows as a site directory with review dates.
commonMistakes: Allowing a single owner.
Collecting a name but not a purpose.
No review date, so sites live for ever.
troubleshooting: If provisioning fails on the alias, it is already used by a group or a deleted group still in the recycle bin.
If owners are not added, the group may not be fully created when the next step runs. Add a short delay or retry.
If requesters choose the wrong type, describe each option in plain words in the form.
If the directory shows sites that no longer exist, update LifecycleStatus when a site is archived or deleted.

design-a-document-approval-register.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design that records every document approval: which version, who approved it, when and with what comments.
design-a-document-approval-register.fullDescription: An approval register is the evidence that a specific version of a document was approved by the right people. Kept as a list alongside the document library, it survives file moves and gives auditors one place to look.
design-a-document-approval-register.problemStatement: Approvals live in email threads and flow run history, which expire, so the organisation cannot show who approved the current version of a policy.
whenToUse: Controlled documents such as policies, procedures and specifications
Quality or compliance audits
Approvals run by Power Automate
whenNotToUse: Informal document review
Regulated e-signature requirements, which need a signature service
design-a-document-approval-register.formulaOrCode:
List: Document Approval Register
  Title             Single line     document title                                  required
  DocumentNumber    Single line     controlled document reference, e.g. POL-HR-012  indexed
  DocumentLink      Hyperlink       link to the file
  VersionLabel      Single line     the version that was approved, e.g. 3.0         required
  DocumentType      Choice          Policy | Procedure | Work instruction | Form | Specification | Plan   indexed
  OwningDepartment  Choice                                                          indexed
  DocumentOwner     Person
  ChangeSummary     Multiple lines  what changed since the last approved version

  Approval
  ApprovalStage     Choice          Technical review | Owner approval | Quality approval | Executive approval
  Approver          Person                                                          required, indexed
  Decision          Choice          Approved | Rejected | Approved with comments    required
  DecisionDate      Date and time                                                   required, indexed
  Comments          Multiple lines
  ApprovalMethod    Choice          Approvals in Teams | Email | Meeting | Wet signature
  ApprovalReference Single line     flow run ID or meeting reference
  EvidenceLink      Hyperlink       exported approval record, where kept

  Lifecycle
  EffectiveDate     Date
