  NextReviewDate    Date                                                            indexed
  Supersedes        Single line     previous version label
  IsCurrent         Yes/No          Yes for the latest approved version only        indexed

One row per approver per version. Three approvers on version 3.0 = three rows.

Views
  Current approved documents : IsCurrent = Yes AND Decision = Approved, group by DocumentType
  By document                : group by DocumentNumber, sort DecisionDate descending   (full history)
  Approvals this quarter     : DecisionDate >= start of quarter
  Review due                 : IsCurrent = Yes AND NextReviewDate <= [Today]+60
  Rejections                 : Decision = Rejected

Settings
  Versioning on. Permissions: flows and document controllers add; nobody edits or deletes
  (item-level permissions: Create and edit access = None, with controllers in a group that has Edit).

Writing rows from the approval flow
  After "Start and wait for an approval", Apply to each on outputs('Approval')?['body/responses']:
    Create item
      Title          : file name
      VersionLabel   : triggerBody()?['{VersionNumber}']
      Approver       : items('Apply_to_each')?['responder']?['email']
      Decision       : items('Apply_to_each')?['approverResponse']
      DecisionDate   : items('Apply_to_each')?['responseDate']
      Comments       : items('Apply_to_each')?['comments']
      ApprovalReference : workflow()?['run']?['name']
  Then set IsCurrent = No on earlier rows for the same DocumentNumber.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the register with the document reference, link and the exact version approved.
Add approver, decision, date, comments and method columns.
Write one row per approver from the approval flow.
Mark only the latest approved version as current.
Lock the list so rows cannot be edited or deleted by ordinary users.
commonMistakes: Recording that a document is approved without recording which version.
One row per document that is overwritten at each approval.
Relying on flow run history, which is kept for a limited time.
troubleshooting: If the version label is blank, read it from the file's properties at the time the approval starts, not afterwards.
If earlier versions still show as current, the flow step that clears IsCurrent is missing or filtered on the wrong reference.
If auditors need the document as approved, link to the specific version URL or keep a PDF copy in a records library.
If approvers respond by email outside the flow, record those manually with the method set to Email and attach the evidence.

design-a-stakeholder-register-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for a project stakeholder register with influence, interest, engagement level and communication needs.
design-a-stakeholder-register-list.fullDescription: A stakeholder register records who is affected by a project, how much they can help or hinder it, how they feel now and what you plan to do about it. As a list, it can be filtered, grouped on a power and interest grid and shared with the team.
design-a-stakeholder-register-list.problemStatement: Stakeholder analysis is done once in a slide and forgotten, so important people are surprised late in the project.
whenToUse: Projects with more than a handful of stakeholders
Change programmes where engagement matters
Teams that share stakeholder contact
whenNotToUse: Small internal tasks with an obvious audience
Sensitive assessments of individuals that should not be shared, unless the list is restricted
design-a-stakeholder-register-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Stakeholder Register
  Title              Single line     stakeholder name (person or group)             required
  StakeholderType    Choice          Individual | Team | Department | External organisation | Committee
  Person             Person          when internal
  Organisation       Single line     RoleTitle  Single line
  Project            Lookup or Single line   for a shared register across projects   indexed
  Category           Choice          Sponsor | Decision maker | User | Subject expert | Supplier | Regulator | Affected party

  Analysis
  Influence          Choice          1 - Low | 2 - Medium | 3 - High                 indexed
  Interest           Choice          1 - Low | 2 - Medium | 3 - High                 indexed
  Strategy           Choice          Manage closely | Keep satisfied | Keep informed | Monitor
                                     (High/High, High influence/Low interest, Low influence/High interest, Low/Low)
  CurrentEngagement  Choice          Unaware | Resistant | Neutral | Supportive | Leading
  DesiredEngagement  Choice          Unaware | Resistant | Neutral | Supportive | Leading
  KeyInterests       Multiple lines  what they care about
  Concerns           Multiple lines  what worries them
  ImpactOfChange     Choice          Low | Medium | High

  Engagement plan
  RelationshipOwner  Person          who on the team manages the relationship       indexed
  PreferredChannel   Choice          Meeting | Email | Teams | Steering group | Newsletter
  Frequency          Choice          Weekly | Fortnightly | Monthly | At milestones
  LastContactDate    Date            NextContactDate  Date                           indexed
  EngagementActions  Multiple lines (append changes)
  Notes              Multiple lines

Calculated helpers
  Strategy can be calculated:
  =IF(AND(LEFT([Influence],1)="3",LEFT([Interest],1)="3"),"Manage closely",
     IF(LEFT([Influence],1)="3","Keep satisfied",
        IF(LEFT([Interest],1)="3","Keep informed","Monitor")))
  EngagementGap : flag where CurrentEngagement <> DesiredEngagement (set in the form or a flow)

Views
  Power and interest grid : group by Influence, then Interest
  Manage closely          : Strategy = Manage closely
  Engagement gaps         : CurrentEngagement <> DesiredEngagement    (via a Yes/No HasGap column)
  My stakeholders         : RelationshipOwner = [Me]
  Contact due             : NextContactDate <= [Today]+7
  Resistant               : CurrentEngagement = Resistant

Permissions
  Assessments of individuals can be sensitive. Limit the list to the project core team.

Automation
  Weekly: email each relationship owner their stakeholders with contact due.
  When an engagement action is logged: set LastContactDate = today and move NextContactDate on by Frequency.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with the stakeholder, type, organisation and category.
Add influence and interest ratings and derive the engagement strategy.
Record current and desired engagement, interests and concerns.
Assign a relationship owner, channel, frequency and next contact date.
Restrict the list to the core team and review it at each project stage.
commonMistakes: Rating influence and interest once and never revisiting.
No relationship owner, so nobody acts.
Sharing candid assessments with the whole project site.
troubleshooting: If the calculated strategy shows an error, the choice values must start with the digit used in the formula.
If a view comparing two columns is needed, SharePoint views cannot compare columns. Add a Yes/No HasGap column set by a flow or the form.
If stakeholders appear twice across projects, use one shared register with a Project column.
If contact dates are never updated, log each contact through a quick form that sets the dates automatically.

design-a-project-communications-log.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for planning and recording project communications: what was sent, to whom, by which channel and with what response.
design-a-project-communications-log.fullDescription: A communications log covers both the plan and the record. Each row is one communication, planned or sent, with its audience, channel, owner and date, plus a link to what was sent and any follow-up it produced.
design-a-project-communications-log.problemStatement: Nobody can confirm whether a group was told about a change, because messages went out from different people's mailboxes with no shared record.
whenToUse: Projects with several audiences and channels
Change programmes that must evidence communication
Teams where more than one person sends updates
whenNotToUse: Small projects with a single weekly update
Marketing campaigns managed in dedicated tools
design-a-project-communications-log.formulaOrCode:
List: Communications Log
  Title             Single line     subject or name of the communication            required
  Project           Single line or lookup                                           indexed
  CommType          Choice          Announcement | Status update | Training invite | Reminder | Decision notice |
                                    Newsletter item | Briefing | FAQ update
  Purpose           Multiple lines  what the audience should know or do afterwards
  KeyMessages       Multiple lines
  Audience          Choice (multiple)   All staff | Managers | Project team | Steering group | Site A | Site B | External
  AudienceSize      Number
  Channel           Choice          Email | Teams post | Intranet news | Town hall | Team meeting | Poster | SMS   indexed
  Sender            Person          whose name it goes out under
  Owner             Person          who prepares it                                 indexed
  Approver          Person
  LinkedMilestone   Single line     project milestone it supports

  Timing and state
  PlannedDate       Date                                                            indexed
  Status            Choice          Planned | Drafting | Awaiting approval | Approved | Sent | Cancelled   default Planned, indexed
  SentDate          Date and time
  ContentLink       Hyperlink       the email, post or page as sent
  Attachments       on              final copy, if short

  Response
  FeedbackSummary   Multiple lines
  QuestionsRaised   Number
  FollowUpNeeded    Yes/No          FollowUpAction  Multiple lines     FollowUpOwner  Person
  Effectiveness     Choice          Not measured | Low | Medium | High     (open rate, attendance or survey)

Views
  Calendar            : calendar view on PlannedDate, all statuses except Cancelled
  This week           : PlannedDate between [Today] and [Today]+7
  Awaiting approval   : Status = Awaiting approval
  Sent log            : Status = Sent, sort SentDate descending
  By audience         : Status = Sent, group by Audience
  Follow-up open      : FollowUpNeeded = Yes
  Overdue             : PlannedDate < [Today] AND Status not Sent and not Cancelled

Validation
  =IF([Status]="Sent", NOT(ISBLANK([SentDate])), TRUE)
  Message: "Enter the date the communication was sent."

Automation
  3 working days before PlannedDate and still Planned or Drafting -> remind the owner
  Status = Awaiting approval -> approval to the Approver, then Approved
  Status = Sent -> stamp SentDate if empty; if LinkedMilestone is set, note it on the milestone
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with type, purpose, key messages, audience and channel.
Add owner, sender and approver columns.
Add planned date, status, sent date and a link to what was sent.
Record feedback and follow-up actions.
Build a calendar view of the plan and a log view of what has been sent.
commonMistakes: Logging only what was sent, with no forward plan.
Free-text audiences that cannot be grouped.
No link to the actual content.
troubleshooting: If the calendar view is crowded, filter it by project or audience.
If multi-choice audience grouping looks odd, grouping on multi-select columns groups by each combination. Use a filter per audience instead.
If the sent date is often missing, stamp it with a flow when the status changes to Sent.
If communications go out without approval, restrict who can set the status to Approved.

design-a-lessons-learned-capture-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for capturing lessons learned so they can be searched, acted on and reused by later projects.
design-a-lessons-learned-capture-list.fullDescription: Lessons are only learned if someone can find and apply them. This schema separates what happened from the recommendation, tags each lesson so it can be found, and tracks whether the recommendation was actually adopted.
design-a-lessons-learned-capture-list.problemStatement: Lessons learned are written into closure reports that nobody reads, and the next project repeats the same mistakes.
whenToUse: PMOs and teams running repeated projects
Capturing lessons during a project, not only at the end
Building a searchable library
whenNotToUse: Incident post-mortems with a formal process of their own
Feedback about individuals, which belongs elsewhere
design-a-lessons-learned-capture-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Lessons Learned
  Title             Single line     the lesson in one sentence                       required
  Project           Single line or lookup                                           indexed
  ProjectType       Choice          Software | Infrastructure | Process change | Construction | Office move | Other   indexed
  Phase             Choice          Initiation | Planning | Delivery | Testing | Go-live | Closure                indexed
  Theme             Choice          Scope | Schedule | Budget | Suppliers | Communication | Resourcing | Quality |
                                    Risk | Technology | Stakeholders | Governance   indexed
  LessonType        Choice          Went well (repeat) | Went badly (avoid) | Idea (try)

  The lesson
  WhatHappened      Multiple lines  the situation and what was done                  required
  Impact            Multiple lines  effect on time, cost, quality or people
  ImpactLevel       Choice          Low | Medium | High                              indexed
  RootCause         Multiple lines  why it happened
  Recommendation    Multiple lines  what to do next time, written as an instruction   required

  Follow-through
  RaisedBy          Person          RaisedOn  Date (default today)
  Status            Choice          Captured | Reviewed | Action agreed | Embedded | No action   indexed
  ActionOwner       Person
  Action            Multiple lines  change to a template, checklist, standard or training
  ActionDueDate     Date
  EmbeddedIn        Single line     name of the template or process that was updated
  ReviewedBy        Person          ReviewedOn  Date

  Reuse
  Keywords          Single line
  ApplicableTo      Choice (multiple)   All projects | Projects with suppliers | Projects with go-live | Large projects
  TimesReferenced   Number

Views
  Library            : Status = Reviewed, Action agreed or Embedded; group by Theme
  For new projects   : ImpactLevel = High, group by Phase     (read at kick-off)
  By project type    : group by ProjectType, then Theme
  To review          : Status = Captured
  Actions open       : Status = Action agreed AND EmbeddedIn is empty
  Went well          : LessonType = Went well (repeat)

Capture during the project
  A short form (Microsoft Forms or a Power App) with four questions: what happened, impact, why, what next time.
  Add a five-minute lessons slot to regular project meetings.

Automation
  New item -> notify the PMO reviewer
  Project start (new row in the projects list) -> email the project manager the high-impact lessons for that project type
  Action due date passed -> remind the action owner
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with project, type, phase and theme for finding lessons later.
Capture what happened, the impact, the cause and a clear recommendation.
Add review status, an action, an owner and where the lesson was embedded.
Build views for the library, for new projects and for open actions.
Capture lessons throughout the project and send relevant ones to new project managers.
commonMistakes: Recording observations with no recommendation.
Capturing lessons only at closure, when details are forgotten.
No one responsible for turning a lesson into a change.
troubleshooting: If the library is ignored, send lessons to people at the moment they start a similar project.
If entries are vague, require the recommendation to start with a verb and review new entries weekly.
If the same lesson recurs, it was captured but not embedded. Check the Actions open view.
If search does not find lessons, fill in keywords and use the theme and phase filters.

design-a-meeting-decision-capture-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for recording decisions made in meetings, with context, owner and follow-up, so they can be found later.
design-a-meeting-decision-capture-list.fullDescription: Decisions buried in minutes are hard to find and easy to dispute. A decision log holds one row per decision with what was decided, why, by whom and what happens next, searchable across meetings.
design-a-meeting-decision-capture-list.problemStatement: Three months on, nobody can find when a decision was made or what was agreed, and the same question is reopened.
whenToUse: Steering groups, boards and project meetings
Programmes with many interdependent decisions
Teams that need an audit trail of who decided what
whenNotToUse: Informal team meetings with no lasting decisions
Board minutes with legal status, which have their own process
design-a-meeting-decision-capture-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Decision Log
  Title             Single line     the decision in one sentence, e.g. "Go-live moved to 12 May"   required
  DecisionRef       Single line     DEC-0042                                         unique, indexed
  Meeting           Single line     forum where it was made                          indexed
  MeetingDate       Date                                                            required, indexed
  Project           Single line or lookup                                           indexed
  Topic             Choice          Scope | Schedule | Budget | Resourcing | Technical | Supplier | Risk | Policy   indexed

  The decision
  Context           Multiple lines  the question or problem                          required
  OptionsConsidered Multiple lines
  Decision          Multiple lines  what was decided, in full                        required
  Rationale         Multiple lines  why this option
  DecisionType      Choice          Approved | Rejected | Deferred | Direction given | Noted
  DecisionMaker     Person          chair or accountable person                      required
  Attendees         Person (multiple) or Multiple lines
  Dissent           Multiple lines  recorded objections, if any

  Follow-up
  Status            Choice          Open | Actioned | Superseded | Reversed          default Open, indexed
  ActionRequired    Multiple lines
  ActionOwner       Person                                                          indexed
  ActionDueDate     Date                                                            indexed
  CompletedOn       Date
  Supersedes        Lookup          to this list
  SupersededBy      Lookup          to this list
  RelatedLinks      Hyperlink       paper, minutes or change request

  ImpactArea        Choice (multiple)   Cost | Time | Scope | Quality | People | Compliance
  CostImpact        Currency        ScheduleImpactDays  Number

Views
  Latest decisions   : sort MeetingDate descending
  By meeting         : group by Meeting, then MeetingDate
  By topic           : group by Topic
  Open actions       : Status = Open AND ActionRequired is not empty, sort ActionDueDate
  My actions         : ActionOwner = [Me] AND Status = Open
  Deferred           : DecisionType = Deferred      (items to bring back)
  Current decisions  : Status <> Superseded AND Status <> Reversed

Good practice
  Write the title so it stands alone. "Approved option B" means nothing next year.
  Record the decision in the meeting, on screen, and read it back before moving on.
  When a decision is changed, add a new row and link the two. Do not edit the original.

Settings: versioning on. Limit editing to the meeting secretary or PMO.

Automation
  New decision with an action -> notify the action owner (or create a Planner task)
  After each meeting -> email attendees the decisions recorded that day (filter by MeetingDate)
  Deferred decisions -> list on the next meeting's agenda
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with a reference, the meeting, date, project and topic.
Capture context, options, the decision and the reasoning.
Record who decided and any follow-up action with an owner and date.
Link decisions that replace earlier ones.
Record decisions live in the meeting and send a summary afterwards.
commonMistakes: Titles that only make sense on the day.
Editing an old decision instead of adding a new one that supersedes it.
Recording the decision without the reasoning.
troubleshooting: If decisions are disputed, record them on screen in the meeting and confirm the wording.
If actions are lost, create a task for each from the list.
If the log grows across many forums, filter views by Meeting and index that column.
If superseded decisions confuse readers, default to the Current decisions view.

design-an-operational-handoff-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for handing a project's deliverables over to the operations team, item by item, with acceptance.
design-an-operational-handoff-list.fullDescription: Handover fails when it is one meeting and a document. This list breaks it into items, each with a deliverer, a receiver, evidence and an acceptance status, so operations takes on only what is ready and gaps are visible.
design-an-operational-handoff-list.problemStatement: The project team disbands, and the support team finds it owns a system with no documentation, no admin access and unknown open issues.
whenToUse: Projects handing over a system, service or process to business as usual
Go-lives with a hypercare period
Operations teams that want formal acceptance
whenNotToUse: Small changes covered by a change request
Teams where the builders also run the service
design-an-operational-handoff-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Operational Handoff
  Title             Single line     handoff item, e.g. "Admin access for support team"   required
  Project           Single line or lookup                                           indexed
  Category          Choice          Documentation | Access and accounts | Monitoring and alerts | Support process |
                                    Training | Open issues | Contracts and licences | Data and backups |
                                    Environments | Known limitations                 indexed
  Description       Multiple lines  what is being handed over
  AcceptanceCriteria Multiple lines what "done" looks like for the receiver         required
  Mandatory         Yes/No          must be accepted before go-live

  People
  DeliveredBy       Person          project side                                    indexed
  ReceivedBy        Person          operations side                                 indexed
  ReceivingTeam     Choice          Service desk | Application support | Infrastructure | Business admin

  Progress
  Status            Choice          Not started | In progress | Ready for review | Accepted |
                                    Accepted with conditions | Rejected | Not applicable   default Not started, indexed
  DueDate           Date                                                            indexed
  EvidenceLink      Hyperlink       document, runbook, ticket or recording
  ReviewComments    Multiple lines (append changes)
  Conditions        Multiple lines  what remains, when accepted with conditions
  ConditionDueDate  Date
  AcceptedOn        Date
  RiskIfMissing     Choice          Low | Medium | High

Standard items to load for every project (keep in a template list and copy at project start)
  Documentation : architecture overview, runbook, admin guide, user guide, data dictionary
  Access        : admin accounts, service accounts and owners, licence assignments, break-glass procedure
  Monitoring    : alerts configured and routed, health checks, flow failure notifications
  Support       : support model and hours, escalation contacts, knowledge articles, ticket categories
  Training      : support team walkthrough, recorded demo
  Open issues   : defect list with severity, workarounds, enhancement backlog
  Commercial    : vendor contacts, contract and renewal dates, support agreement
  Data          : backup and restore tested, retention rules, data owners

Views
  By category        : group by Category, with Status
  Outstanding        : Status not Accepted, not Accepted with conditions, not Not applicable; sort DueDate
  Mandatory gaps     : Mandatory = Yes AND Status not Accepted
  For my review      : ReceivedBy = [Me] AND Status = Ready for review
  Conditions open    : Status = Accepted with conditions, sort ConditionDueDate

Go-live gate
  Go-live allowed when the Mandatory gaps view is empty.
  Summary for the steering group: count by Status, plus the list of mandatory gaps.

Automation
  Status = Ready for review -> notify ReceivedBy
  Status = Rejected -> notify DeliveredBy with the review comments
  ConditionDueDate passed -> escalate to the project sponsor
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with categories, a description and acceptance criteria per item.
Assign a deliverer on the project side and a receiver on the operations side.
Load a standard set of handoff items at the start of each project.
Track status through to accepted, with evidence links and review comments.
Use the mandatory gaps view as a go-live gate.
commonMistakes: Handover as a single sign-off instead of item by item.
Acceptance criteria written by the project team alone.
Conditions accepted with no date or owner.
troubleshooting: If operations rejects late, involve them in writing acceptance criteria at the start.
If items sit at Ready for review, add a reminder to the receiver after three days.
If the list is created afresh for every project, keep a template list and copy its rows with a flow.
If conditions are forgotten after go-live, review the Conditions open view in hypercare meetings.

design-a-release-readiness-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for go-live readiness: criteria by area, each with an owner, evidence and a red, amber or green status.
design-a-release-readiness-list.fullDescription: A release readiness list turns the go or no-go decision into evidence. Each criterion has an owner, a status and proof, grouped by area, so the decision meeting reviews facts instead of opinions.
design-a-release-readiness-list.problemStatement: The go-live decision is made on a show of hands, and problems that someone knew about surface the day after release.
whenToUse: Software, app or process releases with a go or no-go meeting
Repeated releases that should use the same criteria
Releases needing sign-off from several teams
whenNotToUse: Continuous deployment with automated quality gates
Trivial changes
design-a-release-readiness-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Release Readiness
  Title             Single line     the criterion, e.g. "All severity 1 and 2 defects closed"   required
  Release           Single line or lookup    release name or number                 indexed
  Area              Choice          Testing | Data migration | Security | Performance | Training | Communications |
                                    Support | Infrastructure | Business sign-off | Rollback   indexed
  Criterion         Multiple lines  the measurable condition
  Mandatory         Yes/No          a red on a mandatory criterion means no-go
  Owner             Person                                                          required, indexed
  Status            Choice          Not started | On track | At risk | Met | Not met | Waived   indexed
  Rag               Choice          Green | Amber | Red
  Evidence          Multiple lines  what proves it
  EvidenceLink      Hyperlink       test report, sign-off email, dashboard
  DueDate           Date                                                            indexed
  LastUpdated       Date
  Blockers          Multiple lines
  MitigationIfNotMet Multiple lines
  WaivedBy          Person          WaiverReason  Multiple lines
  SignedOffBy       Person          SignedOffOn  Date

Typical criteria to load per release
  Testing        : test cases executed 100 percent; no open severity 1 or 2 defects; UAT signed off
  Data           : trial migration reconciled; cutover plan rehearsed
  Security       : penetration test findings closed; access roles reviewed
  Performance    : load test meets targets
  Training       : key users trained; guides published
  Communications : go-live notice approved; support contacts published
  Support        : service desk briefed; hypercare rota agreed; handoff items accepted
  Infrastructure : production environment built; monitoring live; backups verified
  Rollback       : rollback plan tested; decision point and owner agreed
  Business       : business owner sign-off recorded

Views
  Readiness board   : group by Area, show Rag, Status, Owner
  Reds and ambers   : Rag = Red or Amber, sort Mandatory descending
  Mandatory not met : Mandatory = Yes AND Status not Met and not Waived      (the go/no-go view)
  My criteria       : Owner = [Me]
  Waivers           : Status = Waived

Column formatting for Rag (a coloured dot)
  { "elmType": "div", "style": { "width": "14px", "height": "14px", "border-radius": "50%",
      "background-color": "=if(@currentField == 'Green', '#107c10', if(@currentField == 'Amber', '#ffb900', '#c4314b'))" } }

Decision rule
  GO                : Mandatory not met view is empty
  GO WITH CONDITIONS: only non-mandatory ambers remain, each with an owner and date
  NO-GO             : any mandatory criterion Not met and not waived
  Record the decision, date and attendees in the decision log.

Automation
  Two days before the decision meeting -> ask owners to update status and evidence
  Status changes to Not met on a mandatory row -> alert the release manager at once
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with area, criterion, owner, status and evidence columns.
Mark which criteria are mandatory.
Load the standard criteria for each release from a template.
Ask owners to update status and attach evidence before the decision meeting.
Decide go or no-go from the mandatory not met view and record any waivers with a named approver.
commonMistakes: Criteria that cannot be measured, such as 'testing is going well'.
Green statuses with no evidence.
Waiving mandatory criteria informally.
troubleshooting: If statuses are stale at the meeting, send the reminder flow and show LastUpdated in the view.
If everything is amber, tighten the definitions: amber means a plan exists to be green by go-live.
If the same criteria are re-typed for each release, copy them from a template list by flow.
If the formatted dot does not show, check the JSON was applied to the Rag column and its values match exactly.

design-a-data-quality-issue-list.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for logging data quality problems, assigning them to data owners and tracking the fix and its root cause.
design-a-data-quality-issue-list.fullDescription: Data quality improves when problems are logged in one place and owned. This schema records what is wrong, where, how many records are affected and what it costs, then tracks correction and prevention separately.
design-a-data-quality-issue-list.problemStatement: People fix bad data in their own spreadsheets, the source system stays wrong, and the same errors return every month.
whenToUse: Teams that depend on shared data, such as reporting, finance or CRM users
Data governance programmes
Before and after a migration
whenNotToUse: Automated data quality monitoring that raises its own tickets
One-off clean-ups
design-a-data-quality-issue-list.formulaOrCode:
List: Data Quality Issues
  Title             Single line     short description, e.g. "Duplicate customer records after import"   required
  IssueRef          Single line     DQ-0105                                          indexed
  SourceSystem      Choice          CRM | ERP | HR system | SharePoint list | Data warehouse | Spreadsheet   required, indexed
  DataDomain        Choice          Customer | Supplier | Product | Employee | Finance | Project   indexed
  EntityOrTable     Single line     table, list or report affected
  FieldsAffected    Single line
  IssueType         Choice          Missing | Duplicate | Incorrect | Inconsistent format | Out of date |
                                    Invalid reference | Not conforming to rule        indexed
  Description       Multiple lines  what is wrong, with an example record             required
  HowFound          Choice          Report check | User report | Reconciliation | Automated rule | Audit
  RecordsAffected   Number
  BusinessImpact    Multiple lines  what goes wrong because of it
  Severity          Choice          Low | Medium | High | Critical                    indexed

  Ownership
  ReportedBy        Person          ReportedOn  Date (default today)
  DataOwner         Person          accountable for the data domain                  indexed
  AssignedTo        Person          data steward doing the work                      indexed

  Resolution
  Status            Choice          New | Triaged | Correcting | Corrected | Prevention in progress | Closed |
                                    Accepted (will not fix)                           default New, indexed
  CorrectionAction  Multiple lines  how the existing records are fixed
  CorrectedOn       Date            RecordsCorrected  Number
  RootCause         Choice          Manual entry error | Missing validation | Integration fault | Migration |
                                    Process gap | Unclear definition | Unknown
  RootCauseDetail   Multiple lines
  PreventionAction  Multiple lines  validation rule, training, process or integration change
  PreventionOwner   Person          PreventionDueDate  Date                          indexed
  VerifiedBy        Person          VerifiedOn  Date
  Recurring         Yes/No          RelatedIssue  Lookup to this list

Views
  Triage             : Status = New, sort Severity
  Open by domain     : Status not Closed and not Accepted, group by DataDomain
  My issues          : AssignedTo = [Me] or DataOwner = [Me] (two views)
  High and critical  : Severity = High or Critical AND Status not Closed
  Awaiting prevention: Status = Corrected or Prevention in progress, sort PreventionDueDate
  Root cause analysis: Status = Closed, group by RootCause           (where to invest)
  Recurring          : Recurring = Yes

Measures to report monthly
  Issues opened and closed, open by severity, average days to correct, share with a prevention action, top root causes.

Automation
  New issue -> look up the data owner for the domain from a reference list and assign
  High or Critical -> notify the data owner immediately
  Corrected with no prevention action after 14 days -> prompt the owner
  Closed -> ask the reporter to confirm the data is now right
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with source system, domain, issue type and an example of the problem.
Record the number of records affected, the business impact and severity.
Assign a data owner by domain and a steward to do the work.
Track correction and prevention as separate steps, with a root cause.
Report monthly on open issues and root causes.
commonMistakes: Closing the issue once records are corrected, with nothing done to stop it recurring.
No example record, so the steward cannot reproduce the problem.
No data owner per domain.
troubleshooting: If issues sit in triage, assign owners automatically from a domain-to-owner reference list.
If the same issue is logged repeatedly, link them with RelatedIssue and mark as recurring.
If root cause is always Unknown, make it required before closing.
If the list contains personal data in examples, restrict access and mask values.

design-a-process-improvement-backlog.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design for collecting, scoring and tracking process improvement ideas from suggestion to measured benefit.
design-a-process-improvement-backlog.fullDescription: An improvement backlog needs to do three things: make it easy to submit an idea, give a fair way to prioritise, and show what happened. This schema scores each idea on value and effort and follows it through to a measured result.
design-a-process-improvement-backlog.problemStatement: Ideas are raised in meetings and forgotten, the loudest request gets done, and nobody measures whether changes helped.
whenToUse: Continuous improvement programmes
Teams automating work with Power Platform
Collecting ideas from staff
whenNotToUse: Formal project portfolios with business cases
Bug tracking for a product
design-a-process-improvement-backlog.formulaOrCode:
List: Improvement Backlog
  Title             Single line     the idea in one sentence                         required
  IdeaRef           Single line     IMP-0231
  ProcessArea       Choice          Finance | HR | Operations | Sales | IT | Customer service | Facilities   indexed
  ProcessName       Single line     the specific process
  ProblemStatement  Multiple lines  what is slow, costly or error-prone today        required
  ProposedChange    Multiple lines  the suggested improvement
  ImprovementType   Choice          Automate | Simplify | Standardise | Eliminate | Digitise a form | Reporting
  SubmittedBy       Person          default current user                             indexed
  SubmittedOn       Date            default today
  Department        Choice

  Sizing (filled at triage)
  PeopleAffected    Number
  FrequencyPerMonth Number          how often the process runs
  MinutesSavedEach  Number          estimate per run
  HoursSavedPerYear Calculated      =[FrequencyPerMonth]*[MinutesSavedEach]*12/60
  OtherBenefits     Choice (multiple)   Fewer errors | Faster turnaround | Compliance | Customer experience | Staff satisfaction
  ValueScore        Choice          1 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 8
  EffortScore       Choice          1 | 2 | 3 | 5 | 8
  PriorityScore     Calculated      =VALUE([ValueScore])/VALUE([EffortScore])     (number, 2 decimals)
  Quadrant          Calculated      =IF(VALUE([ValueScore])>=5,IF(VALUE([EffortScore])<=3,"Quick win","Major project"),
                                       IF(VALUE([EffortScore])<=3,"Fill-in","Reconsider"))

  Progress
  Status            Choice          New | Under review | Approved | In progress | Implemented | Measuring |
                                    Completed | Declined | On hold                    default New, indexed
  Sponsor           Person          Owner  Person                                    indexed
  TargetDate        Date
  DeclineReason     Single line
  Solution          Multiple lines  what was actually built or changed
  ImplementedOn     Date

  Result
  ActualHoursSavedPerYear Number
  ResultSummary     Multiple lines
  MeasuredOn        Date

Views
  Triage           : Status = New, sort SubmittedOn
  Prioritised      : Status = Approved, sort PriorityScore descending
  Quick wins       : Quadrant = Quick win AND Status = Under review or Approved
  In progress      : Status = In progress, group by Owner
  My ideas         : SubmittedBy = [Me]
  Delivered        : Status = Completed, totals on ActualHoursSavedPerYear, group by ProcessArea
  Awaiting measure : Status = Implemented or Measuring AND ImplementedOn <= [Today]-60

Automation
  New idea -> thank the submitter and tell them when triage happens
  Status change -> update the submitter (approved, declined with reason, completed)
  60 days after ImplementedOn -> ask the owner to record the measured result
stepByStepInstructions: Create the list with the problem, the proposed change and the process area.
Add sizing columns and a calculated estimate of hours saved per year.
Score value and effort and calculate a priority and quadrant.
Track status, owner, what was built and the measured result.
Keep submitters informed at each status change.
commonMistakes: Asking submitters for a full business case, which discourages ideas.
Prioritising by who asked.
Never measuring the result after delivery.
troubleshooting: If the calculated score shows an error, the choice columns hold text. VALUE converts them, so the choices must be plain numbers.
If view totals are missing on the calculated hours, set its return type to Number.
If submitters stop contributing, check they are being told the outcome, including why an idea was declined.
If estimates are inflated, compare estimated and actual hours on delivered items and feed that back into triage.

design-a-compliance-evidence-tracker.shortDescription: A SharePoint list design that maps controls to the evidence that proves them, with owners, collection frequency and review status.
design-a-compliance-evidence-tracker.fullDescription: Audits ask for evidence that each control operated. This tracker lists every control, what evidence shows it works, who provides it and how often, and whether the current period's evidence has been collected and reviewed.
design-a-compliance-evidence-tracker.problemStatement: Evidence is gathered in a scramble before each audit, from whoever can be found, and nobody knows which controls have no proof until the auditor asks.
whenToUse: ISO 27001, SOC 2, internal control or regulatory audits
Recurring evidence collection through the year
Small compliance teams without a GRC platform
whenNotToUse: Organisations with a GRC or compliance automation tool
Evidence that is too sensitive for a SharePoint site with broad membership
design-a-compliance-evidence-tracker.formulaOrCode:
List 1: Controls
  Title             Single line     control name                                     required
  ControlId         Single line     e.g. A.8.15 or AC-02                              unique, indexed
  Framework         Choice (multiple)   ISO 27001 | SOC 2 | Internal policy | GDPR
  ControlDescription Multiple lines
  ControlOwner      Person                                                          indexed
  Frequency         Choice          Continuous | Monthly | Quarterly | Annually | On event
  EvidenceRequired  Multiple lines  what proves the control operated
  Status            Choice          Implemented | Partly implemented | Planned | Not applicable

List 2: Evidence Tracker (one row per control per period)
  Title             Single line     "<ControlId> - <Period>"
  ControlId         Single line     matches Controls                                 required, indexed
  Period            Single line     2026-Q3, 2026-10 or 2026                          required, indexed
  EvidenceType      Choice          Report export | Screenshot | Ticket sample | Signed record | Meeting minutes |
                                    Configuration export | Log extract
  EvidenceDescription Multiple lines
  EvidenceOwner     Person          who provides it                                  required, indexed
  DueDate           Date                                                            indexed
  Status            Choice          Not started | Requested | Submitted | Accepted | Rejected | Overdue | Not applicable   indexed
  EvidenceLink      Hyperlink       file or folder in the evidence library
  CollectedOn       Date
  CoversFrom        Date            CoversTo  Date        (the period the evidence relates to)
  Reviewer          Person          ReviewedOn  Date
  ReviewNotes       Multiple lines
  RejectionReason   Single line
  AuditorRequested  Yes/No          AuditReference  Single line
  Finding           Choice          None | Observation | Minor nonconformity | Major nonconformity

Library: Compliance Evidence
  Folder per period, or metadata columns ControlId and Period. Restricted permissions.
  File naming: <ControlId>_<Period>_<short description>.pdf

Views (Evidence Tracker)
  Current period     : Period = current, group by Status
  Outstanding        : Status = Not started, Requested, Rejected or Overdue; sort DueDate
  My evidence        : EvidenceOwner = [Me] AND Status not Accepted
  To review          : Status = Submitted
  By control         : group by ControlId, sort Period descending       (history per control)
  Findings           : Finding <> None

Coverage check
  Controls with no accepted evidence this period: compare the two lists in Power BI or a Power App,
  or add a LastAcceptedPeriod column on Controls updated by a flow.

Automation
  Start of each period -> create an evidence row for every control due that period, from Frequency
  14 and 3 days before DueDate -> remind the evidence owner
  DueDate passed and not submitted -> Status = Overdue, notify the control owner
  Submitted -> notify the reviewer; Accepted -> update LastAcceptedPeriod on the control
stepByStepInstructions: Create a Controls list with an ID, owner, frequency and the evidence required.
Create an evidence tracker with one row per control per period.
Store evidence files in a restricted library and link each row to its file.
Generate the period's evidence rows automatically and remind owners before the due date.
Review submitted evidence, record acceptance or rejection, and check coverage before each audit.
commonMistakes: One row per control overwritten each period, which loses history.
Evidence files with no indication of the period they cover.
Collecting evidence only when the auditor asks.
troubleshooting: If rows are not created each period, check the flow's handling of each frequency value.
If auditors reject evidence, record the reason and tighten the EvidenceRequired description on the control.
If owners upload to the wrong place, give them a link from the row straight to the right folder.
If evidence contains personal data, restrict the library and keep only what is needed.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-overdue-app.shortDescription: Build a list view that shows approvals still pending past their due date, oldest first, grouped by approver.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-overdue-app.fullDescription: Approvals stall quietly. A view filtered to pending items whose due date has passed, or that have waited more than a set number of days, gives managers a single place to see what is stuck and with whom.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-overdue-app.problemStatement: Requests wait weeks for approval because nobody can see which ones are overdue or who is holding them.
whenToUse: Lists with an approval status and an approver column
Teams that chase approvals
Weekly review meetings
whenNotToUse: Approvals tracked only inside the Approvals app with no status on the list
Lists with no date to measure waiting time from
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-overdue-app.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  ApprovalStatus     Choice    Pending | Approved | Rejected                 indexed
  Approver           Person                                                 indexed
  SubmittedOn        Date      set when the approval starts                 indexed
  ApprovalDue        Date      SubmittedOn + agreed days (set by the flow)  indexed

View: Overdue approvals
  Filter : ApprovalStatus  is equal to      Pending
           AND
           ApprovalDue     is less than     [Today]
  Sort   : ApprovalDue ascending            (longest overdue first)
  Group  : Approver
  Columns: Title, Requester, Approver, SubmittedOn, ApprovalDue, DaysWaiting, Amount

No due date column? Filter on waiting time instead
  Filter : ApprovalStatus = Pending AND SubmittedOn is less than [Today]-5

Days waiting (column formatting on SubmittedOn; calculated columns cannot use today's date reliably)
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "txtContent": "=floor((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000) + ' days'",
  "style": { "color": "=if((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000 > 10, '#c4314b', '')" }
}

Personal version: "Waiting for me"
  Filter : ApprovalStatus = Pending AND Approver is equal to [Me]

Set ApprovalDue in the approval flow
  addDays(utcNow(), 5, 'yyyy-MM-dd')        or working days through a child flow

Use it
  Weekly digest flow: Get items with the same filter
    Filter Query: ApprovalStatus eq 'Pending' and ApprovalDue lt '@{utcNow('yyyy-MM-dd')}'
  then email each approver their list, copying their manager after 10 days.
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter on ApprovalStatus equals Pending and ApprovalDue less than [Today].
Sort by due date ascending and group by approver.
Format the submitted date to show days waiting.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: Filtering on Modified, which resets whenever anyone edits the item.
A calculated column using TODAY, which only recalculates when the item is edited.
Leaving out the status filter, so completed approvals appear as overdue.
troubleshooting: If the view is empty, check ApprovalDue is being filled by the flow.
If the view fails on a large list, make sure the indexed status filter is the first condition.
If days waiting shows NaN, the date column is empty for that row. Add an empty check to the formula.
If approvers are groups, the Waiting for me view will not match. [Me] matches individual users.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-unassigned-.shortDescription: Build a view that lists items with no owner, so a team lead can pick them up before they are forgotten.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-unassigned-.fullDescription: Unassigned work is invisible in views that group by owner. A dedicated view filtered to an empty assignee and an open status, sorted oldest first, makes triage a routine task.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-unassigned-.problemStatement: New items arrive with no owner and sit unnoticed, because everyone works from their own filtered view.
whenToUse: Shared queues where items are assigned after creation
Triage by a team lead or duty person
Lists with a person column for the assignee
whenNotToUse: Lists where a flow assigns every item on creation
Items owned by a team rather than a person, unless a team column exists
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-unassigned-.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  AssignedTo   Person (single)         indexed
  Status       Choice                  indexed
  Created      built in

View: Unassigned
  Filter : Status      is not equal to   Closed
           AND
           Status      is not equal to   Cancelled
           AND
           AssignedTo  is equal to       (leave the value box empty)
  Sort   : Created ascending
  Columns: Title, Category, Priority, Created By, Created, Status

  Leaving the value empty means "is blank" for person, lookup, date and text columns.

More reliable on large lists: a helper column
  IsAssigned   Yes/No   default No, indexed. A flow sets it to Yes when AssignedTo is filled.
  Filter : IsAssigned is equal to No AND Status is equal to New
  Equality on an indexed Yes/No column stays fast past 5,000 items; "is blank" on a person column may not.

Flow to maintain the helper (When an item is created or modified)
  Trigger condition:
    @not(equals(empty(triggerBody()?['AssignedTo']), not(triggerBody()?['IsAssigned'])))
  Update item: IsAssigned = @{not(empty(triggerBody()?['AssignedTo']))}

Highlight age (view formatting)
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/row-formatting.schema.json",
  "additionalRowClass": "=if((Number(@now) - Number([$Created])) / 86400000 > 2, 'sp-field-severity--warning', '')"
}

Assign quickly
  Use Edit in grid view to fill AssignedTo for several rows at once.
  Or select rows and use the details pane to set the same owner for all of them.

Alert
  Rule (Automate > Create a rule): "When a new item is created, send email to" the triage lead.
  Or a daily flow that posts the unassigned count to the team channel.
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter on an open status and AssignedTo equal to an empty value.
Sort by Created ascending so the oldest unassigned item is on top.
On large lists, add an indexed Yes/No helper column and filter on that.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: Sorting newest first, which hides the items that have waited longest.
Including closed items that were never assigned.
Using a multi-person column, which cannot be filtered for empty in the same way.
troubleshooting: If the empty filter returns nothing, confirm the value box is completely empty, with no space.
If the view breaks past 5,000 items, switch to the indexed helper column.
If items assigned to a group look unassigned to the team, add a separate team column.
If the helper column is out of step, check the flow's trigger condition and run it once over existing items.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-sponsor-dec.shortDescription: Build a view that shows a sponsor only the items waiting for their decision, with the facts needed to decide.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-sponsor-dec.fullDescription: Sponsors have little time. A view filtered to items awaiting a sponsor decision and to the current user, with the option, cost and deadline on one row, lets them decide without opening every item.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-sponsor-dec.problemStatement: Decisions wait on sponsors who would act quickly if they could see, in one place, exactly what needs deciding and by when.
whenToUse: Decision, change or risk lists where some items need sponsor sign-off
Sponsors who work from email links or Teams tabs
Steering group preparation
whenNotToUse: Decisions made only in meetings with a formal paper
Lists with no column identifying the decision maker
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-sponsor-dec.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  DecisionNeeded     Yes/No                                                   indexed
  DecisionStatus     Choice    Awaiting decision | Decided | Deferred | Withdrawn   indexed
  Sponsor            Person                                                   indexed
  DecisionBy         Date      when the decision is needed                     indexed
  Recommendation     Multiple lines (plain)    the team's recommended option
  ImpactIfDelayed    Single line
  CostImpact         Currency      ScheduleImpactDays  Number
  SponsorDecision    Choice    Approve | Reject | Request more information
  SponsorComment     Multiple lines

View: Decisions for me
  Filter : DecisionStatus  is equal to   Awaiting decision
           AND
           Sponsor         is equal to   [Me]
  Sort   : DecisionBy ascending
  Columns: Title, Recommendation, CostImpact, ScheduleImpactDays, ImpactIfDelayed, DecisionBy
  Style  : switch the view to the Gallery (card) layout if rows are text-heavy

View: All sponsor decisions (for the PMO)
  Filter : DecisionStatus = Awaiting decision
  Group  : Sponsor            Sort: DecisionBy ascending

Flag urgency (column formatting on DecisionBy)
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "attributes": { "class": "=if(@currentField < @now, 'sp-field-severity--blocked', if(@currentField < @now + 259200000, 'sp-field-severity--warning', ''))" },
  "txtContent": "=toLocaleDateString(@currentField)"
}

Let the sponsor decide from the view
  Edit in grid view, or select the row and set SponsorDecision and SponsorComment in the details pane.
  A flow on SponsorDecision changing sets DecisionStatus = Decided and records the date and person.

Deliver it
  Link in the weekly sponsor email:  .../Lists/Decisions/Decisions%20for%20me.aspx
  Teams: add the list as a tab in the steering group channel and choose this view.
  The same link works for every sponsor because [Me] resolves to whoever opens it.
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter on DecisionStatus equals Awaiting decision and Sponsor equals [Me].
Show the recommendation, cost and schedule impact and the decision deadline.
Sort by the decision deadline and highlight dates that are close or past.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: Sending sponsors to All Items and expecting them to filter.
Leaving out the recommendation, so each item has to be opened.
One view per sponsor, when [Me] makes a single view work for all.
troubleshooting: If a sponsor sees nothing, the Sponsor column holds a different account or a group.
If long text is cut off, use the gallery layout or widen the column.
If sponsors cannot edit, give them Contribute on the list or collect the decision through an approval flow.
If decided items remain, the flow that sets DecisionStatus is not running.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-blocked-pro.shortDescription: Build a view of projects marked as blocked, showing what is blocking each one, who must act and for how long.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-blocked-pro.fullDescription: A blocked project needs someone outside the team to act. This view lists blocked projects with the blocker, its owner and the date it was raised, so a portfolio meeting can go straight to what needs unblocking.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-blocked-pro.problemStatement: Projects report amber for weeks while waiting on the same unresolved dependency, and leadership only hears when the date is missed.
whenToUse: Project or portfolio lists with a status or health column
Regular portfolio or PMO reviews
Teams that escalate blockers
whenNotToUse: Task-level blockers, which belong in the project's own task list
Portfolios tracked in a project tool with its own reports
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-blocked-pro.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed (Projects list)
  ProjectStatus      Choice    Not started | On track | At risk | Blocked | On hold | Complete   indexed
  BlockedSince       Date      set when status changes to Blocked                indexed
  BlockerSummary     Single line    what is stopping progress
  BlockerType        Choice    Decision | Funding | Resource | Dependency | Supplier | Technical | Approval
  BlockerOwner       Person    who can remove it
  EscalatedTo        Person
  NextAction         Single line
  NextActionDate     Date
  ProjectManager     Person    Sponsor  Person

View: Blocked projects
  Filter : ProjectStatus is equal to Blocked
  Sort   : BlockedSince ascending
  Group  : BlockerType
  Columns: Title, ProjectManager, BlockerSummary, BlockerOwner, BlockedSince, NextAction, NextActionDate

Days blocked (column formatting on BlockedSince)
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "txtContent": "=if(@currentField == '', '', floor((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000) + ' days blocked')",
  "attributes": { "class": "=if((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000 > 14, 'sp-field-severity--blocked', 'sp-field-severity--warning')" }
}

Related views
  Blockers I own        : ProjectStatus = Blocked AND BlockerOwner = [Me]
  Blocked over 14 days  : ProjectStatus = Blocked AND BlockedSince < [Today]-14
  No next action        : ProjectStatus = Blocked AND NextActionDate is empty

Make the data reliable
  List validation: a blocked project must say why
    =IF([ProjectStatus]="Blocked", NOT(ISBLANK([BlockerSummary])), TRUE)
  Flow: when ProjectStatus changes to Blocked, set BlockedSince = today and notify the BlockerOwner.
        When it changes away from Blocked, clear BlockedSince and log the days blocked to a history list.

Meeting use
  Open the view grouped by BlockerType. Decisions and approvals can usually be cleared in the meeting.
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter on ProjectStatus equals Blocked.
Show the blocker, its owner, the date it was raised and the next action.
Sort by BlockedSince ascending and group by blocker type.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: A Blocked status with no explanation of the blocker.
No date, so nobody can tell a new blocker from an old one.
Treating On hold and Blocked as the same thing.
troubleshooting: If BlockedSince is empty, the flow that stamps it is not running. Backfill from version history.
If project managers avoid the Blocked status, make clear it triggers help, and review it in the portfolio meeting.
If validation stops unrelated edits, test the formula returns TRUE for every other status.
If the grouping shows a blank group, some items have no blocker type. Make it required when blocked.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-aging-reque.shortDescription: Build views that show how long open requests have been waiting, in age bands, so the oldest get attention first.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-aging-reque.fullDescription: Age is the simplest signal of a neglected request. Because SharePoint views cannot calculate today's date in a column reliably, this pattern uses date filters for age bands and column formatting to show the age in days.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-aging-reque.problemStatement: The queue looks healthy by count, while a handful of requests have been open for months.
whenToUse: Request, ticket and case lists
Teams with turnaround targets
Weekly queue reviews
whenNotToUse: Lists where age is measured from a date other than creation and that date is not stored
Reporting on closed items, which suits Power BI
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-aging-reque.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  Status     Choice     indexed
  Created    built in   (or SubmittedOn if drafts are possible)

Age-band views (date filters use [Today] and are evaluated each time the view loads)
  Open 0-7 days
    Status <> Closed AND Created >= [Today]-7
  Open 8-30 days
    Status <> Closed AND Created < [Today]-7 AND Created >= [Today]-30
  Open over 30 days
    Status <> Closed AND Created < [Today]-30
  Each: sort Created ascending.

One view, all ages
  Filter : Status is not equal to Closed
  Sort   : Created ascending
  with the age shown and coloured by column formatting on Created:

{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "style": { "padding": "2px 8px", "border-radius": "10px", "display": "inline-block" },
  "attributes": {
    "class": "=if((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000 > 30, 'sp-field-severity--blocked', if((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000 > 7, 'sp-field-severity--warning', 'sp-field-severity--good'))"
  },
  "txtContent": "=floor((Number(@now) - Number(@currentField)) / 86400000) + ' d'"
}

Why not a calculated column?
  =TODAY()-[Created] is only recalculated when the item is edited, so the age freezes.

Need a real number to sort, group or chart on?
  Add AgeDays (Number) and AgeBand (Choice) and update them nightly with a flow:
    Get items: Status ne 'Closed'
    Update item: AgeDays = div(sub(ticks(utcNow()), ticks(item()?['Created'])), 864000000000)
                 AgeBand = if(greater(AgeDays, 30), 'Over 30', if(greater(AgeDays, 7), '8-30', '0-7'))
  Add a trigger condition to other flows so this nightly update does not set them off.
  Then: group by AgeBand, or show the count per band with view totals.

Age since last activity
  Use Modified in place of Created to find requests nobody has touched:
    Status <> Closed AND Modified < [Today]-14
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter on an open status and a Created date older than [Today] minus the number of days.
Create one view per age band, or one view with the age shown by column formatting.
Sort by Created ascending so the oldest request is first.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: A calculated column with TODAY, which goes stale.
Measuring from Modified when you mean time since submission.
Counting drafts in the age.
troubleshooting: If [Today]-30 is rejected, type it with no spaces: [Today]-30.
If the view fails on a large list, put the indexed status condition first.
If ages are a day out, time zones differ between the site and the user. For day counts that is usually acceptable.
If a nightly update triggers other flows, add a trigger condition to those flows that ignores changes to the age columns.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-archived-re.shortDescription: Keep archived items out of everyday views and reachable through a dedicated, fast archive view.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-archived-re.fullDescription: Archiving in place means flagging items instead of moving them. Working views exclude the flag, and an archive view shows only flagged items, filtered by year so it stays within list limits.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-archived-re.problemStatement: Closed records from years ago clutter every view and slow the list, but they must stay available for reference and audit.
whenToUse: Lists that keep completed records for reference
Lists heading past 5,000 items
Teams that occasionally look things up in history
whenNotToUse: Records that must be moved for retention or legal reasons, which need retention labels or a records library
Lists small enough not to need it
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-archived-re.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  IsArchived     Yes/No    default No                    indexed
  ArchivedOn     Date                                    indexed
  ArchiveYear    Number or Single line  e.g. 2025        indexed
  ArchivedBy     Single line (email)

Working views (every one of them)
  Filter : IsArchived is equal to No   (as the first condition)

View: Archive
  Filter : IsArchived   is equal to   Yes
           AND
           ArchiveYear  is equal to   2026           (one view per year, or change the value)
  Sort   : ArchivedOn descending
  Columns: Title, Status, Closed date, Owner, ArchivedOn
  Row limit: 100 per page (the default 30 is slow to page through)

View: Recently archived
  Filter : IsArchived = Yes AND ArchivedOn >= [Today]-30

Find one record without a view
  The list search box searches all items, including archived ones.
  Filter by URL: ...AllItems.aspx?FilterField1=RequestNumber&FilterValue1=REQ-00123

Archive automatically (scheduled flow, weekly)
  Get items
    Filter Query : IsArchived eq 0 and Status eq 'Closed' and ClosedOn lt '@{addDays(utcNow(), -180, 'yyyy-MM-dd')}'
    Top Count    : 500
  Apply to each
    Update item: IsArchived = Yes, ArchivedOn = utcNow(), ArchiveYear = formatDateTime(item()?['ClosedOn'], 'yyyy')

Make archived items read-only (optional)
  In the same loop: stop inheriting permissions and grant Read (Send an HTTP request to SharePoint,
  breakroleinheritance). Use sparingly. Thousands of unique permissions slow a list.

Restore
  Edit the item and set IsArchived to No, or filter the Archive view and use grid edit for several.

When to move instead of flag
  Past roughly 100,000 items, or when different retention applies, move archived rows to a separate
  archive list or export them, and delete them from the working list.
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Add IsArchived, ArchivedOn and ArchiveYear columns and index them.
Add IsArchived equals No as the first filter on every working view.
Create an Archive view filtered to IsArchived equals Yes and a single year.
Set the flag automatically with a scheduled flow for items closed more than a set time ago.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: An archive view with no year filter, which fails once the archive passes 5,000 items.
Forgetting to exclude archived items from apps and flows as well as views.
Breaking permissions on every archived item.
troubleshooting: If the archive view shows a threshold error, add or tighten the year filter, with indexed columns.
If archived items still appear in an app, add IsArchived = false to its Filter.
If the flow stops partway, it hit the item limit per run. Let it run again, or page through with a Do until.
If ArchiveYear is empty on older rows, backfill it once from the closed date.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-upcoming-mi.shortDescription: Build a view of milestones due in the next few weeks, in date order, with late ones flagged.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-upcoming-mi.fullDescription: A rolling window on the due date turns a long milestone list into a short look-ahead. Views can compare a date to [Today] plus or minus days, so the window moves by itself each day.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-upcoming-mi.problemStatement: Milestones are in a plan nobody opens, so the team is surprised by dates that were visible weeks ago.
whenToUse: Project milestone, deliverable or deadline lists
Weekly look-ahead meetings
A milestone web part on a project home page
whenNotToUse: Detailed task scheduling with dependencies
Milestones kept only in a project tool
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-upcoming-mi.formulaOrCode:
Columns needed
  MilestoneDate    Date                                              indexed
  Status           Choice    Not started | In progress | Complete | Missed | Cancelled   indexed
  Project          Single line or lookup
  Owner            Person
  Confidence       Choice    High | Medium | Low
  BaselineDate     Date      the originally agreed date

View: Next 30 days
  Filter : Status         is not equal to            Complete
           AND
           Status         is not equal to            Cancelled
           AND
           MilestoneDate  is less than or equal to   [Today]+30
  Sort   : MilestoneDate ascending
  Columns: MilestoneDate, Title, Project, Owner, Status, Confidence

  This includes anything already late. To show only future dates add:
           AND MilestoneDate is greater than or equal to [Today]

View: Late milestones
  Filter : Status <> Complete AND Status <> Cancelled AND MilestoneDate < [Today]

View: This week
  Filter : MilestoneDate >= [Today] AND MilestoneDate <= [Today]+7

Calendar view
  Create view > Calendar, with MilestoneDate as both the start and end date.

Format the date (column formatting on MilestoneDate)
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "attributes": {
    "class": "=if([$Status] == 'Complete', 'sp-field-severity--good', if(@currentField < @now, 'sp-field-severity--blocked', if(@currentField < @now + 604800000, 'sp-field-severity--warning', '')))"
  },
  "txtContent": "=toLocaleDateString(@currentField) + if([$Status] != 'Complete' && @currentField < @now, ' (late)', '')"
}

Show slippage against the baseline (calculated column, both dates are stored so it stays correct)
  SlipDays = IF(ISBLANK([BaselineDate]), 0, [MilestoneDate]-[BaselineDate])        (return type: Number)

On the project home page
  Add the List web part, choose this list and the "Next 30 days" view, and hide the command bar.

Reminder flow (daily)
  Filter Query: Status ne 'Complete' and MilestoneDate eq '@{addDays(utcNow(), 7, 'yyyy-MM-dd')}'
  Email the owner: "<Title> is due in 7 days."
stepByStepInstructions: Check the columns the filter needs exist, and add an index to each one used in the filter.
Create a new view from All Items and give it a name that says what it shows.
Filter out complete and cancelled milestones, then add MilestoneDate less than or equal to [Today]+30.
Sort by MilestoneDate ascending.
Format the date column so late and near-term milestones stand out.
Add the view to the project home page with the List web part.
Share the view's URL, or pin it as a tab in the team's Teams channel.
commonMistakes: Hiding late milestones by filtering to future dates only.
Overwriting the milestone date with no baseline, so slippage is invisible.
A window so wide the view becomes the whole plan.
troubleshooting: If the filter rejects [Today]+30, remove any spaces around the plus sign.
If completed milestones show as late, add the status conditions.
If the calendar view shows nothing, the date column must be chosen for both begin and end.
If the web part shows the wrong view, edit the web part and select the view by name.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-external-gu.shortDescription: Build a view that shows which items or documents are shared with external guests, so owners can review and remove access.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-external-gu.fullDescription: SharePoint does not offer a view filter for shared externally. This pattern records external sharing in columns, either through a controlled sharing process or a scheduled check, and builds the review view on those columns alongside the built-in sharing report.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-external-gu.problemStatement: Files are shared with clients and suppliers during a project and stay shared for years, because nobody can see a list of what is exposed.
whenToUse: Libraries and lists on sites that allow external sharing
Periodic guest access reviews
Client or supplier collaboration sites
whenNotToUse: Sites where external sharing is turned off
Tenant-wide guest reviews, which use Microsoft Entra access reviews
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-external-gu.formulaOrCode:
First, the built-in report (no setup)
  Site > Settings (gear) > Site usage > "Shared with external users" > Run report
  Saves a CSV listing each item, who it is shared with and the permission. Use it as the baseline.

Columns to add to the library or list
  SharedExternally   Yes/No                                      indexed
  SharedWith         Multiple lines   guest emails or organisation
  ShareReason        Single line
  ShareApprovedBy    Person
  SharedOn           Date
  ShareReviewDate    Date     when access must be re-confirmed    indexed
  ShareStatus        Choice   Active | To remove | Removed         indexed

View: External sharing review
  Filter : SharedExternally is equal to Yes
           AND
           ShareStatus      is equal to Active
  Sort   : ShareReviewDate ascending
  Columns: Name, SharedWith, ShareReason, ShareApprovedBy, SharedOn, ShareReviewDate, Modified

View: Review overdue
  Filter : SharedExternally = Yes AND ShareStatus = Active AND ShareReviewDate < [Today]

View: Guest contributions (what guests have changed)
  Filter : Modified By contains #EXT#       (guest accounts carry #EXT# in their sign-in name)
           If the filter is not accepted on your tenant, group the view by Modified By instead.

Keep the columns accurate
  Option A, controlled sharing: users request sharing through a form or flow, which grants access
           (Grant access to an item or a folder) and fills the columns.
  Option B, scheduled check: a weekly flow reads each item's sharing information and updates the flag:
           Send an HTTP request to SharePoint
             POST _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Documents')/items(<ID>)/GetSharingInformation?$expand=permissionsInformation
           Set SharedExternally when any principal or link is external.
           Suits libraries of modest size; it makes one call per item.

Review routine (quarterly)
  1. Owner opens "External sharing review".
  2. For each row: still needed? If not, Manage access > Stop sharing, then ShareStatus = Removed.
  3. If needed: move ShareReviewDate on by 3 or 6 months.

Reduce the need to review
  Set guest link expiry and guest access expiration in the SharePoint admin center sharing settings.
  Share a dedicated folder or site with guests instead of individual files.
stepByStepInstructions: Run the site's built-in sharing report to see what is shared now.
Add sharing columns: a Yes/No flag, who it is shared with, the reason, approver and a review date.
Keep the columns current through a controlled sharing flow or a scheduled check.
Create a review view filtered to SharedExternally equals Yes and Active status, sorted by review date.
Review each quarter, stop sharing where it is no longer needed and move the review date on for the rest.
commonMistakes: Assuming a view can filter on sharing without any supporting column.
Reviewing guest accounts but not sharing links.
No expiry on guest links.
troubleshooting: If the flag is wrong, sharing was done outside the controlled process. Run the scheduled check or reconcile with the sharing report.
If the sharing report option is missing, you need to be a site owner.
If stopping sharing does not remove a guest's access, they may also be a member of the site or a group.
If the per-item check is slow, limit it to items modified recently or to specific folders.

create-a-sharepoint-view-for-missing-met.shortDescription: Build a view that finds items and documents with required information left empty, so owners can complete them.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-missing-met.fullDescription: Columns added later, bulk uploads and migrated content all leave gaps. A view filtered to empty key columns, opened in grid edit, turns clean-up into a quick routine, and a completeness flag makes it measurable.
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-missing-met.problemStatement: Views and reports that rely on metadata miss half the content because key columns were never filled in.
whenToUse: Document libraries after migration or bulk upload
Lists where columns were added after items existed
Preparing content for search, retention or reporting
whenNotToUse: Lists where every key column is already enforced as required
Optional columns that are legitimately empty
create-a-sharepoint-view-for-missing-met.formulaOrCode:
Decide the key columns, for example: DocumentType, Department, Owner, ReviewDate

View: Missing metadata
  Filter : DocumentType  is equal to  (empty)
           OR
           Department    is equal to  (empty)
           OR
           Owner         is equal to  (empty)
  Sort   : Modified descending
  Columns: Name, DocumentType, Department, Owner, Modified By, Modified
  Leave the value box blank to test for empty.

  An OR filter cannot use indexes, so this works on lists under 5,000 items.
  On larger lists use one view per column:
    Missing document type : DocumentType is equal to (empty)       (indexed)
    Missing owner         : Owner is equal to (empty)              (indexed)
  or the completeness flag below.

Built-in help for libraries
  Files uploaded without required properties appear in the "Files that need attention" view,
  and show a "Required info" marker in the column.

Fix quickly
  Open the view > Edit in grid view > fill down a column like a spreadsheet.
  Or select several files > details pane > "Bulk edit properties".

Completeness flag for large lists and reporting
  MetadataComplete  Yes/No   indexed, default No
  Flow (When an item or file is created or modified), trigger condition to avoid loops:
    @not(equals(triggerBody()?['MetadataComplete'],
         and(not(empty(triggerBody()?['DocumentType'])), not(empty(triggerBody()?['Department'])), not(empty(triggerBody()?['Owner'])))))
  Update: MetadataComplete = and(not(empty(...DocumentType)), not(empty(...Department)), not(empty(...Owner)))
  View filter: MetadataComplete is equal to No

Highlight gaps in any view (column formatting)
{
