        @{n="SecurityGroup";e={$_.Internal.properties.linkedEnvironmentMetadata.securityGroupId}} |
      Export-Csv environments.csv -NoTypeInformation

  Counts per environment
    Get-AdminPowerApp -EnvironmentName <id> | Measure-Object
    Get-AdminFlow     -EnvironmentName <id> | Measure-Object

  Power Automate (weekly)
    Power Platform for Admins > List Environments as Admin
    For each: create or update the row in the inventory list by Environment ID.

  Capacity: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Capacity add-ons / Dataverse > download report.

Fields people must fill in
  Purpose, owners, sensitivity and review decision. Send each new environment's creator a short form.

Views
  No owner              Business owner is empty
  Review due            Next review <= today + 30
  Non-production with no activity   Stage <> Prod and no app launches or flow runs in 90 days
  Trials and developer environments older than 60 days

Review cadence
  Production: yearly.  Sandbox and developer: every six months.  Trial: at 30 days.
  Decision each time: keep, change owner, or delete. Deleted environments can be recovered for 7 days.

Naming convention for new environments
  <Business area> - <Solution or purpose> - <Stage>         Finance - Invoicing - Test
stepByStepInstructions: Export the environment list with PowerShell or the admin connector.
Load it into a SharePoint list or Dataverse table keyed on Environment ID.
Ask each creator or admin for the purpose and owners.
Add DLP policy, security group and sensitivity.
Create the views and schedule the refresh flow.
Run the first review and delete or reassign what nobody claims.
commonMistakes: Recording technical facts only, with no owner or purpose.
Keying the list on display name, which can change.
Never reviewing developer and trial environments.
Deleting environments without contacting the creator or checking for active flows.
troubleshooting: If the PowerShell list is empty, sign in with an account that has the Power Platform administrator role.
If the URL is blank, the environment has no Dataverse database.
If an environment has no creator, it was created by the system (for example the default or a Teams environment).
If an environment was deleted by mistake, recover it from the admin center within seven days.

faqs.question: How do I list all Power Platform environments?
faqs.answer: Use Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment in PowerShell, the List Environments as Admin action in Power Automate, or export the list from the Power Platform admin center.

faqs.question: What should an environment inventory record?
faqs.answer: The environment's ID, type, purpose, owners, region, security group, DLP policy, data sensitivity, storage use and review dates.

faqs.question: How often should environments be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Production yearly, sandbox and developer environments every six months, and trials before they expire.

create-a-connector-review-process.shortDescription: A repeatable way to decide whether a connector, including a custom one, may be used with business data, and to record the decision in DLP policy.
create-a-connector-review-process.fullDescription: Power Platform offers over a thousand connectors, and makers can add custom ones. A connector review gives each request the same questions: what data moves where, who publishes the connector, how it authenticates and what it costs. The answer becomes a DLP classification and an entry in a register.
create-a-connector-review-process.problemStatement: Connector requests are approved or refused by whoever answers the email, with no record, and blocked connectors are unblocked for one person's convenience.
whenToUse: Makers ask for a connector that DLP blocks
A new custom connector is proposed
Annual review of the allowed connector list
whenNotToUse: Connectors already classified as business in the policy that covers the environment
Personal developer environments covered by a policy that already blocks business data
create-a-connector-review-process.formulaOrCode:
Request form
  Connector name and publisher
  Standard, premium or custom
  Environment(s) where it is needed
  Business purpose and owner
  Data sent to it (types, sensitivity, volume)
  Data read from it
  Other connectors it will be combined with
  Authentication method (OAuth, API key, basic, none)
  Requested by, date needed

Review questions
  1. Publisher: Microsoft, a verified publisher, independent publisher, or internal?
  2. Where does the data go? Which service and region, and is there a contract with that provider?
  3. Does the service meet the classification of the data (personal, financial, confidential)?
  4. Authentication: per-user OAuth is preferred. Shared keys must be stored in Key Vault.
  5. Can endpoints be restricted? (DLP endpoint filtering for HTTP, SQL, Dataverse, custom connectors)
  6. Can risky actions be blocked? (DLP connector action control)
  7. Licence impact: premium connectors need premium licences for every user of the app or flow.
  8. Is there an approved connector that already does the job?
  9. Who supports it if it breaks?

Outcomes
  Business       allowed with business data in the named environments
  Non-business   allowed, but cannot be combined with business connectors
  Blocked        not allowed
  Business with conditions   for example only specific endpoints, only in one environment,
                              only read actions

Record the decision (register)
  Connector | Publisher | Tier | Decision | Conditions | Environments | Reviewed by | Date | Next review

Apply it
  Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policies > edit policy
    Connectors: move the connector to Business, Non-business or Blocked
    Configure connector > Connector actions: allow or block individual actions
    Configure connector > Connector endpoints: allow or deny URL patterns, in order
  Set the default group for new connectors to Non-business or Blocked so newly released
  connectors are not allowed automatically.

Custom connectors
  DLP > Custom connectors: classify by URL pattern, for example  https://api.contoso.com/*  -> Business
  and  *  -> Blocked for everything else.
  Review the OpenAPI definition: host, authentication, which operations exist.

Service levels
  Standard Microsoft connector: answer within 3 working days.
  Premium, third-party or custom: within 10 working days, with security input.

Yearly review
  Export the policy's connector list, compare with the register, and re-confirm each exception's owner.
stepByStepInstructions: Publish the request form where makers can find it.
For each request, answer the review questions with the requester and security.
Choose an outcome and any conditions.
Record it in the register.
Update the DLP policy, using action and endpoint controls where they reduce risk.
Tell the requester the outcome and the reason.
Re-review exceptions each year.
commonMistakes: Leaving the default group for new connectors as Business.
Approving HTTP and custom connectors without endpoint filtering.
Granting an exception with no owner or end date.
Ignoring the licence cost of premium connectors.
troubleshooting: If a flow is suspended after a policy change, it combines connectors from different groups. Change the flow or the classification, then turn it on.
If a connector cannot be blocked, it is one of the few non-blockable Microsoft connectors, such as Dataverse or Approvals.
If an endpoint rule seems ignored, rules are evaluated in order. Put specific allow rules above the final deny-all rule.
If makers do not know why something is blocked, set a custom governance error message with a link to the request form.

faqs.question: How do I allow a blocked connector in Power Platform?
faqs.answer: Edit the data policy that covers the environment and move the connector to the Business or Non-business group. Do it after a review that records why.

faqs.question: Can I allow only part of a connector?
faqs.answer: Yes. Connector action control blocks specific actions, and endpoint filtering limits which addresses connectors such as HTTP and SQL Server can reach.

faqs.question: How are custom connectors controlled by DLP?
faqs.answer: By URL pattern. A policy can classify custom connectors whose host matches a pattern as business, non-business or blocked.

create-a-maker-activity-review.shortDescription: A monthly review of who is building what: new makers, new apps and flows, connectors in use, sharing and inactive resources.
create-a-maker-activity-review.fullDescription: Maker activity is the earliest signal of both value and risk. A short monthly review of new makers, new and widely shared apps, premium connector use and stale resources lets the platform team welcome and guide people early, and spot problems before they become incidents.
create-a-maker-activity-review.problemStatement: The platform team learns about a business-critical app shared with 400 people only when it breaks, because nobody was watching what makers were building.
whenToUse: Tenants where makers build in the default or shared environments
Running a centre of excellence or adoption programme
Before licence renewals
whenNotToUse: Tightly locked-down tenants where only a central team can build
Tenants with very few makers, where a quarterly look at the inventory is enough
create-a-maker-activity-review.formulaOrCode:
Monthly review agenda (30 minutes)

1. New makers this month
   Who made their first app or flow, in which environment.
   Action: send the welcome message with training, guidelines and the support channel.

2. New apps and flows
   Name, owner, environment, connectors, created date.
   Flags: premium or custom connectors, HTTP actions, built in the default environment.

3. Widely shared resources
   Apps shared with more than 20 users, with a group, or with Everyone.
   Action: confirm an owner and backup, move to a managed solution and proper environment if critical.

4. Usage
   Top apps by sessions and users. Apps with no launches in 90 days.
   Flows with a high failure rate, and flows that have not run in 90 days.

5. Risk
   Resources owned by disabled or departed users (orphans).
   Flows suspended by DLP. Connections in an error state.

6. Capacity and licences
   Environments near storage limits. Premium use without matching licences.

7. Actions and owners for next month

Where the data comes from
  Power Platform admin center
    Manage > Power Apps / Power Automate inventory (tenant-wide lists with owner, environment, last modified)
    Analytics > Power Apps: usage, sessions, locations.  Analytics > Power Automate: runs, errors.
  Managed Environments: weekly usage insights email to admins.
  CoE Starter Kit: Power BI dashboard with makers, apps, flows, connectors and compliance pages.
  PowerShell
    Get-AdminPowerApp | Select DisplayName, @{n="Owner";e={$_.Owner.displayName}}, EnvironmentName, CreatedTime, LastModifiedTime
    Get-AdminFlow     | Select DisplayName, @{n="CreatedBy";e={$_.CreatedBy.userId}}, EnvironmentName, Enabled, CreatedTime
    New this month:  ... | Where-Object { $_.CreatedTime -gt (Get-Date).AddDays(-30) }
  Sharing
    Get-AdminPowerAppRoleAssignment -AppName <app id> -EnvironmentName <env>
  Audit log (Microsoft Purview): activities such as Created app, Published app, Edited app permission,
    Created flow, Deleted app. Useful for who did what and when.

Thresholds that trigger a conversation with the maker
  Shared with more than 20 users        -> ownership and support check
  Uses premium connector                 -> licence check
  Uses HTTP or custom connector          -> connector review
  More than 100 sessions a month         -> offer ALM help
  No use in 90 days                      -> ask to archive or delete

Welcome message contents
  Where to build, naming rules, how to ask for connectors, training links, community channel.
stepByStepInstructions: Choose the data source: admin center inventory, CoE Starter Kit or PowerShell exports.
Build one saved report for each agenda item.
Hold the review monthly with the platform owner and a security contact.
Contact new makers with the welcome message.
Follow up on each threshold breach with the resource's owner.
Record actions and check them at the next review.
commonMistakes: Treating the review as policing, which pushes makers to hide work.
Looking only at counts, not at sharing and connectors.
No follow-up on orphaned resources.
Reviewing so rarely that critical apps appear fully formed.
troubleshooting: If the inventory misses an environment, the reporting account is not an admin of it or the data has not refreshed yet.
If last-used dates are blank, usage analytics keep a limited history. Use the CoE kit or audit log for longer periods.
If audit log searches return nothing, auditing may not be enabled for the tenant or the activity is older than the retention period.
If makers ignore emails, post in the maker community channel and involve their manager only for risk items.

faqs.question: How can I see who is building apps in my tenant?
faqs.answer: Use the Power Apps and Power Automate inventory in the Power Platform admin center, the CoE Starter Kit dashboard, or Get-AdminPowerApp and Get-AdminFlow in PowerShell.

faqs.question: What should I look for in a maker activity review?
faqs.answer: New makers, new and widely shared apps, premium and custom connector use, failing flows, orphaned resources and anything unused for 90 days.

faqs.question: How do I find out who an app is shared with?
faqs.answer: Open the app's Share panel, or run Get-AdminPowerAppRoleAssignment for the app in PowerShell.

create-a-premium-connector-exception-reg.shortDescription: Track every approved use of premium connectors and features, who pays for the licences, and when each exception is reviewed.
create-a-premium-connector-exception-reg.fullDescription: Premium connectors, Dataverse, custom connectors and on-premises gateways all need premium licences for the people who use the app or flow. A register of approved premium uses links each one to a business case, a licence type and a count, so costs are expected and compliance questions have an answer.
create-a-premium-connector-exception-reg.problemStatement: A maker adds a SQL Server connection to a popular app, and 300 users see a licence prompt the next morning.
whenToUse: Tenants where most users have Microsoft 365 licences only
Before sharing an app that uses a premium connector
Annual licence true-up
whenNotToUse: Organisations where every user already holds Power Apps Premium and Power Automate Premium
Developer environments, where makers can build with premium features under the developer plan
create-a-premium-connector-exception-reg.formulaOrCode:
What makes an app or flow premium
  Premium connectors (SQL Server, Dataverse, HTTP, Azure services, Salesforce and others)
  Custom connectors
  On-premises data gateway
  Dataverse tables (outside Dataverse for Teams)
  AI Builder, Power Pages, RPA (attended and unattended) each have their own licensing

Licence options (confirm current terms in the Microsoft licensing guide)
  Power Apps Premium            per user, unlimited apps
  Power Apps per app            per user, per app (or portal) in one environment
  Pay-as-you-go                 per active user per app per month, billed through Azure
  Power Automate Premium        per user: premium cloud flows and attended RPA
  Power Automate Process        per flow or bot: for flows that serve many people or run unattended
  Flows that run in the context of a licensed premium app are covered by the app's licence.

Register
  Resource              Type   Environment   Premium element       Users   Licence model         Cost owner      Approved by   Approved on   Review on
  Invoice Lookup        App    Finance Prod  SQL Server            45      Power Apps per app    Finance         Platform lead 2026-03-02    2027-03-02
  Supplier Sync         Flow   Finance Prod  HTTP, Dataverse       n/a     Power Automate Process Finance        Platform lead 2026-05-11    2027-05-11
  Site Inspections      App    Ops Prod      Dataverse             120     Pay-as-you-go         Operations      Ops director  2026-08-20    2027-02-20

Request questions
  What does the premium element give that a standard connector cannot?
  How many people will use it, and how often?
  Which licence model is cheapest for that pattern? (few apps, many users -> per app or pay-as-you-go;
  many apps per user -> Premium)
  Who pays, and from which budget?
  Is there a standard alternative (SharePoint, Excel, Outlook) that would meet the need?

Find premium use
  Power Platform admin center > Licensing: licence consumption and pay-as-you-go reports.
  Power Apps inventory: filter or export; the app's Details page shows "License designation: Premium".
  PowerShell
    Get-AdminPowerApp | ForEach-Object {
      [pscustomobject]@{
        App = $_.DisplayName; Environment = $_.EnvironmentName
        Connectors = ($_.Internal.properties.connectionReferences.PSObject.Properties.Value.displayName -join "; ")
      } }
  CoE Starter Kit: connector reference table marks each connector's tier.

Controls
  DLP: block premium connectors in the default environment; allow them in governed environments.
  Per-app licences: allocate capacity to the environment (admin center > Capacity > add-ons) and
  turn on "Auto assign per app passes" on the app.
  Pay-as-you-go: link the environment to an Azure subscription through a billing policy.

Review
  At each review date: is the app still used, has the user count changed, is the licence model
  still the cheapest, does the cost owner still agree?
stepByStepInstructions: Identify existing premium apps and flows from the admin center or PowerShell.
Create the register and add each with its users and licence model.
Publish a short request form for new premium use.
Agree a cost owner for every entry.
Apply DLP so premium connectors are only available in governed environments.
Review each entry on its date and at licence renewal.
commonMistakes: Sharing a premium app widely before licences are in place.
Assuming a flow is covered because the maker has a licence, when it serves many other users.
Buying per-user licences where per-app or pay-as-you-go would cost less.
No cost owner, so the platform team's budget absorbs everything.
troubleshooting: If users see a licence prompt or trial offer, the app became premium. Check its connections and assign per-app passes or licences.
If per-app passes are not consumed, capacity has not been allocated to that environment.
If a flow shows as out of compliance, its owner lacks the needed licence or it needs a Process licence.
If pay-as-you-go charges are higher than expected, check active users per app in the Azure cost report and consider per-user licences.

faqs.question: What makes a Power App premium?
faqs.answer: Using a premium or custom connector, Dataverse, or the on-premises gateway. Every user of that app then needs a premium licence.

faqs.question: Which licence is cheapest for a premium app?
faqs.answer: For one or two apps used by many people, per-app or pay-as-you-go usually costs less. For people who use several premium apps, Power Apps Premium per user is simpler and often cheaper.

faqs.question: How do I find which apps use premium connectors?
faqs.answer: Check the licence designation on each app's details page, export the app inventory from the admin center, or use the CoE Starter Kit's connector reports.

create-a-tenant-settings-review.shortDescription: Review the tenant-level Power Platform settings that decide who can create environments, trials and shared resources, with recommended values.
create-a-tenant-settings-review.fullDescription: A small set of tenant settings shapes everything else: who can create environments, whether users can start trials, how widely apps can be shared and what insights are collected. Many are permissive by default. A settings review once or twice a year records each value, the reason for it and who approved it.
create-a-tenant-settings-review.problemStatement: Any user can create a production environment or sign up for a trial, and the tenant slowly fills with unmanaged environments and expired trials.
whenToUse: Setting up governance in a new or inherited tenant
After Microsoft adds new tenant settings
Annual security review
whenNotToUse: When you are not a Power Platform or Global administrator and cannot see or change these settings
Environment-level settings such as auditing and features, which need a separate per-environment review
create-a-tenant-settings-review.formulaOrCode:
Power Platform admin center > Settings (tenant settings)

Environment creation
  Setting                                         Typical recommendation
  Developer environment assignments               Everyone (low risk, isolates personal work), or specific admins
  Production environment assignments              Only specific admins
  Trial environment assignments                   Only specific admins
  Add-on capacity assignments                     Only specific admins
  Environment routing                             On: new makers land in their own developer environment
                                                  instead of the default environment

Sharing and makers
  Sharing with Everyone                           Off (PowerShell: disableShareWithEveryone)
  Managed Environments > Limit sharing            Exclude sharing with security groups, or cap the number of users
  Canvas app insights / Analytics                 On
  Weekly digest (Managed Environments)            On, sent to the admin group

Features
  Copilot and AI features                         Decide per environment group; record data-movement choices
  Publish bots / agents with AI features          By policy
  Power Platform customer lockbox                 On where required by compliance
  Auto-claim policies for licences                Configure if using per-user licences

Self-service
  Self-service trials and purchases (Microsoft 365 admin, MSCommerce PowerShell)
    Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <id> -Enabled $false
  Internal trials through "AllowAdHocSubscriptions" (Entra ID) decide whether users can sign up themselves.

Security
  Tenant isolation                                On, with an allow list of partner tenants
  Data policies                                   A tenant-wide baseline policy exists and covers all environments
  Customer-managed key                            Where required
  IP firewall / IP cookie binding (Managed Environments)   For sensitive environments
  Guest access                                    Decide whether guests can make or only use

Default environment
  Rename it ("Personal productivity"), apply the strictest DLP policy, and tell makers what belongs in it.
  It cannot be deleted or restricted by a security group.

Read and change settings with PowerShell
  $s = Get-TenantSettings
  $s.disableEnvironmentCreationByNonAdminUsers
  $s.disableTrialEnvironmentCreationByNonAdminUsers
  $s.powerPlatform.powerApps.disableShareWithEveryone
  $s.disableEnvironmentCreationByNonAdminUsers = $true
  Set-TenantSettings -RequestBody $s

Review record
  Setting | Current value | Recommended | Decision | Reason | Approved by | Date
  Keep it with the security documentation and repeat every six to twelve months.
stepByStepInstructions: Export current values with Get-TenantSettings and from the admin center.
Fill in the review record with current and recommended values.
Discuss differences with security and the platform owner.
Change settings in a planned window and tell makers what will be different.
Check tenant isolation and the baseline DLP policy.
Schedule the next review.
commonMistakes: Leaving production and trial environment creation open to everyone.
Blocking developer environments too, which pushes all experiments into the default environment.
Turning on tenant isolation without listing partner tenants that flows already connect to.
Changing settings without telling makers.
troubleshooting: If a setting is greyed out, you need the Power Platform administrator or Global administrator role.
If users can still create environments after the change, they hold an admin role or the change has not propagated yet. Allow up to an hour.
If flows fail after enabling tenant isolation, add the other tenant to the allow list in the needed direction.
If environment routing does not apply, the user is not in the selected security group, or developer environment creation is blocked for them.

faqs.question: How do I stop users creating Power Platform environments?
faqs.answer: In the admin center's tenant settings, set production and trial environment assignments to specific admins only.

faqs.question: Should I block developer environments?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A personal developer environment keeps experiments out of the default environment. Environment routing can send new makers to one automatically.

faqs.question: What is tenant isolation?
faqs.answer: A setting that blocks connectors from signing in to other Microsoft Entra tenants, in either direction, unless a tenant is on the allow list.

create-a-support-intake-queue.shortDescription: A single front door for Power Platform requests: a form, a queue with categories and priorities, routing rules and response targets.
create-a-support-intake-queue.fullDescription: Platform teams receive the same handful of request types through email, chat and hallway conversations: new environments, connector access, licences, help with a broken flow. A simple intake queue with a form, categories and an owner for each makes the work visible and measurable.
create-a-support-intake-queue.problemStatement: Requests arrive in five channels, some are answered twice and others never, and nobody can say how long a new environment takes.
whenToUse: More than one person handles platform requests
Makers do not know how to ask for environments, connectors or licences
You need figures to justify the platform team's time
whenNotToUse: Organisations whose service desk tool already has a Power Platform category with routing
Very small teams where one person handles every request and a shared mailbox is enough
create-a-support-intake-queue.formulaOrCode:
Request types and routing
  Type                         Asks for                                    Routed to          Target
  New environment              purpose, owner, stage, data sensitivity     Platform admin     3 days
  Connector or DLP change      connector, purpose, data involved           Platform + security 5-10 days
  Licence                      user(s), app or flow, cost centre           Licence admin      2 days
  Access to app or environment user, role, approver                        App owner          1 day
  Something is broken          app or flow link, error text, screenshot    Support tier 2     by criticality
  Deployment request           solution, version, target, window           Platform admin     per release calendar
  How do I...? / design advice description                                 Community / coach  3 days
  New app or automation idea   problem, users, value                       Intake board       next board meeting

Queue (SharePoint list or Dataverse table)
  Title, Request type (choice), Description, Requester (person), Department
  Environment, Resource link
  Priority (Low | Normal | High | Urgent), Business impact
  Status (New | Triaged | In progress | Waiting for requester | Resolved | Closed), default New
  Assigned to (person), Assigned team
  Due date (set by flow from type and priority)
  Resolution notes, Resolved on
  Index Status, Request type and Assigned to.

Form
  Microsoft Forms, a canvas app, or the list's own form. Show different questions per request type.
  Link it from the maker welcome message, DLP error message and the community channel.

Triage flow
  Trigger: When an item is created
  Switch on Request type: set Assigned team and Due date = addDays(utcNow(), <target>)
  Post a card to the team's channel with a link, and email the requester a confirmation with the item ID.
  Daily at 9:00: Get items where Status ne 'Closed' and DueDate lt today -> post an overdue digest.

Views
  New and unassigned          Status = New
  My queue                    Assigned to = [Me], Status <> Closed
  Overdue                     Due date < [Today], Status not in Resolved, Closed
  Waiting for requester       older than 5 days -> remind, then close after 10

Measures (monthly)
  Requests by type, median time to first response, median time to resolve,
  percentage within target, top five recurring questions (turn these into guidance pages).

Automate the common ones
  Environment requests: an approval, then Create Environment (Power Platform for Admins V2 connector).
  Licence requests: add the user to the licensing group after approval.
stepByStepInstructions: List the request types you receive today and who handles each.
Create the queue list and its views.
Build the form with questions per type.
Add the triage flow that assigns, sets due dates and confirms to the requester.
Publish the link everywhere makers look for help.
Redirect requests that arrive by email or chat to the form.
Review the measures monthly and automate the most common type first.
commonMistakes: Launching the form but still accepting requests by direct message.
One generic request type, so nothing can be routed or measured.
No confirmation to the requester, who then asks again elsewhere.
Targets with nobody watching the overdue view.
troubleshooting: If requests sit in New, nobody owns triage. Name a daily triage owner on a rota.
If requesters skip key details, make those questions required for that type.
If the flow assigns the wrong team, check the Switch cases match the choice values exactly.
If the queue fills with how-to questions, publish answers and point the form's first page at them.

faqs.question: How should makers request a new Power Platform environment?
faqs.answer: Through a form that asks for the purpose, owner, stage and data sensitivity, feeding a queue the platform team works from. The creation itself can be automated after approval.

faqs.question: What tool should I use for a platform support queue?
faqs.answer: A SharePoint list or Dataverse table with a form and a triage flow is enough for most teams. Use the service desk tool if one already exists.

faqs.question: What should be measured?
faqs.answer: Volume by request type, time to first response, time to resolve and the share completed within target.

create-a-capacity-monitoring-checklist.shortDescription: Keep Dataverse database, file and log storage under control: where to see usage, what consumes it and what to clean up first.
create-a-capacity-monitoring-checklist.fullDescription: Dataverse capacity is pooled across the tenant and split into database, file and log. When the pool is exceeded, administrators lose the ability to create, copy and restore environments. A monthly check and a few bulk-delete jobs usually keep usage steady without buying more.
create-a-capacity-monitoring-checklist.problemStatement: An environment copy is blocked during a release because the tenant is over its storage entitlement, and nobody knows what filled it.
whenToUse: Tenants with several Dataverse environments
Usage above 80 percent of entitlement in any storage type
Before creating or copying environments for a project
whenNotToUse: Tenants using only SharePoint-backed apps with no Dataverse databases
Tenants far below their entitlement with no growth, where a quarterly check is enough
create-a-capacity-monitoring-checklist.formulaOrCode:
Where to look
  Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Capacity add-ons / Dataverse
    Summary        entitlement and use for Database, File and Log, tenant-wide
    Dataverse tab  usage per environment; open an environment for its top tables and a trend chart
    Download       CSV of all environments for the monthly record

What each type holds
  Database   table rows
  File       attachments (Notes, email attachments), file and image columns, web resources, solution files
  Log        audit logs and plug-in trace logs

Monthly checklist
  [ ] Tenant totals: any type above 80 percent of entitlement?
  [ ] Top five environments by each type, and change since last month
  [ ] For each: top tables
  [ ] Environments with a database but no activity (candidates for deletion)
  [ ] Trial and developer environments older than 60 days
  [ ] Audit retention set on every environment
  [ ] Bulk delete jobs ran successfully
  [ ] Record the figures and actions

Usual causes and fixes
  Table / symptom                  Fix
  AsyncOperationBase               Bulk delete completed system jobs older than 30 days
  WorkflowLogBase / flow run data  Bulk delete; reduce logging on classic workflows
  ActivityMimeAttachment, Annotation (File)   Delete old email attachments and large notes; move files to SharePoint or Azure Blob
  AuditBase (Log)                  Set audit retention (for example 180 days); delete old audit logs
  PluginTraceLogBase               Turn plug-in trace logging to Off or Exception; bulk delete
  DuplicateRecordBase, ImportJobBase, BulkDeleteOperationBase   Bulk delete
  SubscriptionTrackingDeletedObject   Reduce the deleted-records tracking window via support guidance
  Your own tables                  Archive closed rows; use Dataverse long term retention; remove unused file columns

Bulk delete (per environment)
  Admin center > Environments > select > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion > New
  Example: System Jobs where Status = Succeeded and Completed On older than 30 days, recurring every 7 days.

Audit retention
  Environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings > Retain these logs for: choose a period.
  Free log space: Audit log management > Delete logs (by table, user or date range).

Environments
  Delete unused sandboxes, trials and developer environments (recoverable for 7 days).
  Each new environment with a database needs at least 1 GB of database capacity available.

What happens when over capacity
  Notifications to admins. Then you cannot create, copy, restore or convert environments, or add
  Dataverse to an environment, until usage is back under entitlement. Existing apps keep running.

Add capacity
  Each premium licence adds to the pool. Extra capacity can be bought per GB by type.
  Compare the cost with archiving before buying.

Alerting
  Scheduled flow: Power Platform for Admins > List environments as admin, read capacity properties,
  post to the admin channel when any environment grows more than 10 percent in a month.
stepByStepInstructions: Download the capacity report and record this month's totals.
Open the largest environments and note their top tables.
Create recurring bulk delete jobs for system jobs and logs in each environment.
Set audit retention everywhere.
Delete or archive unused environments.
Agree an archiving approach for the largest business tables.
Repeat monthly and chart the trend.
commonMistakes: Buying capacity before running basic bulk deletes.
Audit retention left on Forever.
Storing large files in Notes when SharePoint or Blob storage would do.
Plug-in trace logging left on All in production.
troubleshooting: If usage does not drop after deleting, the capacity report can take up to 24 hours to refresh.
If a bulk delete job fails or stalls, narrow its criteria so each run handles fewer rows.
If file storage keeps growing, check email attachments from server-side sync and large Notes.
If you cannot create an environment, the tenant is over entitlement in at least one storage type. Free space or add capacity first.

faqs.question: How do I check Dataverse storage usage?
faqs.answer: Open the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing and then the Dataverse capacity page. It shows tenant totals, usage per environment and the largest tables.

faqs.question: What happens if I exceed Dataverse capacity?
faqs.answer: Apps keep working, but administrators cannot create, copy or restore environments until usage is back within the entitlement.

faqs.question: How can I reduce Dataverse storage?
faqs.answer: Bulk delete completed system jobs and logs, set audit log retention, remove large attachments, archive old rows and delete environments nobody uses.

create-a-center-of-excellence-triage-vie.shortDescription: One prioritised view for a centre of excellence team: the apps, flows and environments that need attention this week, and why.
create-a-center-of-excellence-triage-vie.fullDescription: The CoE Starter Kit and the admin center produce thousands of rows about apps and flows. A triage view reduces them to a short worklist using a few rules: orphaned, widely shared without a backup owner, non-compliant, failing or unused. The team works the list top to bottom each week.
create-a-center-of-excellence-triage-vie.problemStatement: The CoE dashboard has twelve pages of charts, and the team still finds out about problems from users because nothing says what to do next.
whenToUse: Teams running the CoE Starter Kit or their own inventory
Weekly platform operations meetings
When governance work is ad hoc and reactive
whenNotToUse: Tenants with only a handful of apps, where a monthly look at the admin center is enough
Tenants with no inventory data yet. Set up the inventory first
create-a-center-of-excellence-triage-vie.formulaOrCode:
Triage rules (highest priority first)
  Rule                                                   Why it matters                Action
  1. Owner account disabled or deleted (orphan)          nobody can fix or approve     assign new owner, or archive
  2. Flow suspended or failing > 50% of runs in 7 days   process is broken             contact owner, fix or turn off
  3. Shared with > 20 users or a group, single owner     no backup                     add co-owner, record support owner
  4. Shared with Everyone or with guests                 exposure                      confirm intent with owner
  5. Uses blocked or non-business connector / DLP hit    policy                        review or redesign
  6. Premium connector, no licence record                cost and compliance           add to exception register
  7. Missing business justification (CoE compliance)     unknown purpose               request details; follow the kit's process
  8. Production-like use in the default environment      no ALM                        plan move to a managed environment
  9. No launches or runs in 90 days                      clutter                       ask owner; archive after 30 days' notice
  10. Environment without owner or past review date      sprawl                        review or delete

Scoring (so the list sorts itself)
  Score = 5 x Orphaned + 4 x Failing + 3 x WidelySharedSingleOwner + 3 x SharedWithEveryone
        + 3 x DlpIssue + 2 x PremiumNoRecord + 1 x NoJustification + 1 x Unused90Days
  Sort by Score descending, then by number of users.

With the CoE Starter Kit (Dataverse tables admin_App, admin_Flow, admin_Environment, admin_Maker)
  Model-driven view on Power Apps Apps, for example "Triage - orphaned":
    Filter: App Is Orphaned equals Yes  AND  App Deleted equals No
  "Triage - widely shared":
    Filter: App Shared Users greater than 20  OR  App Shared With Tenant equals Yes
  "Triage - unused":
    Filter: App Last Launched On older than 90 days
  Column names vary slightly between kit versions. Check them in the table's column list.

  Power BI: add a table visual to the kit's report using the same filters and the score as a measure:
    Triage Score =
        5 * MAX(App[IsOrphaned]) + 3 * IF(MAX(App[SharedUsers]) > 20, 1, 0)
      + 3 * MAX(App[SharedWithTenant]) + IF(DATEDIFF(MAX(App[LastLaunched]), TODAY(), DAY) > 90, 1, 0)

Without the kit
  Export the Power Apps and Power Automate inventory from the admin center, or use
  Get-AdminPowerApp and Get-AdminFlow, load into a list, and add the rule columns as Yes/No.
  Owner status: Get-MgUser -UserId <owner id> -Property accountEnabled

Triage record (one row per item worked)
  Resource, Rule hit, Owner contacted on, Response, Decision (Keep | Fix | Reassign | Archive | Delete),
  Decided by, Due date, Closed on

Weekly meeting (20 minutes)
  Top ten by score. Assign each to a person. Check last week's items are closed.

Archive before delete
  Export the app (.msapp) or flow package, store it, remove sharing, wait 30 days, then delete.
  The CoE kit's inactivity process automates the notices.
stepByStepInstructions: Confirm the inventory is refreshing, from the CoE kit or your own export.
Add the rule columns or views for each triage rule.
Build one sorted view or report page with the score.
Create the triage record list.
Hold a short weekly meeting and work the top items.
Tune thresholds after a month so the list stays at a size the team can clear.
commonMistakes: Showing everything, so the list never shrinks and gets ignored.
Deleting unused resources without notice or an archive copy.
Contacting makers with accusations instead of offers of help.
Not recording decisions, so the same item reappears every week.
troubleshooting: If orphan flags look wrong, the kit's sync flows may have failed. Check the Admin | Sync Template flows' run history.
If last launched dates are empty, the kit needs the audit log sync configured to collect usage.
If the view is slow, filter on indexed or simple columns first and keep the columns shown to a minimum.
If owners do not reply, escalate to their manager only for rules one to five.

faqs.question: What should a Power Platform CoE look at each week?
faqs.answer: A short list of orphaned resources, failing flows, widely shared apps with one owner, DLP or licence issues and resources unused for 90 days, sorted by risk.

faqs.question: What is an orphaned app or flow?
faqs.answer: One whose owner's account has been disabled or deleted, leaving nobody able to maintain it or approve changes.

faqs.question: Do I need the CoE Starter Kit for this?
faqs.answer: No. The kit makes it easier, but the admin center inventory export or the admin PowerShell cmdlets provide the same basic data.

create-a-public-intake-portal-checklist.shortDescription: Plan and build a Power Pages site where the public or external partners submit requests into Dataverse, with the security and spam controls it needs.
create-a-public-intake-portal-checklist.fullDescription: A public intake site takes a form from someone outside your organisation and creates a Dataverse row for staff to work. The build is quick. The risks are in the details: anonymous create permissions, spam, file uploads and what the submitter can see afterwards. This checklist covers each in order.
create-a-public-intake-portal-checklist.problemStatement: A portal form goes live with anonymous access to the whole table, no spam protection and no confirmation, and fills with junk within a week.
whenToUse: External people must submit requests, applications or reports
Staff then process them in a model-driven or canvas app
Replacing an emailed form or PDF
whenNotToUse: Internal-only forms, where a canvas app or Microsoft Forms is cheaper
Simple surveys with no follow-up process
create-a-public-intake-portal-checklist.formulaOrCode:
1. Decide who submits
  Anonymous       anyone with the link. Simplest, highest spam risk, no "my requests" page.
  Authenticated   sign-in through Microsoft Entra External ID, Entra ID or another provider.
                  Needed if people must return to see or update their submissions.

2. Data model
  Table: Intake Request (contoso_IntakeRequest)
    Subject, Details, Category (choice), Submitter name, Submitter email, Phone,
    Contact (lookup, filled when signed in), Status reason (Submitted | In review | Completed),
    Source (default "Portal"), Consent given (Yes/No), Created On
  Keep internal-only columns (notes, score, assignee) off the portal form.

3. Form
  Power Pages design studio > Data > the table > Forms > New form (portal-specific, minimal fields)
  Pages > add page > Form component > choose the form
    Data from this form: Creates a new record
    On submit: Show a message, or redirect to a thank-you page
    CAPTCHA: On
    Attachments: On only if needed; limit count, size (MB) and file types (for example .pdf,.jpg,.png)

4. Table permissions
  Anonymous submit
    Name: Intake - anonymous create      Table: Intake Request
    Access type: Global                  Privileges: Create only (no Read, Write or Delete)
    Web role: Anonymous Users
  Signed-in submit and view own
    Access type: Contact                 Relationship: contact -> intake request
    Privileges: Create, Read, Append     Web role: Authenticated Users
  Attachments need a child permission on Note (annotation) with Create and Append,
  and Append To on the parent.

5. Confirmation and routing (Power Automate, Dataverse trigger "When a row is added")
  Filter rows: contoso_source eq 'Portal'
  Send the submitter an email with their reference number.
  Assign to the team queue or post to the team's channel.

6. Spam and abuse
  [ ] CAPTCHA on the form
  [ ] Web Application Firewall enabled for the site (Set up > Security > Web application firewall)
  [ ] Rate limiting rule if available on your plan
  [ ] Maximum lengths on text columns
  [ ] No anonymous Read permission on any table with personal data

7. Privacy
  [ ] Consent checkbox and link to the privacy notice
  [ ] Retention period decided, with a bulk delete job for old submissions
  [ ] Site visibility set to Public only when ready (Set up > Site visibility)

8. Before launch
  [ ] Site checker run (Set up > Site checker) with no errors
  [ ] Security scan run (Security > Run scan)
  [ ] Submitted as an anonymous user in a private browser window
  [ ] Tried to open another submission's URL and the Web API as anonymous: access denied
  [ ] Custom domain and certificate in place
stepByStepInstructions: Decide between anonymous and signed-in submission.
Create the intake table and a minimal portal form.
Add the form to a page with CAPTCHA and a thank-you redirect.
Create table permissions with Create only for anonymous users.
Build the confirmation and routing flow.
Turn on the firewall and run the site checker and security scan.
Test as an outsider in a private window, then make the site public.
commonMistakes: Giving the Anonymous Users role Read access so the form 'works'.
Using the main model-driven form on the portal, exposing internal fields.
No CAPTCHA.
Leaving the site public while still under construction.
troubleshooting: If the form shows 'You don't have the appropriate permissions', the web role lacks Create on the table, or table permissions are not enabled on the form.
If attachments fail, add a child table permission on Note with Create and Append.
If the submission saves but no email arrives, check the flow's trigger filter and that it runs under an account with access to the table.
If changes do not show on the site, select Sync in the design studio, or clear the site cache from the admin center.

faqs.question: Can people submit a Power Pages form without signing in?
faqs.answer: Yes. Give the Anonymous Users web role a table permission with Create only, and turn on CAPTCHA to limit spam.

faqs.question: How do I stop spam on a Power Pages form?
faqs.answer: Enable CAPTCHA on the form, turn on the site's web application firewall, limit field lengths and never grant anonymous users more than Create.

faqs.question: How do submitters see their own requests later?
faqs.answer: They need to sign in. A table permission with Contact access type then limits them to rows linked to their own contact.

create-a-web-role-matrix.shortDescription: Map each kind of Power Pages visitor to a web role and each role to pages and table permissions before configuring security.
create-a-web-role-matrix.fullDescription: Power Pages security has three moving parts: web roles assigned to contacts, page permissions that control who can see a page, and table permissions that control data. A matrix that lines up visitor types against pages and tables, agreed before building, prevents the common result of everyone ending up in one over-privileged role.
create-a-web-role-matrix.problemStatement: Every signed-in user gets the same role with global read on several tables, because roles were added one error message at a time.
whenToUse: Sites with more than one type of signed-in user
Partner or customer portals where organisations must not see each other's data
Before a security review
whenNotToUse: Fully public, read-only sites with no sign-in
Sites where every signed-in visitor has exactly the same access
create-a-web-role-matrix.formulaOrCode:
Visitor types -> web roles
  Visitor                         Web role                  Assigned how
  Anyone not signed in            Anonymous Users           built in, automatic
  Anyone signed in                Authenticated Users       built in, automatic
  Customer contact                Customer                  flow on registration, or invitation
  Customer account manager        Customer Manager          by staff, in the Portal Management app
  Partner technician              Partner                   invitation with role
  Staff content editor            Content Editor            staff contact records
  Site administrator              Administrators            built in

Pages
  Page                    Anonymous   Authenticated   Customer   Customer Manager   Partner
  Home, Help              view        view            view       view               view
  Submit request          -           -               view       view               -
  My requests             -           -               view       view               -
  Company requests        -           -               -          view               -
  Assigned jobs           -           -               -          -                  view
  Set with Page permissions: page > ... > Page settings > Permissions > "I want to choose who can see this page".
  Child pages inherit unless set otherwise.

Tables
  Table       Role               Access type   Relationship                    Privileges
  Request     Customer           Contact       contact -> request (Requester)  Create, Read, Write, Append
  Request     Customer Manager   Account       account -> request (Company)    Read
  Request     Partner            Contact       contact -> request (Technician) Read, Write
  Note        Customer           Parent        child of the Request permission Create, Read, Append
  Category    Authenticated      Global                                         Read
  Knowledge   Anonymous          Global                                         Read

Access types
  Global    every row                     reference data, published content
  Contact   rows related to the signed-in contact
  Account   rows related to the contact's parent account
  Self      the contact's own contact row (profile page)
  Parent    rows reached through a parent table permission

Rules
  A contact can hold several web roles. Permissions add up.
  Give Authenticated Users only what every signed-in user may have.
  Never Global with Write or Delete for an external role.
  Column permission profiles hide or lock individual columns for the Web API.

Assigning roles
  Portal Management app > Contacts > open contact > Related > Web Roles > Add existing
  On registration (flow): When a row is added (Contact) with a condition on email domain or invitation,
  then Relate rows: contact -> web role (relationship adx_webrole_contact).
  Invitations (Portal Management > Invitations) can assign web roles and an account on redemption.

Test plan
  One test contact per role. For each cell of the matrix: can they open the page, can they see only
  their rows, can they change what they should not? Test the Web API as well as the pages:
  /_api/contoso_requests should return only permitted rows.
stepByStepInstructions: List visitor types with the business owner.
Create a web role for each type beyond the two built-in ones.
Fill in the page and table sections of the matrix.
Configure page permissions.
Create table permissions with the narrowest access type that works, and link them to roles.
Decide how each role is assigned.
Test every cell with a contact per role.
commonMistakes: Putting everything on Authenticated Users.
Using Global access where Contact or Account would do.
Forgetting that lists and forms must have table permissions enabled.
Testing only as an administrator, who bypasses most restrictions.
troubleshooting: If a user sees no rows in a list, their role's table permission relationship does not match how rows link to their contact or account.
If a page shows 'Page not found' for some users, page permissions exclude their role.
If a user sees other companies' data, a Global permission is attached to one of their roles. Check every role they hold.
If a role change does not apply, the user must sign out and in again. Server-side caching can also take a few minutes.

faqs.question: What is a web role in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A named group assigned to contacts. Page permissions and table permissions are linked to web roles to decide what each visitor can see and do.

faqs.question: What is the difference between web roles and Dataverse security roles?
faqs.answer: Web roles apply to external site visitors, who are contacts. Dataverse security roles apply to licensed internal users of apps.

faqs.question: Can a contact have more than one web role?
faqs.answer: Yes. Their permissions are the combination of all roles they hold, plus Authenticated Users.

create-a-basic-form-validation-plan.shortDescription: Decide which validation happens in Dataverse, in the Power Pages form settings and in JavaScript, and build each layer for a basic form.
create-a-basic-form-validation-plan.fullDescription: Portal forms are filled in by people you cannot train, so validation matters more than in an internal app. Three layers are available: column rules in Dataverse, form metadata in Power Pages, and custom JavaScript for anything conditional. Server-side rules are the only ones that cannot be bypassed, so the plan starts there.
create-a-basic-form-validation-plan.problemStatement: Validation exists only as JavaScript on the page, so rows with missing or impossible values still arrive through slow browsers, scripts and the Web API.
whenToUse: Any basic or multistep form on a Power Pages site
Forms with conditional required fields or cross-field rules
Before opening a form to the public
whenNotToUse: Read-only forms
Internal canvas or model-driven forms, which have their own validation features
stepByStepInstructions: List every rule and place it in the plan table.
Set required, length and format on the Dataverse columns.
Add Entity-scope business rules for cross-field checks.
Configure required fields, messages and regular expressions in the form settings and metadata.
Add JavaScript validators only for conditional behaviour.
Test each rule in the browser and through the Web API.
commonMistakes: Relying on JavaScript alone.
Vague messages such as 'Invalid input'.
Hiding a required field with script, which blocks submission with no visible reason.
Hard-coding choice values in script without noting where they come from.
troubleshooting: If a custom validator never fires, it was added before Page_Validators existed. Wrap it in document ready.
If the form will not submit and shows no message, a hidden field is still required. Remove the requirement when hiding it.
If a regular expression rejects valid input, test it against real examples and remember the metadata field needs the pattern without slashes.
If a business rule error shows as a generic message, set the rule's scope to Entity and keep its message short.

faqs.question: How do I make a field required on a Power Pages form?
faqs.answer: Select the form in the design studio, choose Edit fields and mark the field required, or set the Dataverse column to Business required so it applies everywhere.

faqs.question: How do I add custom validation to a Power Pages basic form?
faqs.answer: Use Basic Form Metadata for regular expressions and ranges. For conditional rules, add a validator to Page_Validators in the form's custom JavaScript, and back it with a Dataverse business rule.

faqs.question: Is JavaScript validation enough?
faqs.answer: No. Client-side checks can be bypassed. Enforce important rules in Dataverse so they apply to every route in.

create-a-portal-content-publishing-workf.shortDescription: A draft, review and publish routine for Power Pages content, using publishing states, a development site and deployment between environments.
create-a-portal-content-publishing-workf.fullDescription: Changes made in the Power Pages design studio are live as soon as they sync. A publishing workflow gives content authors a safe place to draft, a reviewer who checks before visitors see anything, and a repeatable way to move approved changes to the production site.
create-a-portal-content-publishing-workf.problemStatement: An author fixes a typo on the live site and accidentally breaks the home page layout, and there is no previous version to go back to.
whenToUse: Sites edited by more than one person
Sites with legal, brand or accessibility review requirements
Any production site with real visitors
whenNotToUse: Prototype sites that are still private
Single-author sites where one person writes, reviews and publishes
create-a-portal-content-publishing-workf.formulaOrCode:
Two levels of control

A. Within one site: publishing states
  Each web page has a Publishing State (Portal Management app > Web Pages > Publishing State).
    Draft       not visible to visitors
    Published   visible
  Roles
    Author     creates and edits pages in Draft
    Reviewer   checks content, links, accessibility, then sets Published
  Publishing State Transition Rules (Portal Management > Publishing States) can limit which web roles
  may move a page from Draft to Published.
  Front-side preview: users whose web role has website access permission "Preview Unpublished Entities"
  can see draft pages while signed in.

  Content snippets and web templates have no draft state: changes are live on save.
  For those, use level B.

B. Between environments: build in dev, deploy to prod
  Development site (private)  ->  Test site (private)  ->  Production site (public)
  Move changes with one of:
    Solutions (enhanced data model): add the site and its components to a solution, deploy managed
      through Power Platform pipelines.
    Power Platform CLI:
      pac pages download --path ./site --webSiteId <dev site id> --modelVersion 2
      (commit to source control, review the diff)
      pac pages upload   --path ./site/<site-name> --deploymentProfile prod --modelVersion 2
      Deployment profiles (deployment-profiles/prod.deployment.yml) hold values that differ per
      environment, such as site settings.

Workflow
  1. Request     author logs the change (what, why, page, go-live date)
  2. Draft       in the development site, or as a Draft page in production for simple text
  3. Review      second person checks against the checklist
  4. Approve     content owner signs off
  5. Publish     reviewer sets Published, or the deployment runs
  6. Verify      open the live page signed out, on a phone and a desktop
  7. Record      note the change and date

Review checklist
  [ ] Spelling, tone, and facts confirmed by the content owner
  [ ] Links work and open the right target
  [ ] Images have alt text; headings are in order (one H1)
  [ ] Colour contrast and keyboard access checked
  [ ] Page title and description set (SEO)
  [ ] Page permissions correct: public pages are public, restricted pages are restricted
  [ ] Looks right at phone width

Site visibility
  Keep development and test sites Private (Set up > Site visibility) so only chosen staff can open them.

Rollback
  With source control: upload the previous commit. With solutions: re-import the previous version.
  For a single page: set it back to Draft and restore the earlier copy from the dev site.

Cache
  After a deployment, clear the site cache: Power Platform admin center > Resources > Power Pages sites >
  select site > Site actions > Purge cache.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a private development copy of the site in a separate environment.
Name the authors, reviewers and content owners.
Use Draft for new pages and restrict who can publish.
Choose solutions or the pac CLI for moving changes, and store the site in source control.
Adopt the seven-step workflow and the review checklist.
After each deployment, purge the cache and verify signed out.
commonMistakes: Editing templates and snippets directly on the live site.
Reviewing only on a desktop while signed in as an administrator.
Leaving the development site public.
No record of what changed and when.
troubleshooting: If a published change is not visible, purge the site cache and check the page's publishing state.
If draft pages are visible to visitors, their publishing state is Published or the visitor has a role with preview rights.
If pac pages upload skips files, it uploads only changed files. Use --forceUploadAll after a profile change.
If the wrong model version is used, check whether the site is on the standard or enhanced data model and set --modelVersion to match.

faqs.question: How do I preview Power Pages changes before publishing?
faqs.answer: Create pages in the Draft publishing state, or make changes in a private development site and deploy them to production after review.

faqs.question: How do I move a Power Pages site between environments?
faqs.answer: Use solutions with the enhanced data model, or download and upload the site with the Power Platform CLI's pac pages commands.

faqs.question: Why are my changes not showing on the live site?
faqs.answer: The site caches content. Select Sync in the design studio or purge the cache from the admin center.

create-a-dataverse-backed-contact-experi.shortDescription: Let signed-in Power Pages visitors see and update their own contact details and related records, with Self and Contact table permissions.
create-a-dataverse-backed-contact-experi.fullDescription: Every signed-in portal user is a Dataverse contact. A good contact experience gives them a profile page to keep their details current and pages listing the records linked to them, such as requests or orders, while guaranteeing they can never reach anyone else's.
create-a-dataverse-backed-contact-experi.problemStatement: Customers email staff to change a phone number, and a 'my requests' page built with a global permission shows them everyone's requests.
whenToUse: Customer or partner portals with sign-in
Any site where visitors own data in Dataverse
Reducing manual updates to contact records
whenNotToUse: Anonymous-only sites
Sites where contact data is mastered in another system and must be read-only
create-a-dataverse-backed-contact-experi.formulaOrCode:
1. Identity Set up > Identity providers: enable Microsoft Entra External ID (or another provider) and set it as default. On first sign-in a contact is created or matched by email. Site setting Authentication/Registration/RequiresConfirmation and related settings control email confirmation. 2. Profile page (built in: /profile) The Profile Web Form / basic form edits the signed-in contact. Choose its fields: Portal Management > Basic Forms > "Profile Web Form" uses the Contact form named "Profile Web Form". Edit that Dataverse form to add or remove fields. Table permission Name: Contact - own record Table: Contact Access type: Self Privileges: Read, Write Web role: Authenticated Users 3. My requests (list + details) List component on page "My requests" Table: Request View: Active Requests Enable table permissions: On Details page: "Request details" Create page: "New request" Table permission Name: Request - own Access type: Contact Relationship: contoso_contact_request (Requester) Privileges: Create, Read, Write, Append Web role: Authenticated Users Child permission for notes and attachments: Table Note, Access type Parent, Create, Read, Append. 4. Set the requester automatically on create Basic Form Metadata on the create form: Attribute = Requester, Set Value On Save = Yes, Type = Current portal user, From attribute = Contact. 5. Company-wide view for account managers Table permission: Access type Account, Relationship account -> request, Privileges Read. Web role: Customer Manager. The contact's Parent Customer must be the account. 6. Show the user's details with Liquid {% if user %}

Signed in as {{ user.fullname }} ({{ user.emailaddress1 }})

Company: {{ user.parentcustomerid.name }}

{% else %} Sign in {% endif %} 7. Read related rows with FetchXML (respects table permissions) {% fetchxml my_requests %} {% endfetchxml %} {% for r in my_requests.results.entities %}
  • {{ r.contoso_name }} - {{ r.statuscode.label }}
    • {% endfor %} 8. Privacy controls [ ] Profile form shows only fields the person should edit (not owner, credit limit, internal flags) [ ] Column permission profile restricts sensitive contact columns for the Web API [ ] Email change process decided (the sign-in identity and the contact email are separate) [ ] Account deletion or data request route published
stepByStepInstructions: Enable an identity provider and test registration.
Trim the profile form to the fields visitors may edit.
Add the Self permission on Contact.
Build the list, details and create pages for the related table.
Add the Contact-scoped table permission and the child permission for notes.
Set the requester automatically with form metadata.
Test with two contacts and confirm neither can see the other's rows.
commonMistakes: Using Global access for 'my' lists and filtering in the view instead.
Leaving internal fields on the profile form.
Forgetting the child permission for attachments.
Not setting the requester on create, so new rows vanish from the user's own list.
troubleshooting: If the profile page says the user lacks permission, add a Self permission with Read and Write on Contact.
If a newly created row does not appear in My requests, its contact lookup was not set. Add Set Value On Save.
If the manager view is empty, the contact has no parent account or the relationship in the permission is wrong.
If Liquid shows nothing for user fields, the page is cached for anonymous visitors or the user is not signed in.

faqs.question: How do portal users update their own details?
faqs.answer: Through the built-in profile page, which edits their contact row. Give Authenticated Users a table permission on Contact with Self access and Read and Write.

faqs.question: How do I show a user only their own records?
faqs.answer: Use a table permission with Contact access type and the relationship between contact and the table. Lists and FetchXML then return only related rows.

faqs.question: Is every Power Pages user a contact?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each signed-in visitor is linked to a contact row in Dataverse, and web roles are assigned to that contact.

create-a-site-launch-readiness-review.shortDescription: A go-live review for a Power Pages site covering security, performance, accessibility, SEO, domain, licensing and support.
create-a-site-launch-readiness-review.fullDescription: A Power Pages site is public infrastructure. Before it is opened to visitors it needs the same checks as any website, plus a few specific to Dataverse: table permissions, anonymous access and capacity licensing. This review collects them into one go or no-go list.
create-a-site-launch-readiness-review.problemStatement: A site goes public on a temporary URL with the default theme, an open Web API and no licence capacity, and is taken down a week later.
whenToUse: Before changing a site's visibility to Public
Before a major redesign goes live
Annual health check of a live site
whenNotToUse: Private development and test sites
Internal-only sites restricted to employees, which need a shorter review
create-a-site-launch-readiness-review.formulaOrCode:
Site launch readiness review

Security
  [ ] Security scan run and findings resolved (Power Pages > Security > Run scan)
  [ ] Table permissions reviewed: no Global Write/Delete for external roles; anonymous has only what it needs
  [ ] Every list and form has "Enable table permissions" on
  [ ] Web API enabled only for required tables and columns (site settings Webapi/<table>/enabled, /fields)
  [ ] Web Application Firewall on; HTTPS only; TLS minimum version set
  [ ] HTTP headers set through site settings: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options,
      X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security
  [ ] Identity providers: only the ones in use are enabled; local sign-in disabled if not needed
  [ ] Open registration decision made (invitation only, or open with email confirmation)
  [ ] Custom error pages turned on (no stack traces)
  [ ] Administrators web role limited to named people

Content and accessibility
  [ ] All pages reviewed and Published; no sample or template pages left
  [ ] Header, footer, privacy notice, terms, cookie notice in place
  [ ] Accessibility: headings, alt text, contrast, keyboard navigation, form labels (WCAG 2.1 AA)
  [ ] 404 page and sign-in pages styled
  [ ] Works at phone width

Performance
  [ ] Site checker run with no errors (Set up > Site checker)
  [ ] Content delivery network enabled (Set up > Performance and protection)
  [ ] Images compressed; large files not served from Notes
  [ ] Lists page their results and FetchXML queries use filters and top
  [ ] Header and footer output caching on

SEO and analytics
  [ ] Page titles and meta descriptions set
  [ ] robots.txt and sitemap reviewed (site markers and settings)
  [ ] Analytics or tag manager snippet added with consent handling
  [ ] Redirects from the old site's URLs (Portal Management > Redirects)

Domain and environment
  [ ] Custom domain added with SSL certificate (Set up > Custom domains)
  [ ] Site converted from Trial to Production
  [ ] Site is in the production environment, deployed from dev through the agreed path
  [ ] Site visibility set to Public at the launch time only

Licensing and capacity
  [ ] Authenticated users per site per month and anonymous users per site per month capacity purchased
      or pay-as-you-go meters linked
  [ ] Dataverse storage sufficient for expected submissions and files

Operations
  [ ] Business owner, content owner and technical owner named
  [ ] Monitoring: diagnostic logging to Azure Blob storage enabled if needed
  [ ] Backup and restore approach understood (environment backups)
  [ ] Support route for visitors published
  [ ] Rollback: site can be set to Private within minutes

Decision: Go | Go with conditions | No-go        Signed by owners, with date.
stepByStepInstructions: Run the security scan and the site checker and fix what they report.
Walk through the site signed out, as a new visitor would.
Test each web role with a dedicated contact.
Confirm domain, certificate, production conversion and licence capacity.
Complete the review with the owners and record the decision.
Switch visibility to Public at the agreed time and verify from outside the network.
commonMistakes: Going live on the trial site and losing it at expiry.
Leaving the Web API open on tables that do not need it.
No licence capacity for anonymous or authenticated users.
Testing only while signed in as an administrator.
troubleshooting: If the custom domain shows a certificate error, the SSL binding is missing or the certificate does not cover the host name.
If the public site asks visitors to sign in with a work account, site visibility is still Private.
If pages are slow, enable the CDN and check for lists or FetchXML without filters.
If search engines do not index the site, check robots.txt and that pages are Published and public.

faqs.question: What should I check before making a Power Pages site public?
faqs.answer: Run the security scan and site checker, review table permissions and the Web API, set up the custom domain and certificate, convert the site to production and confirm licence capacity.

faqs.question: How do I make a Power Pages site public?
faqs.answer: In Set up, change Site visibility from Private to Public. Until then only chosen people in your organisation can open it.

faqs.question: Do I need licences for site visitors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Production sites use capacity for authenticated users and for anonymous users per site per month, bought as packs or pay-as-you-go.

create-an-anonymous-access-risk-checklis.shortDescription: Find everything an unauthenticated visitor can reach on a Power Pages site (pages, tables, Web API, files) and close what should not be open.
create-an-anonymous-access-risk-checklis.fullDescription: Most Power Pages data leaks come from one cause: a table permission with Global access linked to the Anonymous Users role, often added to make a list work. This checklist walks through every route an anonymous visitor has to your data and shows how to test each one from outside.
create-an-anonymous-access-risk-checklis.problemStatement: A list page that was meant for staff is readable by anyone on the internet, including through the Web API and OData feed, and nobody notices for months.
whenToUse: Before any site goes public
After any change to table permissions or web roles
As a quarterly security check on live sites
whenNotToUse: Sites restricted to Private visibility that will never be public, although the checks still help
Sites with no Dataverse data components at all, only static pages
create-an-anonymous-access-risk-checklis.formulaOrCode:
1. Table permissions for anonymous users
  Portal Management app > Table Permissions > view filtered by Web Role = Anonymous Users
  or Power Pages design studio > Security > Table permissions.
  For each one ask: is this data meant to be public?
    Acceptable: Read on published knowledge articles, categories, public event listings.
    Create only on an intake table (no Read).
    Never: Read on Contact, Account, requests, notes; Write or Delete on anything.

2. Lists and forms without table permissions
  Each List and Basic Form has "Enable table permissions". If it is off, the component ignores
  permissions. Find them:
  Portal Management > Lists / Basic Forms > add the column "Enable Table Permissions" to the view and filter No.
  Newer sites enforce permissions regardless, but turn it on everywhere.

3. Web API
  Site settings (Portal Management > Site Settings), per table:
    Webapi/<table logical name>/enabled   true | false
    Webapi/<table logical name>/fields    list the columns needed; avoid *
  Test signed out:   https://<site>/_api/contacts?$top=1          expect 401/403 or an empty result
                     https://<site>/_api/<your table set>?$top=1

4. OData feeds on lists
  List > Options > "OData Feed: Enabled" exposes  https://<site>/_odata/<set name>
  Turn it off unless needed. Test:  https://<site>/_odata

5. Search
  Site search returns rows from searchable tables the visitor can read.
  Check the Portal Search view on each table and the anonymous table permissions together.

6. Pages
  Pages with "Anyone can see this page" should contain no data components for restricted tables.
  Check page permissions on parent pages; children inherit.

7. Files
  Web files (images, documents) on public pages are public. Notes attachments are reachable through
  /_entity/annotation/<id> only when table permissions allow. Do not store private documents as web files.

8. Sign-up
  If registration is open, "authenticated" means "anyone with an email address".
  Treat Authenticated Users almost as carefully as Anonymous Users, or switch to invitation only:
  site setting  Authentication/Registration/OpenRegistrationEnabled = false

9. Built-in scan
  Power Pages > Security > Run scan (checks for common exposure issues), and
  Set up > Site checker for anonymous access warnings on lists and forms.

10. Outside-in test (private browser window, not signed in)
  [ ] Open each list page URL directly
  [ ] /_api/ and /_odata/ URLs for your tables
  [ ] Site search for a customer's name
  [ ] Guess a details page URL with ?id=<guid>
  [ ] View page source for Liquid output of data
  Record the result of each test with the date.

If something is exposed
  Remove the permission or switch the site to Private at once, then assess what could have been read
  and for how long, and follow your organisation's incident process.
stepByStepInstructions: List all table permissions linked to Anonymous Users and justify each.
Turn on table permissions for every list and form.
Restrict Web API site settings to the needed tables and columns.
Disable OData feeds that are not required.
Decide whether registration should be open.
Run the security scan.
Repeat the outside-in tests from a private window and record the results.
commonMistakes: Adding a Global Read permission to Anonymous Users to make a page work.
Using * in Webapi fields.
Assuming a page nobody links to is private.
Open registration with generous Authenticated Users permissions.
troubleshooting: If a list still shows data to anonymous visitors, look for a second permission on a parent table or another web role named Anonymous Users with Global access.
If the Web API returns data when signed out, the table has an anonymous Read permission. The Web API follows table permissions.
If you cannot tell which role grants access, remove permissions from the Anonymous Users role one at a time in a test site.
If a fix does not take effect, purge the site cache.

faqs.question: How do I check what anonymous users can see on my Power Pages site?
faqs.answer: Review table permissions linked to the Anonymous Users role, run the built-in security scan, and test list pages, /_api/ and /_odata/ URLs from a private browser window.

faqs.question: Is the Power Pages Web API open by default?
faqs.answer: No. A table must be enabled through site settings and the visitor needs a table permission. Check both for every table.

faqs.question: What is the most common cause of data exposure in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A table permission with Global access attached to the Anonymous Users web role, or a list with table permissions turned off.

create-a-portal-feedback-capture-process.shortDescription: Collect page feedback and ratings from Power Pages visitors into Dataverse, route it to content owners and close the loop.
create-a-portal-feedback-capture-process.fullDescription: Visitors know which pages are confusing long before analytics does. A small feedback form on each page, stored in Dataverse with the page it came from, gives content owners a steady list of fixes. The process around it, triage, owner and response, is what turns comments into improvements.
create-a-portal-feedback-capture-process.problemStatement: The site has a general contact form, feedback about pages is lost among support requests, and nobody knows which articles fail readers.
whenToUse: Knowledge, guidance or service sites
After launch, to prioritise improvements
When content owners need evidence of what to fix
whenNotToUse: Transactional sites where a support request form already covers the need
Sites with too little traffic for ratings to mean anything
stepByStepInstructions: Create the feedback table and the Create-only table permission.
