Enable the Web API for the table with just the needed columns.
Add the web template to the page template or footer.
Build the routing flow and the weekly digest.
Agree the triage states and response time with content owners.
Review helpful rates monthly and fix the worst pages first.
commonMistakes: Collecting feedback with nobody assigned to read it.
Granting Read on the feedback table to anonymous users.
Acting on a rating from three responses.
Asking for an email address when no reply will be sent.
troubleshooting: If the POST returns 403, the Web API site settings or the Create table permission are missing for the visitor's role.
If the request fails with a token error, the anti-forgery token was not sent. Use shell.getTokenDeferred.
If spam arrives, add a honeypot field, tighten firewall rate limits or require sign-in to comment.
If the owner is blank, the page URL matched no prefix in the owners table. Add a default owner.

faqs.question: How do I add a 'Was this page helpful?' control to Power Pages?
faqs.answer: Create a small Dataverse table for feedback, allow Create through a table permission and the Web API, and add a web template with Yes and No buttons that posts the page URL and comment.

faqs.question: Where is Power Pages feedback stored?
faqs.answer: In Dataverse. The built-in rating feature uses the Feedback table. A custom control stores rows in your own table, where staff can triage them.

faqs.question: Should feedback be anonymous?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, to get more responses. Capture the contact automatically when a visitor is signed in, and never give anonymous users Read access to the feedback table.

create-a-page-template-governance-guide.shortDescription: Set rules for Power Pages page templates, web templates and content snippets so every page shares the same layout, and changes are controlled.
create-a-page-template-governance-guide.fullDescription: In Power Pages, a page template decides which web template renders a page, and web templates hold the Liquid and HTML that many pages share. A handful of well-named templates with clear ownership keeps a site consistent. Dozens of copies edited by different people make every change a hunt.
create-a-page-template-governance-guide.problemStatement: Each new page was built by copying another and editing its markup, so the header exists in nine slightly different versions and a brand change takes weeks.
whenToUse: Sites with more than about twenty pages
Sites with several content authors
Before a redesign or brand update
whenNotToUse: Small sites built entirely with the design studio's sections and components and no custom templates
Single-page campaign sites that will be retired within months
create-a-page-template-governance-guide.formulaOrCode:
The pieces Page template a named layout authors choose for a page. Points at a web template (Type: Web Template) and says whether to use the site header and footer. Web template Liquid + HTML source. Can include other web templates and define blocks. Content snippet a small piece of editable text or HTML reused across pages (footer text, phone number). Site marker a named pointer to a page, so templates link by name instead of URL. Template catalogue (keep this short) Page template Web template Use for Owner Home Home the home page only Web team Landing Landing section landing pages Web team Article Article guidance and knowledge pages Content lead Form page Form Page pages hosting one form Web team List page List Page pages hosting one list Web team Full width Full Width special layouts, by request Web team Structure with inheritance (web template: "Layout Base")
{% block breadcrumbs %}{% include 'Breadcrumbs' %}{% endblock %}
{% block title %}

{{ page.title }}

{% endblock %} {% block main %}{{ page.adx_copy }}{% endblock %}
{% block aside %}{% endblock %}
Web template "Article" {% extends 'Layout Base' %} {% block aside %} {% include 'Related Links' %} {% include 'Page feedback' %} {% endblock %} Shared pieces {% include 'snippet', snippet_name: 'Footer/Contact' %} or {{ snippets['Footer/Contact'] }} {{ sitemarkers['Contact Us'].url }} Naming Web templates: Title Case, purpose first: "Article", "List Page", "Card - Service". Partial templates meant for include only: prefix with the component type: "Partial - Related Links". Content snippets: Area/Name: "Footer/Contact", "Home/Hero heading". No "Copy of", "v2" or personal names. Rules 1. Authors choose from the catalogue. New page templates need the web team's approval. 2. No page-specific HTML in web templates. Page content lives in the page copy or snippets. 3. Shared markup lives in one web template and is included, never pasted. 4. CSS goes in the site's theme or a custom CSS file, not inline in templates. 5. Templates change in the development site and are deployed. Never edit on production. 6. Every web template has a comment line at the top: purpose, owner, where it is used. {% comment %} Article layout. Owner: content lead. Used by: Article page template. {% endcomment %} 7. Retire unused templates each quarter. Find what uses a template Portal Management > Web Templates > open > Related > Page Templates. Page Templates > open > Related > Web Pages. Search includes with the CLI download: grep -r "include 'Related Links'" ./site/web-templates Source control pac pages download writes each web template as a folder with .html source, so changes can be reviewed as diffs before upload. Accessibility built into templates One h1 per template, landmark elements (header, nav, main, footer), a skip link to #mainContent, and labels on every form control.
stepByStepInstructions: List existing page templates and web templates and where each is used.
Agree the catalogue and merge duplicates into it.
Build a base layout web template and extend it for each layout.
Move repeated markup into included templates and text into content snippets.
Apply the naming rules and add the comment line to each template.
Restrict template editing to the web team and route changes through the development site.
Review and retire unused templates each quarter.
commonMistakes: Copying a web template for each new page.
Hard-coding URLs instead of using site markers.
Editing templates on the live site.
Putting text that authors need to change inside Liquid source.
troubleshooting: If a template change shows on some pages only, those pages use a copy. Find it through the page's page template.
If an include renders nothing, the web template name in the include does not match exactly, including case.
If a block does not override, the child template is missing the extends line as its first statement.
If changes do not appear, purge the site cache or select Sync in the design studio.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a page template and a web template in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A page template is the layout an author picks for a page. A web template is the Liquid and HTML source that the page template points to.

faqs.question: How do I reuse a header or sidebar across Power Pages?
faqs.answer: Put the markup in one web template and bring it into others with the include tag, or build a base layout and use extends with blocks.

faqs.question: What are content snippets for?
faqs.answer: Small pieces of text or HTML, such as footer contact details, that authors can edit in one place and that templates display on many pages.

create-an-adaptive-card-approval-summary.shortDescription: Post an adaptive card to Teams that summarises a request (who, what, how much, why) with a link to the full record, so approvers can decide without opening three systems.
create-an-adaptive-card-approval-summary.fullDescription: Approvers decide faster when the key facts are in front of them. This card puts the request's title, requester, amount, dates and justification into a compact layout with a button to the source record, and pairs with the Approvals action or a wait-for-response card for the decision itself.
create-an-adaptive-card-approval-summary.problemStatement: Approval notifications say only 'You have a new approval' and approvers must open the app, find the item and read it before they can respond.
whenToUse: Approvals where a few facts decide most cases
Requests raised in SharePoint or Dataverse and approved in Teams
Posting an approval summary to a team channel for visibility
whenNotToUse: Approvals that need many attachments or long documents read first
Very sensitive data that should not appear in chat
stepByStepInstructions: List the four to six facts approvers need most.
Design the card in the Adaptive Cards Designer with sample data.
Replace sample values with flow expressions, with fallbacks for empty fields.
Escape free-text fields before inserting them into the JSON.
Post the card to the approver and add the approval or wait-for-response action.
Test with long text, empty optional fields and special characters.
commonMistakes: Putting every column on the card.
Unescaped quotes or line breaks in user text breaking the JSON.
formatDateTime on an empty date, which fails the flow.
Using a card schema version newer than Teams supports.
troubleshooting: If the action fails with a JSON parse error, a text value contains a quote or line break. Escape it as shown.
If the card posts but shows 'We're sorry, this card couldn't be displayed', lower the version to 1.4 and remove unsupported elements.
If the amount shows many decimals, format it with formatNumber.
If the Open request link fails for the approver, they lack permission to the list or record.

faqs.question: How do I send an approval summary to Teams with Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Build an adaptive card with the key facts and use the Teams action Post card in a chat or channel. Pair it with an approval action, or put Approve and Reject buttons on the card with the wait-for-response action.

faqs.question: Which adaptive card version works in Teams?
faqs.answer: Use version 1.4 for cards posted by flows. Newer features may not render in every Teams client.

faqs.question: Why does my adaptive card fail when the description has quotes?
faqs.answer: The text is inserted into JSON and the quote ends the string early. Escape backslashes, quotes and line breaks before using the value.

create-a-teams-notification-routing-rule.shortDescription: Route flow notifications to the right Teams channel, chat or person from a rules table instead of hard-coding recipients in every flow.
create-a-teams-notification-routing-rule.fullDescription: As notification flows multiply, each one hard-codes its own team, channel and recipients. A routing table (category and severity in, destination out) moves those decisions into data. Flows look up the rule and post, and owners change routing without editing a flow.
create-a-teams-notification-routing-rule.problemStatement: Changing which channel receives finance alerts means editing six flows, and two of them still post to a channel that was archived.
whenToUse: Several flows post to Teams
Destinations depend on department, category, severity or time
Business owners want to change recipients themselves
whenNotToUse: A single flow with one fixed destination
Urgent alerts that must always reach the same on-call channel regardless of category
create-a-teams-notification-routing-rule.formulaOrCode:
Routing list (SharePoint list "Notification Routes") Title rule name, for example "Finance - High" Category Choice / text Finance | IT | Facilities | Default Severity Choice Low | Medium | High | Any Destination Choice Channel | Chat | Email TeamId Text GUID of the team ChannelId Text for example 19:abc123...@thread.tacv2 Recipients Text semicolon-separated emails (for Chat or Email) MentionOwner Yes/No QuietHours Yes/No hold Low and Medium until 08:00 IsActive Yes/No default Yes SortOrder Number lower wins when several rules match Get the ids Teams > channel > ... > Get link to channel. The link contains the channel id (URL-decode it) and groupId (the team id). Or use the Teams actions List teams and List channels once and copy the ids. Child flow "Send notification" (so every flow routes the same way) Trigger: Manually trigger a flow Inputs: Category, Severity, Title, Message, Link, OwnerEmail Get items (Notification Routes) Filter Query: IsActive eq 1 and (Category eq '@{triggerBody()?['text']}' or Category eq 'Default') and (Severity eq '@{triggerBody()?['text_1']}' or Severity eq 'Any') Order By: SortOrder asc Top Count: 1 Condition: length(body('Get_items')?['value']) is greater than 0 If no -> post to the admin channel "No route for /" and Terminate (Succeeded) Compose "Route": first(body('Get_items')?['value']) Condition (quiet hours) and( equals(outputs('Route')?['QuietHours'], true), not(equals(triggerBody()?['text_1'], 'High')), or( less(int(convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'HH')), 8), greaterOrEquals(int(convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'HH')), 18) ) ) If yes -> Create item in a "Held notifications" list; a scheduled flow sends them at 08:00. Switch on outputs('Route')?['Destination']?['Value'] Channel -> Post message in a chat or channel Post as Flow bot, Post in Channel Team: @{outputs('Route')?['TeamId']} (enter custom value) Channel: @{outputs('Route')?['ChannelId']} Message: @{triggerBody()?['text_2']}
@{triggerBody()?['text_3']}
Open Chat -> Apply to each split(outputs('Route')?['Recipients'], ';') Post message in a chat or channel, Post in: Chat with Flow bot, Recipient: current item Email -> Send an email (V2) to Recipients Respond to a Power App or flow: routed = true, destination = rule title Calling flow Run a Child Flow: Send notification Category: @{triggerBody()?['Department']?['Value']} Severity: High Title, Message, Link, OwnerEmail Rule examples Finance - High Finance High Channel Finance team / Alerts Finance - Other Finance Any Channel Finance team / General SortOrder 20 Default Default Any Channel Operations / Notifications SortOrder 99 Both flows must be in the same solution, and the child flow's connections set to "Use this connection" under Run only users.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the routing list and add a Default rule.
Collect team and channel ids for each destination.
Build the child flow in a solution with the lookup, quiet hours and switch.
Set the child flow's run-only connections to its own.
Replace hard-coded Teams actions in existing flows with a call to the child flow.
Give business owners edit rights to the routing list and a short guide.
commonMistakes: No default rule, so unmatched notifications vanish.
Typing the channel name instead of its id as the custom value.
Leaving the child flow's connections as 'Provided by run-only user', which fails when called.
Letting anyone edit the routing list with no check on ids.
troubleshooting: If posting fails with 'Team not found' or 'Channel not found', the ids are wrong or the Flow bot's connection account is not a member of the team.
If the wrong rule is chosen, check SortOrder and that the Category text matches exactly.
If the child flow cannot be selected, it is not in a solution or has no Respond action.
If private or shared channel posts fail, the Flow bot cannot post there. Use Post as User, or a standard channel.

faqs.question: How do I post to different Teams channels from one flow?
faqs.answer: Store team and channel ids in a list keyed by category and severity, look up the matching row in the flow, and pass the ids to the Teams action as custom values.

faqs.question: Where do I find a Teams channel id?
faqs.answer: Use Get link to channel and decode the link, which contains the channel id and the team's group id, or run the List channels action once.

faqs.question: Can business users change where notifications go?
faqs.answer: Yes. With routing in a list, they edit a row instead of asking for a flow change.

create-a-channel-based-exception-alert.shortDescription: Post flow failures and business exceptions to a Teams channel as one actionable card each, with deduplication so the channel stays readable.
create-a-channel-based-exception-alert.fullDescription: Failure emails go to one person and are ignored. A channel alert puts each exception in front of the whole support team with what failed, for which record, the error text and links to the run and the record. Deduplication and a daily summary keep the channel from becoming noise.
create-a-channel-based-exception-alert.problemStatement: A flow has been failing for nine days. The failure emails went to a maker who was on leave, and the business found out from a customer.
whenToUse: Production flows that a team supports
Business exceptions such as missing data or failed validation that need human action
Replacing per-person failure emails
whenNotToUse: Personal flows
High-volume errors better handled by retries and a log table than by a message per failure
create-a-channel-based-exception-alert.formulaOrCode:
In each production flow
  Scope "Try"     the business actions
  Scope "Catch"   Configure run after: Try has failed, has timed out
    Filter array "Failed":  From @{result('Try')}   where  @equals(item()?['status'], 'Failed')
    Compose "Error":
      @{coalesce(first(body('Failed'))?['error']?['message'],
                 first(body('Failed'))?['outputs']?['body']?['error']?['message'],
                 first(body('Failed'))?['outputs']?['body']?['message'], 'Unknown error')}
    Run a Child Flow "Raise exception alert"
      Source     : @{workflow()?['tags']?['flowDisplayName']}
      Action     : @{first(body('Failed'))?['name']}
      Error      : @{outputs('Error')}
      RecordTitle: @{triggerBody()?['Title']}
      RecordLink : @{triggerBody()?['{Link}']}
      RunLink    : https://make.powerautomate.com/environments/@{workflow()?['tags']?['environmentName']}/flows/@{workflow()?['name']}/runs/@{workflow()?['run']?['name']}
      Severity   : High
    Terminate: Failed

Child flow "Raise exception alert"
  1. Compose "Key": @{concat(triggerBody()?['text'], '|', triggerBody()?['text_1'], '|', take(triggerBody()?['text_2'], 80))}
  2. Get items (list "Flow Exceptions")
       Filter Query: AlertKey eq '@{replace(outputs('Key'), '''', '''''')}' and Created ge '@{addHours(utcNow(), -4)}'
       Top Count: 1
  3. Condition: an alert with this key exists in the last 4 hours
       Yes -> Update item: OccurrenceCount = add(OccurrenceCount, 1). No new post.
       No  -> Create item (AlertKey, Source, Action, Error, RecordLink, RunLink, Severity, Status = Open, OccurrenceCount = 1)
              Post card in a chat or channel (Flow bot, the support channel)
              Update item: MessageId = @{outputs('Post_card_in_a_chat_or_channel')?['body/id']}

Card
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.4",
  "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
  "body": [
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Flow failed: @{triggerBody()?['text']}", "weight": "Bolder", "color": "Attention", "wrap": true },
    { "type": "FactSet", "facts": [
      { "title": "Action", "value": "@{triggerBody()?['text_1']}" },
      { "title": "Record", "value": "@{coalesce(triggerBody()?['text_3'], 'n/a')}" },
      { "title": "Severity", "value": "@{triggerBody()?['text_6']}" },
      { "title": "Time", "value": "@{convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'dd MMM HH:mm')}" } ] },
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{take(replace(replace(triggerBody()?['text_2'], '\', '/'), '"', ''''), 300)}", "wrap": true, "isSubtle": true }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Open run",    "url": "@{triggerBody()?['text_5']}" },
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Open record", "url": "@{triggerBody()?['text_4']}" },
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Exception log", "url": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Ops/Lists/FlowExceptions" }
  ]
}

Working the alert
  Reply in the thread with who is taking it. When fixed, set Status = Resolved in the list with a note.
  Resubmit the failed run from the run link where safe.

Daily summary (scheduled, 08:30)
  Get items: Status eq 'Open'. Group by Source, show count and oldest. Post one message.
  If none are open, post nothing.

Flows that fail before the Try scope (trigger or connection problems)
  These never reach Catch. Cover them with a monitor flow: Power Automate Management >
  List flows, then for each critical flow check recent runs, or use the built-in
  "flow failure" notifications and Managed Environments alerts.

Channel set-up
  A dedicated channel, for example "Automation alerts". Members: the support owners.
  Ask members to set channel notifications to All new posts.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the exception log list and the alerts channel.
Build the child flow with the deduplication key and the card.
Add Try and Catch scopes to each production flow and call the child flow from Catch.
End each Catch with Terminate set to Failed.
Add the daily open-exceptions summary.
Agree who watches the channel and how alerts are acknowledged and closed.
commonMistakes: Posting every single failure with no deduplication.
Alerts with no link to the run or the record.
Catching the error and leaving the run marked as succeeded.
A channel nobody has notifications turned on for.
troubleshooting: If the same failure posts many times, the key includes changing text such as an id inside the error message. Shorten or normalise the key.
If the card fails to post, the error text contains characters that break the JSON. Strip quotes and backslashes as shown.
If no alert arrives for a broken flow, it failed at the trigger. Use a monitor flow or platform alerts for that case.
If the run link opens the wrong environment, build it from workflow() values, not a copied URL.

faqs.question: How do I get notified in Teams when a flow fails?
faqs.answer: Wrap the flow's actions in a Try scope, add a Catch scope that runs on failure, and post a card to a support channel with the error and a link to the run.

faqs.question: How do I stop alert spam from a failing flow?
faqs.answer: Record each alert with a key made from the flow, action and error. Skip posting when the same key was raised in the last few hours, and count occurrences instead.

faqs.question: How do I link to the failed run?
faqs.answer: Build the URL from workflow(): the environment name, the flow name and the run name.

create-a-queue-digest-card.shortDescription: Send a scheduled Teams card that summarises a work queue: counts by status, the oldest items and what is overdue, with links to each view.
create-a-queue-digest-card.fullDescription: A digest replaces dozens of individual notifications with one message that answers the questions a team lead asks each morning: how many items are waiting, which are oldest, what is overdue and who has the most. The card is built from a single Get items call and a few array expressions.
create-a-queue-digest-card.problemStatement: The team channel receives a message for every new request, people mute it, and items sit untouched because nobody sees the overall picture.
whenToUse: Shared queues of requests, tickets or approvals
Daily or weekly stand-ups
Replacing per-item notifications for low-urgency work
whenNotToUse: Urgent items that need an immediate alert
Queues with fewer than a handful of items a week
create-a-queue-digest-card.formulaOrCode:
Flow
  Trigger: Recurrence, weekdays 08:30, local time zone

  Get items (Requests)
    Filter Query: Status ne 'Closed' and Status ne 'Cancelled'
    Order By: Created asc      Top Count: 2000      Pagination: On
    Select Query (Limit Columns by View) to keep the payload small

  Compose "Open":        @{body('Get_items')?['value']}
  Compose "Total":       @{length(outputs('Open'))}

  Filter array "New":        Status/Value equals New
  Filter array "InProgress": Status/Value equals In progress
  Filter array "Waiting":    Status/Value equals Waiting for requester
  Filter array "Overdue":    @less(item()?['DueDate'], utcNow())   (advanced mode; items with a due date)
  Filter array "Unassigned": @empty(item()?['AssignedTo'])

  Select "Oldest five" (From: take(outputs('Open'), 5))
    Map (text mode):
    {
      "type": "TextBlock",
      "text": "[@{replace(item()?['Title'], '"', '''')}](@{item()?['{Link}']}) · @{div(sub(ticks(utcNow()), ticks(item()?['Created'])), 864000000000)} days · @{coalesce(item()?['AssignedTo']?['DisplayName'], 'Unassigned')}",
      "wrap": true, "spacing": "Small"
    }

  Condition: Total is equal to 0 -> Terminate (Succeeded). No card on an empty queue.

  Post card in a chat or channel (Flow bot, team channel)

Card
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.4",
  "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
  "body": [
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Request queue · @{convertFromUtc(utcNow(), 'GMT Standard Time', 'ddd d MMM')}", "weight": "Bolder", "size": "Medium" },
    { "type": "ColumnSet", "columns": [
      { "type": "Column", "width": "stretch", "items": [
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{outputs('Total')}", "size": "ExtraLarge", "weight": "Bolder", "horizontalAlignment": "Center" },
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Open", "isSubtle": true, "horizontalAlignment": "Center", "spacing": "None" } ] },
      { "type": "Column", "width": "stretch", "items": [
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{length(body('New'))}", "size": "ExtraLarge", "weight": "Bolder", "horizontalAlignment": "Center" },
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "New", "isSubtle": true, "horizontalAlignment": "Center", "spacing": "None" } ] },
      { "type": "Column", "width": "stretch", "items": [
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{length(body('Overdue'))}", "size": "ExtraLarge", "weight": "Bolder", "color": "@{if(greater(length(body('Overdue')), 0), 'Attention', 'Default')}", "horizontalAlignment": "Center" },
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Overdue", "isSubtle": true, "horizontalAlignment": "Center", "spacing": "None" } ] },
      { "type": "Column", "width": "stretch", "items": [
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{length(body('Unassigned'))}", "size": "ExtraLarge", "weight": "Bolder", "horizontalAlignment": "Center" },
        { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Unassigned", "isSubtle": true, "horizontalAlignment": "Center", "spacing": "None" } ] }
    ] },
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Oldest open", "weight": "Bolder", "spacing": "Medium" },
    { "type": "Container", "items": @{body('Oldest_five')} }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Unassigned", "url": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Ops/Lists/Requests/Unassigned.aspx" },
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Overdue",    "url": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Ops/Lists/Requests/Overdue.aspx" },
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "All open",   "url": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Ops/Lists/Requests/Open.aspx" }
  ]
}

Per-person digest
  Select the AssignedTo emails, union(body('Select'), body('Select')) for distinct people,
  Apply to each person: Filter array to their items, post the card to their chat with the Flow bot.

Counts by assignee (top section alternative)
  For each distinct assignee: length(filter) and build FactSet facts { "title": name, "value": count }.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide the four numbers the team lead needs.
Create list views for each number so the card's buttons have somewhere to go.
Build the scheduled flow with one Get items and Filter array actions for each count.
Use Select to build the oldest-items rows.
Compose the card and post it to the channel.
Skip the post when the queue is empty, and review after two weeks whether the numbers are the right ones.
commonMistakes: Calling Get items once per count instead of filtering one result.
Posting an empty digest every day.
Listing every open item, which makes the card too long.
Leaving out links, so the card informs but nobody can act.
troubleshooting: If counts stop at 100, set Top Count and turn on pagination in Get items.
If the card fails when a title contains a quote, replace quotes in the Select as shown.
If Overdue includes items with no due date, add a condition that the date is not empty.
If the card exceeds the size limit (about 28 KB), reduce the number of rows.

faqs.question: How do I send a daily summary to Teams from a SharePoint list?
faqs.answer: Use a scheduled flow with Get items, count each group with Filter array and length(), and post an adaptive card with the totals and links to list views.

faqs.question: How do I put a list of items inside an adaptive card?
faqs.answer: Use a Select action to turn each item into a TextBlock object, then insert the Select output as the items array of a Container.

faqs.question: How do I avoid posting when there is nothing to report?
faqs.answer: Add a condition on the total and end the flow with Terminate when it is zero.

create-a-decision-capture-card.shortDescription: Capture a decision in Teams with an adaptive card (options, comments, decided by, time) and write it back to the record as an audit trail.
create-a-decision-capture-card.fullDescription: Decisions made in chat are lost in chat. A decision card asks one clear question, offers the allowed options, requires a comment where it matters and records who answered and when. The flow then writes the result to the source record and replaces the card with the outcome so nobody answers twice.
create-a-decision-capture-card.problemStatement: The team agrees an outcome in a Teams thread, nobody updates the record, and a month later there is no evidence of who decided what.
whenToUse: Go or no-go, approve or defer, and similar choices made by one accountable person
Decisions that need a comment and an audit trail
Processes already running in Teams
whenNotToUse: Formal approvals needing delegation, reassignment and history, where the Approvals connector fits better
Decisions needing many people to vote
create-a-decision-capture-card.formulaOrCode:
Flow
  Trigger: item reaches "Decision needed" (trigger condition on status)

  Post adaptive card and wait for a response (Teams)
    Post as: Flow bot      Post in: Chat with Flow bot
    Recipient: @{triggerBody()?['DecisionOwner']?['Email']}
    Update message: "Decision recorded. Thank you."
    Should update card: Yes
    Message: card below
  Settings > Timeout: P3D

Card
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard", "version": "1.4",
  "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json",
  "body": [
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Decision needed", "weight": "Bolder", "color": "Accent", "size": "Small" },
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerBody()?['Title']}", "weight": "Bolder", "size": "Medium", "wrap": true },
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerBody()?['DecisionQuestion']}", "wrap": true },
    { "type": "Input.ChoiceSet", "id": "decision", "label": "Your decision", "style": "expanded",
      "isRequired": true, "errorMessage": "Choose an option.",
      "choices": [
        { "title": "Approve", "value": "Approve" },
        { "title": "Approve with conditions", "value": "Conditional" },
        { "title": "Defer", "value": "Defer" },
        { "title": "Reject", "value": "Reject" }
      ] },
    { "type": "Input.Text", "id": "comments", "label": "Reason or conditions", "isMultiline": true,
      "maxLength": 1000, "isRequired": true, "errorMessage": "Add a short reason." },
    { "type": "Input.Date", "id": "reviewDate", "label": "Review again on (if deferred)" }
  ],
  "actions": [
    { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Record decision" },
    { "type": "Action.OpenUrl", "title": "Open record", "url": "@{triggerBody()?['{Link}']}" }
  ]
}

Read the response
  Decision     body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['decision']
  Comments     body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['comments']
  Review date  body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['reviewDate']
  Responder    body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['responder']?['email']
               body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['responder']?['displayName']
  Time         body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['responseTime']

Write it back
  Update item
    Decision          : the decision value
    DecisionComments  : comments
    DecisionBy        : responder email
    DecisionOn        : responseTime
    ReviewDate        : reviewDate (only when Defer)
    Status            : Switch on decision -> Approved | Approved with conditions | Deferred | Rejected
  Create item in "Decision log" (one row per decision: record id, question, decision, by, on, comments)
  so later changes to the record do not overwrite history.

Tell others
  Post message in the project channel: "<Responder> recorded: Approve with conditions. <comments>"

Make comments required only for some options
  Input validation cannot depend on another input. Keep comments required for all, or check in the
  flow and send the card again with a note when a rejection has no reason.

Posting in a channel instead of a chat
  Anyone in the channel can respond. The first response wins. Check the responder against the
  allowed decision makers and re-post if someone else answered.

Timeout branch (run after: has timed out)
  Remind once, then escalate to the backup decision owner.
stepByStepInstructions: Write the decision question and the allowed options.
Add columns for decision, comments, decided by, decided on and review date to the record.
Build the card with required inputs.
Post it with the wait-for-response action and a timeout.
Write the response to the record and to a decision log.
Announce the outcome in the team's channel.
Add the reminder and escalation branch.
commonMistakes: Free-text decisions instead of fixed options.
Not recording the responder and time from the response.
Posting to a channel and accepting whoever clicks first.
No timeout, so the flow waits until it expires at 30 days.
troubleshooting: If the response has no data values, the inputs are missing id properties.
If required validation does not show, set isRequired and errorMessage and give the input a label.
If the flow never continues, the card was posted with the plain Post card action. Use Post adaptive card and wait for a response.
If the card does not update after submit, set Should update card to Yes and supply an update message.

faqs.question: How do I collect a decision in Teams with Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use the Teams action Post adaptive card and wait for a response with a card that has an Input.ChoiceSet for the options and a text input for comments, then read the values from the action's data output.

faqs.question: How do I know who responded to an adaptive card?
faqs.answer: The wait-for-response action returns a responder object with the person's email and display name, and a response time.

faqs.question: Should I use an adaptive card or the Approvals connector?
faqs.answer: Use Approvals for formal approvals that need reassignment, multiple approvers and history. Use a card for a single decision with custom options and fields.

create-a-card-retry-and-timeout-path.shortDescription: Handle what happens when an adaptive card is never answered, cannot be delivered or fails to post: timeouts, reminders, escalation and retries.
create-a-card-retry-and-timeout-path.fullDescription: A flow that posts a card and waits is paused until someone clicks. People are on leave, bots get blocked and Teams throttles. A complete path sets a timeout, reminds once, escalates, retries delivery failures and always leaves the record in a known state.
create-a-card-retry-and-timeout-path.problemStatement: A wait-for-response flow sits for 30 days and then fails silently, leaving the request stuck in 'Pending' with nobody aware.
whenToUse: Any flow using Post adaptive card and wait for a response
Approvals or decisions with a service level
Flows posting to people who may not have Teams or the Flow bot available
whenNotToUse: Informational cards that need no response
Formal approvals, where the Approvals connector already handles reminders and reassignment
create-a-card-retry-and-timeout-path.formulaOrCode:
1. Timeout on the wait action
  Post adaptive card and wait for a response > Settings > Timeout: P2D   (ISO 8601: PT4H, P2D, P1W)
  Without it the action waits until the flow run expires at 30 days.

2. Branch on the result
  Scope "Responded"    Configure run after: wait action is successful
    process the answer
  Scope "No response"  Configure run after: wait action has timed out
    reminder / escalation
  Scope "Could not deliver"   Configure run after: wait action has failed
    fallback channel

3. Reminder then escalation (inside "No response")
  Update item: Status = Awaiting response (reminded), ReminderSentOn = utcNow()
  Post adaptive card and wait for a response        (same card, title prefixed "Reminder:")
    Timeout: P1D
  If that also times out:
    Get manager (V2) of the original recipient, or use the BackupApprover column
    Post adaptive card and wait for a response to the backup, with a note of who did not respond
    Timeout: P2D
  If that times out too:
    Update item: Status = Escalation failed
    Post to the support channel; Terminate (Failed)

4. Loop form, when several reminders are needed
  Initialize variable Attempt = 0, Answered = false
  Do until  Answered equals true  OR  Attempt is greater than or equal to 3
    Post adaptive card and wait for a response     Timeout: P1D
    (run after successful)  Set Answered = true
    (run after timed out)   Increment Attempt
  Set the loop's limits: Count 5, Timeout P5D.
  After the loop: if Answered is false, escalate.

5. Delivery failures
  Typical causes: the recipient has no Teams licence, the Flow bot app is blocked by policy,
  the user is a guest, or the email is wrong.
  Fallback inside "Could not deliver":
    Send email with options (Outlook) to the same person: Options "Approve, Reject"
    or Start and wait for an approval, which also notifies by email.
  Record DeliveryChannel = Email on the item.

6. Retry policy for transient errors (429 throttling, 5xx)
  On the Teams actions: Settings > Retry policy: Exponential interval, Count 4, Interval PT20S,
  Maximum interval PT5M. The default policy also retries, but set it explicitly on critical steps.
  Avoid posting in a tight loop: add a Delay of a second or two between cards in Apply to each,
  and set its concurrency to 1.

7. Late answers
  After a timeout the old card can still be clicked, but the flow has moved on.
  Keep "Should update card" on so answered cards are replaced, and put the request's reference
  and the date on the card so a stale one is recognisable.
  In "Responded", re-read the item first and ignore the answer if Status is no longer Pending.

8. Always leave a trail
  Columns: ReminderSentOn, EscalatedTo, EscalatedOn, DeliveryChannel, LastFlowRunLink
  Final step in every branch updates Status so no item stays Pending without an owner.

Run duration limit
  Total of all waits must stay under 30 days. For longer processes, end the run after
  escalation and let a scheduled flow pick up items still waiting.
stepByStepInstructions: Set a timeout on every wait-for-response action.
Add three scopes after it: responded, timed out and failed, using run-after settings.
Build the reminder and escalation steps with their own timeouts.
Add an email fallback for delivery failures.
Set retry policies on Teams actions.
Re-read the record before acting on a response.
Update status and trail columns at the end of every branch.
commonMistakes: No timeout, so the run expires silently after 30 days.
Run-after left as 'is successful' on the next step, so the flow fails on timeout instead of branching.
Reminding forever with no escalation.
Acting on a late answer after the request has already been escalated and decided.
troubleshooting: If the timeout branch never runs, check the timeout is set on the wait action and the branch's run-after includes has timed out.
If the action fails with 'Bot is not part of the conversation roster', the Flow bot cannot message that user. Use the email fallback.
If you see 429 errors, too many posts were sent at once. Add delays and reduce concurrency.
If the run shows as failed after a handled timeout, add a final action that runs after all branches so the run ends successfully.

faqs.question: How long does Post adaptive card and wait for a response wait?
faqs.answer: Until someone responds or the flow run expires at 30 days, unless you set a shorter timeout in the action's settings.

faqs.question: How do I send a reminder if nobody answers the card?
faqs.answer: Set a timeout on the action, add a branch that runs after it has timed out, and post the card again or escalate from there.

faqs.question: What if the user cannot receive the card?
faqs.answer: The action fails. Add a branch that runs on failure and fall back to an email with options or an approval.

create-a-teams-handoff-message-template.shortDescription: A fixed message format for handing work between people or shifts in Teams: what, state, next step, owner and links, posted by a flow or from an app.
create-a-teams-handoff-message-template.fullDescription: Handoffs fail when the next person has to ask questions. A template makes every handoff answer the same five things in the same order, whether it is typed by a person, posted from a Power App button or sent by a flow when a record is reassigned.
create-a-teams-handoff-message-template.problemStatement: Work is passed on with 'can you pick this up?' and a link, and the new owner spends the first hour working out what has already been done.
whenToUse: Shift changes and holiday cover
Reassigning a case, request or project
Escalating from first-line to second-line support
whenNotToUse: Simple notifications where nothing is being handed over
Teams whose case management tool already records handoff notes on reassignment
create-a-teams-handoff-message-template.formulaOrCode:
The template HANDOFF: () From / To: @from -> @to Current state: one sentence on where it stands Done so far: up to three bullets Next step: the single next action, with a date Watch out for: risks, promises made to the customer, access needed Links: record, files, previous thread Flow: post when a record is reassigned Trigger: When an item is created or modified Trigger condition: @not(equals(triggerBody()?['AssignedTo']?['Email'], coalesce(triggerBody()?['PreviousAssigneeEmail'], ''))) Get an @mention token for a user: @{triggerBody()?['AssignedTo']?['Email']} Post message in a chat or channel (Flow bot, the team's channel):

Handoff: @{triggerBody()?['Title']} (@{triggerBody()?['Reference']})

From @{triggerBody()?['PreviousAssigneeName']} to @{outputs('Get_an_@mention_token_for_a_user')?['body/atMention']}

Current state: @{triggerBody()?['Status']?['Value']}. @{triggerBody()?['HandoffSummary']}

Next step: @{triggerBody()?['NextStep']} by @{formatDateTime(triggerBody()?['NextStepDue'], 'dd MMM')}

Watch out for: @{coalesce(triggerBody()?['HandoffRisks'], 'Nothing noted')}

Open the record

Update item: PreviousAssigneeEmail and PreviousAssigneeName = the new assignee (ready for the next change) Columns the template needs AssignedTo (Person), PreviousAssigneeEmail, PreviousAssigneeName (text, maintained by the flow) HandoffSummary (multiple lines), NextStep (text), NextStepDue (date), HandoffRisks (multiple lines) From a Power App: require the handoff notes before reassigning // btnReassign.DisplayMode If(IsBlank(txtSummary.Value) || IsBlank(txtNextStep.Value) || IsBlank(cmbNewOwner.Selected), DisplayMode.Disabled, DisplayMode.Edit) // btnReassign.OnSelect Patch(Requests, selectedRequest, { AssignedTo: { Claims: "i:0#.f|membership|" & Lower(cmbNewOwner.Selected.Mail), DisplayName: cmbNewOwner.Selected.DisplayName, Email: Lower(cmbNewOwner.Selected.Mail) }, HandoffSummary: txtSummary.Value, NextStep: txtNextStep.Value, NextStepDue: dpNextDue.SelectedDate, HandoffRisks: txtRisks.Value }); Notify("Handed over to " & cmbNewOwner.Selected.DisplayName, NotificationType.Success) Adaptive card version (with acknowledgement) Post adaptive card and wait for a response to the new owner: body: the same fields in a FactSet and TextBlocks actions: Action.Submit "I've got it" | Action.Submit "I can't take this" with a comment input On "I've got it": Update item HandoffAcceptedOn = utcNow(). On refusal or timeout (P1D): notify the team lead. Shift handover (many items at once) Scheduled at shift end: Get items assigned to the outgoing shift with Status not Closed, build one message with a line per item (title, state, next step), post to the shift channel. Typed by hand Save the template as a Teams message extension, a pinned post, or a Loop component in the channel so people paste and fill it in.
stepByStepInstructions: Agree the template headings with the team.
Add the handoff columns to the list or table.
Make the summary and next step required in the app when the assignee changes.
Build the flow that detects a change of assignee and posts the message with a mention.
Add acknowledgement with a card if handoffs are being missed.
Review a sample of handoffs monthly and trim headings nobody fills in.
commonMistakes: Optional notes, which are then left empty.
Mentioning the whole channel instead of the new owner.
A template so long that people skip it.
No link back to the record.
troubleshooting: If the flow posts on every edit, the trigger condition is not comparing with the stored previous assignee.
If the mention shows as plain text, insert the atMention token from the mention action, not the person's name.
If the date expression fails, NextStepDue is empty. Make it required or wrap it with a fallback.
If the new owner is not notified, they are not a member of the team or have muted the channel. Post to their chat as well.

faqs.question: What should a handoff message include?
faqs.answer: What is being handed over, its current state, what has been done, the single next step with a date, anything to watch out for, and links.

faqs.question: How do I post a Teams message when an item is reassigned?
faqs.answer: Use a flow triggered on modification with a trigger condition that compares the assignee with a stored previous value, then post a message that mentions the new owner.

faqs.question: How do I confirm the new owner has accepted?
faqs.answer: Send an adaptive card with an acknowledgement button using the wait-for-response action and record the time they accept.

create-a-card-schema-versioning-checklis.shortDescription: Keep adaptive cards working as they change: pick the schema version Teams supports, store cards as templates, version your own payload and test before release.
create-a-card-schema-versioning-checklis.fullDescription: Adaptive cards have two kinds of version: the Adaptive Card schema version, which decides which elements a client can render, and your own card's version, which matters when flows are waiting on older cards. A short checklist prevents the two classic failures: a card that will not render on mobile and a response that no longer matches what the flow expects.
create-a-card-schema-versioning-checklis.problemStatement: A card edited in the designer with the newest schema shows as blank for half the team, and a renamed input breaks every flow run still waiting on the old card.
whenToUse: Cards used by more than one flow
Cards with inputs that flows read
Teams with desktop, web and mobile users
whenNotToUse: One-off informational cards in a single flow
Cards rendered outside Teams, such as Outlook actionable messages, which have their own version rules
create-a-card-schema-versioning-checklis.formulaOrCode:
Schema version
  [ ] "version" set to "1.4" for cards posted by Power Automate to Teams
      (Teams supports up to 1.5 for bots; flows posting through the Flow bot are safest at 1.4)
  [ ] "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json"
  [ ] Designer host app set to Microsoft Teams (adaptivecards.io/designer) when authoring
  [ ] No elements above the chosen version: check each element's "Version" in the schema explorer
      1.2  Action.ToggleVisibility, Input validation basics, RichTextBlock
      1.3  Input labels, isRequired, errorMessage, regex
      1.4  Action.Execute (bots; not handled by flows), refresh, overflow menu
      1.5  Table, masked input, tooltips, isEnabled on actions
  [ ] "fallbackText" set, and "fallback" on optional newer elements:
      { "type": "Table", ..., "fallback": { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "See details in the app." } }

Not supported or limited in Teams
  Action.Submit works with flows; Action.Execute needs a bot.
  Media elements, most HTML, and markdown tables are not rendered.
  Markdown: bold, italic, links and lists only.
  Card size limit about 28 KB. Images must be reachable by HTTPS URL or small base64.

Your card's own version
  [ ] Card templates stored in one place (a SharePoint list "Card templates": Name, Version, Json,
      IsCurrent; or files in source control; or environment variables of type JSON)
  [ ] Each card carries its template name and version in the submit data:
      { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Approve", "data": { "card": "request-approval", "cardVersion": 3, "decision": "Approve" } }
  [ ] Flows read cardVersion and handle older versions for as long as cards may be pending
  [ ] Input ids are treated as a contract: never rename or remove an id in place.
      Add new ids; keep old ones until no pending card uses them.
  [ ] Choice values (the "value", not the "title") are stable codes: "Approve", not "Approve request".

Change types
  Safe          wording, layout, colours, adding an optional input, adding a fact
  Needs care    making an input required, adding a choice the flow does not handle
  Breaking      renaming or removing an input id, changing choice values, changing data keys
  For breaking changes: raise cardVersion, deploy the flow that understands both versions first,
  then switch the template.

Template with tokens filled by the flow
  Store:  { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "${title}", "wrap": true }
  Fill:   replace(replace(variables('CardJson'), '${title}', outputs('SafeTitle')), '${link}', triggerBody()?['{Link}'])
  Escape user text for JSON before replacing (quotes, backslashes, line breaks).

Test matrix before release
                    Desktop   Web   iOS   Android
  Light theme         [ ]     [ ]   [ ]    [ ]
  Dark theme          [ ]     [ ]   [ ]    [ ]
  Long text wraps     [ ]     [ ]   [ ]    [ ]
  Inputs validate     [ ]     [ ]   [ ]    [ ]
  Submit reaches flow [ ]     [ ]   [ ]    [ ]
  Also: chat, channel and group chat if the card is used in each.

Release
  [ ] Change note: what changed, card version, flows affected
  [ ] Old version kept for rollback
  [ ] After release, check the first real response in run history
stepByStepInstructions: Set every flow-posted card to schema version 1.4 and add fallback text.
Move card JSON out of individual flows into one template store.
Add the card name and version to each submit action's data.
Treat input ids and choice values as fixed, and document them.
Classify each change as safe, needs care or breaking, and release breaking changes in two steps.
Run the test matrix on desktop and mobile in both themes before release.
commonMistakes: Authoring in the designer with the default host and newest version.
Renaming an input id while flows are waiting on the old card.
Using button titles as the values the flow compares.
Testing only in desktop light theme.
troubleshooting: If a card shows as blank or 'couldn't be displayed', it uses an element above the supported version. Lower the version and remove or add fallback for that element.
If the flow reads null for an input, the id changed or the user answered an older card. Check cardVersion in the response.
If colours are unreadable in dark theme, remove hard-coded colours and use the built-in color and style properties.
If an image is missing, its URL needs sign-in. Use a public HTTPS URL or embed a small base64 image.

faqs.question: Which adaptive card version should I use with Power Automate and Teams?
faqs.answer: Version 1.4 is the safe choice for cards posted by flows. Elements introduced in later versions may not render on every Teams client.

faqs.question: Why does my adaptive card not display in Teams?
faqs.answer: It probably contains an element or property newer than the client supports, invalid JSON, or exceeds the size limit. Validate it in the designer with the Teams host selected.

faqs.question: How do I change a card without breaking running flows?
faqs.answer: Keep input ids and choice values stable, include a card version in the submit data, and release breaking changes by first updating the flow to accept both versions.
